ideas.title: Private randomness against a non-adaptive opponent
ideas.domain: Online algorithms and competitive analysis (online graph coloring)
ideas.problem: Deterministic online decision rules can be fully anticipated by an opponent, so the worst-case cost of any fixed rule can be forced high even when computation is unlimited.
ideas.approach: Let each decision be made with private random choices that the opponent cannot see, and bound performance against an opponent who fixes its entire input sequence in advance without observing those choices. The randomized strategy then achieves a competitive ratio that no deterministic strategy can match.
ideas.principle: When an opponent commits its moves without seeing hidden coin flips, a strategy that mixes in private randomness cannot be anticipated, so it can beat every fixed deterministic rule regardless of how much computation the rule uses.

ideas.title: Random unit dropout against co-adaptation
ideas.domain: Deep learning for image classification
ideas.problem: Large models with many parameters fit their training data too closely, and their components come to depend on specific partners, so they generalize poorly.
ideas.approach: During each training step, a random fraction of the units is temporarily switched off, so the model is trained on a different sub-structure each time. At test time the full structure is used, which approximates averaging over the many sub-structures.
ideas.principle: Randomly silencing a fraction of components on each update stops any component from relying on particular others, so the learned behaviour is spread across redundant pathways and approximates an average over many reduced versions of the system.

ideas.title: Microsimulation from aggregate static records
ideas.domain: Urban mobility modeling and transport simulation
ideas.problem: Fine-grained, time-varying behavior of many individuals is costly or impossible to observe directly, while the only available data are coarse, static, aggregated totals.
ideas.approach: Build a synthetic ensemble of individual agents consistent with the aggregate marginals, generate each agent's dynamic activity schedule from an existing activity simulator, and assign each agent a discrete option by comparing the costs of alternatives on a shared network. The simulated aggregate output is then checked against an independent empirical proxy.
ideas.principle: Recover a fine-grained, dynamic picture of a large population from coarse static totals by sampling a synthetic ensemble of agents, letting each agent act through a generative schedule, choosing among alternatives by comparing their costs on a common substrate, and validating the aggregated result against an independent proxy.

ideas.title: Gated self-sustaining memory cell
ideas.domain: Recurrent neural networks and sequence learning
ideas.problem: Learning dependencies across long time gaps fails because feedback-based learning signals decay or blow up as they propagate back through many steps, so information cannot be held over extended intervals.
ideas.approach: Route the signal through a unit that feeds back onto itself with unit weight, so its value and learning signal persist unchanged, and place multiplicative gates on its input and output that learn when to admit, release, or clear its contents.
ideas.principle: A state that carries itself forward with unit self-coupling keeps a quantity from fading over arbitrarily long delays, while learned multiplicative gates decide when it is written, read, or reset, so retention is selective rather than automatic.

ideas.title: Distill deliberation into compiled rules, then execute without the planner
ideas.domain: LLM agents and business process automation
ideas.problem: Agents that follow a procedure re-run an expensive planning model to pick every step, adding latency and cost even when the same procedure runs again on new inputs.
ideas.approach: Mine the stated rationale behind each past action across several logged runs, merge those conditions into a compact rule set, and compile it into a fixed executor that selects the next step with code instead of a model. Keep the platform-specific part confined to the final compilation stage.
ideas.principle: Repeated decision-making can be distilled from many traces by extracting the justification attached to each choice, consolidating those justifications into a shared rule set, and compiling it into a fast deterministic controller, with the expensive decision source needed only for generating and repairing the rules.

ideas.title: Bandwidth-for-SNR exchange as a quantifiable trade-off
ideas.domain: Information theory / communication engineering
ideas.problem: Communication systems lacked a general theory that accounts for noise, source statistical redundancy, and the needs of the final receiver when trading resources against each other.
ideas.approach: Model the channel and the message source together so that the achievable rate of reliable transmission is set by the source's statistical structure and by the noise, letting redundancy be removed and resources traded against one another under a single quantitative framework.
ideas.principle: A bounded-capacity link carrying a patterned stream under disturbance has one quantitative ceiling set by how predictable the stream is and how strong the disturbance is; the gap between the raw size and that ceiling is removable redundancy, so competing resources can be traded against each other with an exact budget.

ideas.title: Shared-computation candidate generator guiding a costly verifier
ideas.domain: Computer vision, object detection
ideas.problem: Generating candidate locations for detection is a separate, expensive step that becomes the bottleneck once the downstream classifier is fast.
ideas.approach: A small network reuses the features already computed for the whole input to predict candidate regions and scores at every position almost for free. The expensive verifier then examines only those few candidates, and the two stages are trained jointly so the generator learns to direct the verifier's attention.
ideas.principle: Cheap, shared-computation proposals narrow a large search space so that an expensive evaluator only inspects a small, promising subset, with the proposer trained end-to-end on the evaluator's outcomes.

ideas.title: Reusable-knowledge separation with verified-procedure index for layered system adaptation
ideas.domain: On-device LLM inference engines and agentic model enablement
ideas.problem: Adapting a layered system to each new instance requires coordinated edits across many interdependent layers, and generic agents miss cross-layer dependencies and struggle to diagnose failures that span the boundary between host and target.
ideas.approach: Before any new instance arrives, record the system's layer structure and cross-layer dependencies as an index, and pre-validate the build, run, and debug procedures on instances already known to work. For each new instance, a proposer makes coordinated multi-layer changes using that index, while a separate auditor checks completeness and drives iterative fixes from outcome feedback gathered on the real target.
ideas.principle: Keep reusable structural knowledge about a layered system apart from instance-specific changes: map its layers and dependencies and verify procedures on known-good cases first, then let a proposer make coordinated edits while a checker audits completeness and iterates against ground-truth feedback from the target.

ideas.title: Uniform interface across interchangeable methods
ideas.domain: Machine learning software libraries
ideas.problem: A large collection of specialized methods is hard for non-experts to adopt because each one has its own usage conventions, so switching between them costs relearning.
ideas.approach: Expose many different methods behind one consistent calling pattern, with uniform documentation and minimal dependencies, so any method can be used or swapped in the same way.
ideas.principle: When many interchangeable components share one identical interface and conventions, users can change component without relearning how to operate it, so usability comes from uniformity of the contract rather than from the individual components.

ideas.title: Marginal-preserving sparse reweighting
ideas.domain: Graph theory and theoretical computer science (directed graph sparsification)
ideas.problem: A dense directed connection pattern is expensive to store and operate on, and naive sparsification breaks the exact per-node in-totals and out-totals that many downstream computations depend on.
ideas.approach: Keep only a small subset of the existing connections and assign them nonnegative new weights chosen so that every node's incoming and outgoing totals are reproduced exactly. The reduced structure is built so that its bilinear and spectral behaviour stays within a set error of the original, with support size near-linear in the number of nodes.
ideas.principle: A large nonnegative coupling between two families of units can be compressed to a sparse subset of its links, reweighted nonnegatively so that each unit's totals on both sides are preserved exactly, which keeps the induced bilinear form accurate while the support size scales with the number of units rather than the number of pairs.

ideas.title: Joint end-to-end training of a multi-stage pipeline
ideas.domain: Machine learning for document recognition
ideas.problem: Multi-stage recognition systems are usually built from modules that are each optimized separately, so no single stage is tuned for the final performance measure.
ideas.approach: Represent the chain of modules as one differentiable structure in which each module passes weighted alternatives to the next, and train all modules together by minimizing a single overall performance score with gradient methods.
ideas.principle: When a sequence of separately designed processing stages passes soft, weighted alternatives forward, one global error measure can be propagated backward through the whole chain so every stage is adjusted to serve the final outcome rather than its own local target.

ideas.title: Scaling-minimum bracketing of a weighted count
ideas.domain: Approximate counting of combinatorial objects via log-concave polynomials
ideas.problem: Exactly counting weighted combinatorial configurations (such as tableaux of a given shape and content) is hard, and existing tools give no fast, provably accurate estimate for the count.
ideas.approach: Express the count as a coefficient of a positive, log-concave generating function and bound it by the minimum, over positive rescalings of the variables, of the ratio of the function to the target monomial. Approximate that minimum by first-order optimization over an explicitly bounded region, using approximate gradient oracles, and handle boundary cases by factoring the object into smaller instances of the same kind.
ideas.principle: A hard total count over weighted configurations can be sandwiched within a factor exponential in the problem size by the minimum of a positive, log-concave function over multiplicative rescalings; that minimum is a convex problem over a bounded box and can be solved to additive accuracy in log-scale with approximate gradients.

ideas.title: Structure-based fidelity scoring over pointwise error
ideas.domain: Image quality assessment (perceptual image quality)
ideas.problem: Quality metrics that sum pointwise differences between a degraded signal and its reference measure error visibility, which does not match how observers judge how much meaning or form has been lost.
ideas.approach: Score fidelity by how much of the reference's organized, relational structure survives in the degraded version, combining comparisons of local mean, contrast, and pattern correlation rather than raw differences.
ideas.principle: To judge how faithfully a transformed signal preserves a reference, measure the retention of its internal ordering and relations (average level, variability, and shape-matching across local neighborhoods) instead of summing per-element discrepancies.

ideas.title: Provenance-linked verification of distilled summaries
ideas.domain: LLM agent external memory and experience reuse
ideas.problem: Compressed lessons distilled from past runs are applied without any way to check them against the evidence they came from, so a wrong or misread lesson can make the agent worse than having no memory at all.
ideas.approach: Store each distilled item as a short insight linked to a summary of its outcome and to the raw source record it was derived from. At use time, the consumer starts from the short insights and descends the links to the source only when an item is incomplete, conflicts with another, or comes from a failure, correcting it before acting.
ideas.principle: A compressed claim that keeps pointers to its unabridged origin lets a consumer audit it on demand: it trusts the compact form by default, and goes back to the source only when the compact form is missing detail, contradicts something, or is flagged as unreliable.

ideas.title: Elitist layered-dominance survivor selection with density tie-breaking
ideas.domain: Multi-objective evolutionary optimization
ideas.problem: Methods that rank candidates by mutual non-dominance are slow to sort, can lose the best candidates between generations, and need a hand-tuned sharing parameter to keep solutions spread out.
ideas.approach: Merge the current and newly generated populations, sort the merged pool into successive layers of mutually non-dominated items with a fast single-pass sorting procedure, and fill the next population layer by layer. When a layer must be cut, keep the items that are most isolated, measured by a parameter-free crowding distance to their neighbours in the objective space.
ideas.principle: When choosing a fixed-size subset from a combined pool judged on several competing criteria, keep whole nested strata of mutually incomparable items in order of stratum, and break ties within the cut stratum by preferring items with the largest gaps to their nearest neighbours, so that both quality and coverage are preserved without a tuning parameter.

ideas.title: Budget-free adaptive stopping for iterative protected construction
ideas.domain: Differentially private gradient boosted decision tree learning in trusted execution environments
ideas.problem: In a protected iterative learner, choosing how many build steps to run normally requires looking at the data, and that look consumes the protection budget or leaks information.
ideas.approach: Use an early stopping rule that selects the number of boosting rounds adaptively without adding any privacy cost, and keep the rollback mechanism safe against timing side channels so that stopping and restoring do not reveal extra information.
ideas.principle: In a sequential build that must stay within a fixed disclosure budget, the stopping point can be chosen by a rule whose inputs are already covered by the guarantee, so picking when to end costs nothing extra.

ideas.title: Alternating expectation and re-optimization with monotone improvement
ideas.domain: Statistical estimation from incomplete data (computational statistics)
ideas.problem: Maximizing an objective that depends on unobserved or partially observed quantities is hard to do directly, because the objective cannot be optimized in closed form over the parameters alone.
ideas.approach: Iterate two steps: first, compute the expected value of the missing quantities under the current parameter estimate, which yields a tractable surrogate objective; second, set the parameters to the value that maximizes that surrogate. Each round is shown to never decrease the original objective, so the iteration converges.
ideas.principle: When an objective depends on hidden quantities, alternate between averaging those hidden quantities under the current guess to form a tractable surrogate and re-optimizing the guess against that surrogate; a surrogate that matches the objective at the current guess guarantees the objective never gets worse across rounds.

ideas.title: Robust consensus direction with half-space conflict projection
ideas.domain: Parallel split learning for resource-constrained federated devices
ideas.problem: Independent local updates from heterogeneous participants diverge and can conflict with one another when no central step averages them, so the shared process can fail to converge.
ideas.approach: Estimate a robust reference direction from the participants' update directions by iterative geometric-median (Weiszfeld) reweighting, then constrain each participant's update to the half-space whose boundary is set by that reference so that it no longer opposes the consensus.
ideas.principle: When many independent agents propose corrections that partly disagree, compute a outlier-resistant consensus direction by iteratively reweighted averaging, and clip each agent's proposal so it has non-negative alignment with that consensus, removing conflict without a central controller.

ideas.title: Decreasing-Noise Uphill Acceptance
ideas.domain: Statistical mechanics applied to combinatorial optimization
ideas.problem: Greedy local search for a minimum of a complex function gets trapped in local minima and cannot reach the global optimum.
ideas.approach: Accept worse candidate solutions with a probability that depends on a control parameter, and lower that parameter gradually over the run. Early on, the search wanders freely and can escape traps; later, it settles into a good region.
ideas.principle: Search a landscape of configurations while sometimes accepting worse states with a probability that shrinks on a gradually lowered noise level. Early randomness lets the search escape local traps, and late stillness locks in a good state.

ideas.title: Signed-change setpoint adjustment with background personalization
ideas.domain: Affective computing for human-agent negotiation
ideas.problem: A generic perception model trained on general data degrades when applied to new individuals and contexts, so the agent's decisions are driven by inaccurate readings.
ideas.approach: A continual learner personalizes the perception model in a background process while the interaction runs. The signed direction and magnitude of change in the perceived signal are converted into adjustments of the agent's target value, and the learner updates asynchronously so the decision loop is not blocked.
ideas.principle: A fixed measurement model drifts across instances, so a background learner continually personalizes it while the controller runs. The controller's setpoint is shifted by the signed rate and size of change in the measured signal, and learning is decoupled from acting.
concepts: online personalization of a shared model

ideas.title: Taxonomy-guided failure correction from interaction logs
ideas.domain: LLM agent collaboration evaluation
ideas.problem: Paired agents fail in interaction, and the failures are not understood well enough to fix in a targeted way, since individual breakdowns look different on the surface.
ideas.approach: Failed interaction records are coded into a small, hierarchically organized taxonomy of failure types derived from the data itself. An intervention is then designed around those categories, and it is shown to raise success on a fresh set of interactions.
ideas.principle: Recurring breakdowns in a multi-party exchange are grouped into a few data-derived, layered categories, and the corrective step targets each category rather than each instance. Repeated unsuccessful responses to outside feedback are treated as a key signal of failure.

ideas.title: Intrinsic-gap bound for without-replacement subsampling error
ideas.domain: Federated learning convergence analysis (FedAvg with partial participation)
ideas.problem: Existing convergence analyses of randomly subsampled iterative averaging over heterogeneous units need a uniform worst-case dissimilarity assumption, which many well-behaved objectives violate and which inflates the error due to sampling.
ideas.approach: Express the error from drawing a subset without replacement through an intrinsic gap: the difference between the collective optimum and the average of each unit's own optimum, scaled by a finite-population factor (n-S)/(n-1). The resulting bound holds without assuming bounded dissimilarity and keeps the sampling term from being amplified by the number of local steps.
ideas.principle: When a random subset of a fixed finite population is averaged without replacement, the sampling error is controlled by a finite-population correction times the population's own spread around its collective target, so a bound stated in that intrinsic spread needs no worst-case uniform assumption on the population.

ideas.title: Multiscale center-surround contrast for selecting salient locations
ideas.domain: Active computer vision (visual saliency and attention)
ideas.problem: An artificial exploring system needs a way to decide which parts of a large, unstructured input deserve focused attention and how to summarize them compactly.
ideas.approach: Each local region is scored by how much it differs from its surrounding area, computed separately at several resolutions. The strongly contrasting locations are then grouped by similarity into a higher-level summary that guides where the system looks next.
ideas.principle: Items stand out when they differ from their immediate neighborhood, measured across several scales of resolution; the standouts are then clustered by similarity into a compact higher-level description that directs further exploration.

ideas.title: Conditional privilege for self-declared class membership
ideas.domain: Network traffic management and quality-of-service scheduling
ideas.problem: A sender can claim membership in a privileged traffic class without any check, so the class can be abused by spoofed traffic, and the system has no way to verify that a claim matches actual behavior.
ideas.approach: Grant the privileged tier only to participants whose observed behavior matches their declared class. Demote any participant whose behavior contradicts the claim to a tier served after the default tier, and cap the rate of the privileged tier so that spoofed claims cannot overwhelm it.
ideas.principle: A participant that declares membership in a privileged group keeps the privilege only while its observed behavior matches the declaration. Mismatches are moved to a lower tier, and the privileged tier is rate-capped so that false declarations cannot exhaust it.

ideas.title: Interpolated synthetic minority augmentation with majority thinning
ideas.domain: Machine learning on imbalanced classification datasets
ideas.problem: When one outcome is much rarer than another, a learner trained on the raw sample is biased toward the common outcome, and simply duplicating rare cases adds no new variation.
ideas.approach: Generate new rare-case examples by interpolating between each existing rare example and its nearest rare neighbours in feature space, and combine this with undersampling the common cases to reach a usable balance.
ideas.principle: When a rare kind of case is underrepresented, create new instances that lie between existing rare instances and their close neighbours, and thin the abundant kind, so the sample is balanced without exact duplication.

ideas.title: Rewrite from the underlying goal, not the legacy reference
ideas.domain: HPC performance portability for climate-model kernels
ideas.problem: When an existing computational code is ported to new hardware, its double-precision reference version constrains the rewrite, so the developer inherits its structure and misses optimizations available from the problem itself.
ideas.approach: Treat the underlying scientific problem as the specification and rebuild the computation from it, rather than using the legacy reference as the baseline. Then evaluate candidate tooling by how easily it lets each target configuration be customized.
ideas.principle: When redesigning an inherited process, anchor the new version on the underlying objective rather than on the artifact produced by the old method, so that the artifact's representation stops limiting which improvements are reachable, and measure the alternatives by how easily they can be tuned per target.

ideas.title: Heavy-tailed target kernel to relieve crowding
ideas.domain: High-dimensional data visualization (nonlinear dimensionality reduction)
ideas.problem: When relations among many items are compressed into fewer dimensions, the low-dimensional space lacks room for moderately distant items, so they crowd together near the center and the map loses structure.
ideas.approach: Match the pairwise similarities in the reduced space with a heavy-tailed (Student-t, long-tailed) kernel instead of a Gaussian, and optimize the layout so that the two similarity distributions agree. The heavy tail lets moderately dissimilar items sit much farther apart, which opens space for well-separated groups.
ideas.principle: When a structure defined in many dimensions is squeezed into fewer, use a long-tailed similarity function in the reduced space so that moderate separations can be represented by large gaps, which prevents everything from collapsing into a dense central mass.

ideas.title: Random subset deactivation with full-structure rescaling at inference
ideas.domain: Deep learning regularization for neural networks
ideas.problem: Large, highly parameterized models overfit, and averaging many such models at test time to reduce overfitting is too slow to be practical.
ideas.approach: During each training pass, randomly deactivate a fraction of the model's elements along with their links, so every pass trains a different reduced version and no element can rely on specific others. At inference, use the full model with scaled-down weights, which approximates averaging the predictions of all the reduced versions at once.
ideas.principle: Train a large shared structure while repeatedly switching random subsets of its parts off, so no part can depend on particular others; at use time, run the whole structure with scaled contributions to approximate the average over all the reduced versions without evaluating each one.

ideas.title: Dependency-Spreading Placement to Contain Cascading Failures
ideas.domain: Mobile network design and cloud function placement
ideas.problem: When interdependent functions are consolidated onto shared hosts, a single host failure can disable many functions at once and cascade into a wide outage, while consolidation is still needed for cost savings.
ideas.approach: Formulate the assignment of dependent function components to hosts as an optimization that jointly minimizes inter-function dependency and placement cost, under explicit limits on how critical any single host can become. This keeps the cost benefit of consolidation while bounding how much of the system one host failure can take down.
ideas.principle: Assign mutually dependent components to units so that no single unit's failure severs many dependencies, trading a modest rise in assignment cost for a bounded per-unit loss of linked components.

ideas.title: Estimation-control duality via error-covariance recursion
ideas.domain: Linear filtering and prediction of random processes (control and signal estimation)
ideas.problem: Computing the optimal real-time estimate of a hidden quantity from noisy, sequential observations requires a separate, costly design procedure, and its relation to optimal control design is unclear.
ideas.approach: Track the uncertainty of the estimate itself with a nonlinear recursion; its solution directly yields the optimal update gains. Show that this estimation problem is the dual of a noise-free optimal control problem, so the same solution machinery solves both.
ideas.principle: Inferring an unseen internal variable from successive noisy readings is the time-reversed mirror of steering a system toward a target. The recursion that governs the inference's own uncertainty, once solved, supplies the correction weights directly, so one computation yields both the estimator and its gains.

ideas.title: Performance-and-similarity weighted retrieval to seed a new search
ideas.domain: Mobile edge computing and UAV trajectory planning with deep reinforcement learning
ideas.problem: A learning controller facing a new scenario starts from scratch or from a poorly matched prior, so it wastes effort and can fail to generalize to unseen conditions.
ideas.approach: Keep a memory of solutions from past scenarios and, for a new scenario, rank stored solutions by a weighted score that blends how similar their conditions are with how well they performed. The top-ranked solutions are then used to guide the learner, which is a retrieval-augmented warm start.
ideas.principle: When a new case arrives, rank stored solutions from earlier cases by a weighted sum of closeness to the current case and their past quality, then use the best-ranked ones to initialize a generic adaptive search.

ideas.title: Shared-component mixture with per-item mixing weights
ideas.domain: Probabilistic topic modeling of discrete collections
ideas.problem: Collections of discrete count data, such as documents or user-item records, are hard to represent compactly when each item may draw on several shared themes, and single-cluster assignment or unigram-style models discard that mixed structure and give no explicit per-item representation for unseen items.
ideas.approach: Each item is modeled as a finite mixture over a small set of shared latent components, and each item's mixing proportions are themselves drawn from a common prior. The per-item proportions serve as an explicit low-dimensional representation, fitted with approximate variational inference and empirical Bayes estimation of the shared prior.
ideas.principle: Each item in a collection is explained as a weighted combination of a few shared latent patterns, where the weights are drawn from a common prior; the weight vector gives every item a compact, explicit representation that generalizes to new items.

ideas.title: Separate utility from fidelity when reusing stored state across versions
ideas.domain: LLM inference, key-value cache reuse across model updates
ideas.problem: Reusing precomputed intermediate state after a system is updated saves recomputation, but it is unclear whether the reused state preserves only task-relevant information or also reproduces the updated system's behavior.
ideas.approach: Measure reuse on two separate axes: task success on the downstream problem, and a divergence score that compares the next-step output distributions produced under reused state against those produced under freshly computed native state.
ideas.principle: A stored internal state carried over from an earlier version of a system can keep the information needed for the target task while producing outputs that differ from the new version's native behavior, so reuse should be judged both by task utility and by distributional agreement with native computation.

ideas.title: Dense fixed-template prediction across scales
ideas.domain: Computer vision, object detection in images
ideas.problem: Locating instances of unknown kind, size, and shape in a continuous output space usually requires a separate proposal stage, which makes the pipeline slow and hard to train and integrate.
ideas.approach: Discretize the continuous output space into a dense grid of fixed reference templates spread over several coarseness levels and shape variants. A single network scores each template for presence and predicts a small correction to it, pooling predictions from all levels in one forward pass.
ideas.principle: A continuous space of possible outcomes is covered by a dense lattice of fixed reference templates at several coarseness levels; each template gets a presence score and a local correction, so one feed-forward pass replaces a separate candidate-generation stage.

ideas.title: Explicit competing criteria yield an optimal response with a fundamental trade-off
ideas.domain: Computer vision (edge detection in images)
ideas.problem: Detecting a feature well is hard to specify because the goals for a good detector are vague and partly conflict, so there is no principled way to derive the best detector.
ideas.approach: Write each goal as a precise, measurable functional of the detector's response, add a constraint that rules out duplicate responses, then numerically optimize the response against these criteria. The analysis of the two main goals shows they trade off against each other, which fixes a single optimal shape at any scale.
ideas.principle: A desired behavior is made precise by stating several competing quality measures as functionals of a response function, then optimizing that response under them; the unavoidable conflict between two measures sets a fixed bound that determines the optimal form.

ideas.title: Staged difficulty curriculum for transferable sequential construction
ideas.domain: Wireless network planning with graph reinforcement learning
ideas.problem: A sequential construction rule trained on one instance layout and one constraint regime generalizes poorly to new layouts, and hard feasibility constraints make training unstable.
ideas.approach: Train a relational-structure-aware encoder with an actor-critic learner under a multi-stage curriculum that first raises constraint difficulty and then increases the diversity of instance layouts. The learned rule is then applied to unseen layouts without retraining.
ideas.principle: A sequential builder that must satisfy coverage and feasibility limits learns a stable, reusable rule by facing progressively harder constraint levels across a widening set of instance configurations, while an encoder that respects the relational structure of the input lets the rule carry over to new configurations.

ideas.title: Demand-proportional deactivation of stateless units
ideas.domain: Serverless computing and energy-efficient clusters of single-board computers
ideas.problem: Infrastructure that serves on-demand work draws most of its power while idle, so total consumption does not fall with the workload even when the work itself is intermittent.
ideas.approach: Because each unit of work is stateless, whole physical units can be powered off when idle and powered back on under load, with unit power state included in the choice of which unit receives work. The cost appears as a delay for requests that arrive when every unit is off, while sustained load keeps the system always on.
ideas.principle: When each request is independent of the state of the unit serving it, idle units can be fully deactivated and reactivated on demand, so resource consumption tracks load; the dispatch rule trades standby energy against the latency of waking a deactivated unit.

ideas.title: Minimal-subset hypothesis consensus
ideas.domain: Computer vision and automated image analysis (model fitting with gross errors)
ideas.problem: Fitting a model to measurements is corrupted when a large share of the measurements are gross errors, so least-squares or similar fits built on all points are dominated by outliers.
ideas.approach: Repeatedly draw the smallest random subset of observations that determines a candidate solution, then count how many other observations agree with that candidate within a tolerance. Keep the candidate with the largest agreeing set and refit using only those consistent observations.
ideas.principle: Generate many candidate explanations from minimal random samples of noisy observations, score each by how many observations it accounts for within a tolerance, and keep the best-supported explanation so that erroneous observations are excluded without being explicitly modeled.

ideas.title: Furthest-reach frontier pruning over cost-and-offset keys
ideas.domain: Bounded sequence alignment and string algorithms (weighted edit distance)
ideas.problem: Dynamic programming over all alignment paths for a bounded comparison is too large, because the number of partial solutions grows with the input length and the cost alphabet, even though most partial solutions are redundant for the final answer.
ideas.approach: Each partial solution is indexed by its accumulated cost and by a balance quantity (the difference between total gap costs of the two aligned prefixes). For each such key, only the partial solution that has progressed furthest through the input is kept; all others with the same key are discarded, so the number of live states is bounded by the number of distinct keys rather than by the number of paths.
ideas.principle: When advancing a sequential process whose partial states can be grouped by a cost value and a bounded offset, a state that has advanced further under the same cost and offset dominates the others, so keeping one furthest-advanced representative per key preserves the optimal outcome while the active set stays bounded by the number of keys.

ideas.title: Recovery from few random probes via convex minimal-support search
ideas.domain: Compressed sensing and signal reconstruction from linear measurements
ideas.problem: Recovering a high-dimensional object normally requires about as many measurements as its raw size, which wastes effort when its essential content is concentrated in a few components of some hidden coordinate system.
ideas.approach: Take a small number of nonadaptive, generic random linear readings of the object, then recover it by solving a convex linear program that minimizes the L1 norm of its coefficients in the suitable transform, which stands in for minimizing the number of active components. The measurement count then scales with the content's effective complexity rather than its ambient dimension.
ideas.principle: An object that is simple under some change of coordinates can be reconstructed from far fewer generic random linear probes than its raw size, provided the reconstruction picks the solution with the fewest active components via a convex surrogate objective.

ideas.title: Error-localizing advice encoding
ideas.domain: Learning-augmented algorithms for parallel machine scheduling
ideas.problem: Noisy predictions of an optimal combinatorial solution can be unusable: if the advice is encoded in a form where a single wrong piece cascades into many wrong decisions, recovering the optimum from the prediction becomes computationally hard even with only a few errors.
ideas.approach: Choose a representation of the advice (an ordering of items rather than a direct assignment or a greedy-optimality signal) in which prediction errors remain dispersed locally, then run an exact dynamic program over that representation so that the recovered solution is optimal despite the noise.
ideas.principle: When a structured solution is supplied as imperfect guidance, encode it as a sequence whose mistakes stay confined to nearby positions rather than propagating globally, and then recover the optimum with a left-to-right exact search that exploits that locality.

ideas.title: Cross-condition knowledge reuse
ideas.domain: Machine learning (transfer learning)
ideas.problem: A model built for the situation where it will be used assumes that past and future observations share the same representation and distribution, so when the target setting differs and has few labeled examples, performance drops and new labeling is expensive.
ideas.approach: Knowledge from a data-rich source setting is carried over to a label-scarce target setting, even when the two differ in representation or conditions, so the target does not have to be learned from scratch. The survey organizes the methods by what is transferred and how it is adapted.
ideas.principle: When a new situation differs from a well-sampled one but shares some underlying structure, reuse the parts of what was learned that remain valid across the change, and adapt only the parts that shift, instead of relearning everything from scarce data.

ideas.title: Path-decomposed implicit hierarchy storage
ideas.domain: Stringology and suffix-tree indexing for pattern matching
ideas.problem: A hierarchical structure that grows one element at a time must support constant-time incremental updates and fast queries, but storing its full explicit link topology makes each update costly.
ideas.approach: Decompose the hierarchy into chains of nodes, and store each chain in a keyed dictionary that records parent-child relations implicitly through keys instead of explicit pointers. Appending a new element then touches only a few chains.
ideas.principle: A branching structure can be stored as a set of linear chains, each kept in a keyed lookup table, so that connections are recovered from keys rather than stored links. This keeps incremental extension cheap and the representation compact.

ideas.title: Soft depletion-threshold eligibility for load-balanced selection
ideas.domain: Wireless sensor network routing with deep reinforcement learning
ideas.problem: Hard reserve cutoffs remove depleting resource holders from candidacy, so the remaining well-provisioned holders absorb all the load and fail early, concentrating depletion on a few hotspots.
ideas.approach: Candidates below an adaptive reserve threshold stay eligible as long as they pass the other selection criteria, so the hard cutoff becomes a soft condition. The state also encodes each candidate's projected future load and hotspot risk, and a multi-objective reward guides the learned choice.
ideas.principle: Rather than excluding an agent outright once its reserve falls below a cutoff, keep it selectable under a relaxed condition and encode its projected burden, so that demand spreads across the pool and no single member is drained first.

ideas.title: Slack-bounded coupling certificate
ideas.domain: Multi-agent formation control with finite-time transitions
ideas.problem: Reaching a target configuration in finite time does not guarantee that transient deviations stay within safety and connectivity limits, and no explicit link ties internal spread during the transition to geometric margins for choosing the coupling strength.
ideas.approach: Bound the worst-case internal spread of the coupled units during the transition using a network-dependent term, then require that bound to fit within the measured geometric slack. This gives a sufficient condition that can be checked offline and yields a rule for choosing the coupling gain that balances convergence speed against control effort.
ideas.principle: When many coupled components converge to a shared target, their worst-case internal spread can be bounded by a quantity that shrinks as coupling strength grows. Requiring that bound to stay within the available slack gives a checkable sufficient condition and a parameter-selection rule that trades speed against effort.

ideas.title: Batch-by-oldest-age charging with union-of-windows comparison
ideas.domain: online network design with batched service
ideas.problem: When arriving items can be grouped to share a fixed service cost, an online policy must decide when to dispatch a group, and a clairvoyant offline schedule can batch better than any policy that does not know future arrivals.
ideas.approach: Each batch is charged a shared service cost plus the waiting time of its oldest member, so a policy can hold items to share the cost. The analysis compares the policy against the offline optimum by measuring the union of the time intervals during which the pending items were waiting, rather than summing per-item costs.
ideas.principle: Items accumulate and are released in groups, where each group pays a fixed shared charge plus the age of its earliest member. Bounding the online cost by the total measure of the waiting windows, and comparing that measure to what any schedule must incur, gives a competitive ratio that does not depend on the arrival pattern.

ideas.title: Offset co-occurrence signature
ideas.domain: Image texture analysis for remote sensing and photomicrography
ideas.problem: A spatially structured field has no compact, easily computed descriptor that captures its local arrangement well enough to tell different kinds of structure apart.
ideas.approach: Tally how often each pair of discrete states occurs at a fixed relative offset across the field, normalize the tally into a joint distribution, and reduce it to a few scalar statistics that serve as a feature vector for classification. Simple decision rules over these features then assign categories.
ideas.principle: Describe a spatially arranged system by the normalized frequency of pairwise state combinations at a fixed displacement, then condense that table into a few summary numbers that act as a signature for recognizing its class.

ideas.title: Rate-based fixed structure for batching against waiting
ideas.domain: Online algorithms for network design with delays and stochastic arrivals
ideas.problem: Online systems must decide when to pool incoming requests into shared resources, since pooling saves setup and travel cost but makes each request wait, and the arrivals are unknown in advance and revealed only on arrival.
ideas.approach: Use the known arrival rates to choose a fixed shared configuration in advance, without reacting to the realized sequence. Pooling savings are balanced against the expected waiting cost implied by those rates, and the resulting cost is compared with an offline benchmark that may adapt to the actual arrivals.
ideas.principle: When events arrive stochastically at known intensities, a fixed shared structure chosen from those intensities, rather than reacted to online, can stay within a bounded factor of a hindsight-adaptive benchmark by balancing the savings of pooling against the accumulated waiting it imposes.
concepts: online personalization of a shared model

ideas.title: Hidden-state sequence inference with iterative re-estimation
ideas.domain: Hidden Markov models for speech recognition
ideas.problem: Observed sequences are produced by an underlying process whose internal condition is not directly visible, so the condition sequence, the likelihood of an observation sequence, and the model parameters cannot be read off directly.
ideas.approach: Treat each observation as a probabilistic function of a hidden state that evolves by a chain of transition probabilities. Compute the likelihood of an observed sequence with a forward recursion, recover the most probable hidden path with a Viterbi-style dynamic program, and refit transition and emission parameters by iterating expectation over hidden paths and re-estimation (Baum-Welch).
ideas.principle: A sequence of unseen conditions that each depend only on the immediately preceding condition generates noisy visible signals; the unseen path and the generating rules can be jointly recovered by alternating probabilistic scoring over all paths with updating of the rules from those scores.

ideas.title: Per-region model selection by predicted cost over recursive partitions
ideas.domain: Learned database index structures
ideas.problem: A single uniform model type applied everywhere fits heterogeneous local data distributions poorly, so efficiency is lost in regions the model does not suit.
ideas.approach: Recursively split the data domain into regions, and for each region pick the cheapest of several candidate model types using a cost estimate built from data-driven approximations. Mixing model types across the hierarchy lets each local region use the model that fits it best.
ideas.principle: Recursively partition a domain into a hierarchy, and assign each region the lowest-cost option from a heterogeneous set of candidate approximators, with the cost predicted from sampled statistics rather than measured exhaustively.

ideas.title: Rate-controlled sparse sampling to widen reach without added cost
ideas.domain: Deep convolutional networks for dense semantic segmentation
ideas.problem: Enlarging a model's view of context usually requires downsampling or extra parameters, which discards the resolution needed for dense per-element prediction.
ideas.approach: Keep a small fixed set of weights but spread its taps apart by a tunable dilation rate, so each readout covers a wider span while the parameter count and computation stay the same. Varying the rate lets the same weights probe the input at several scales and resolutions.
ideas.principle: A fixed-size set of weights can read a grid of inputs whose spacing is a tunable rate; raising the rate widens each readout's reach at no extra cost in weights or compute, and the rate separately sets the resolution at which outputs are produced.

ideas.title: Closed-Form Shapley Split of Shared-Plus-Individual Costs
ideas.domain: LLM inference energy accounting and cost attribution
ideas.problem: An aggregate cost measured only at the total level must be fairly attributed to participants who share the same rounds of work, but proportional-usage heuristics are unfair and exact Shapley computation needs exponentially many measurements.
ideas.approach: Decompose each round's cost into a shared part that is incurred whenever the round runs and a participant-specific part. Charge each participant its own part plus an equal share of the shared part for every round it takes part in, which gives the Shapley value in closed form from one pass over the activity log. Calibrate the two parts once with a short microbenchmark.
ideas.principle: When a total cost is a sum over rounds of a fixed component shared by all active members plus member-specific components, the fair Shapley split can be computed in closed form by charging each member its own component plus an equal share of the fixed component for every round it is active, avoiding enumeration of all coalitions.

ideas.title: Kernel-decomposed covariance for comparing correlated empirical statistics
ideas.domain: Statistics of diagnostic test evaluation (ROC curve comparison)
ideas.problem: When several performance summaries are computed on the same units, their differences cannot be tested correctly without accounting for the correlation among them, and parametric models for that correlation are often unjustified.
ideas.approach: Write each summary as a symmetric average over subsets of observations (a kernel-based statistic), then estimate the joint covariance matrix of these statistics nonparametrically from the kernel projections. The estimated covariance is used to test differences between the summaries.
ideas.principle: A set of statistics computed on the same sample can be written as averages of a common symmetric function over subsets of the sample. Their joint variability then follows from the variance of the per-item projections, so their dependence is estimated without distributional assumptions.

ideas.title: Replication-Gated Selection with Magnitude Floor
ideas.domain: Statistical learning: selecting feature interactions in predictive models
ideas.problem: A strong association found in one fitted run may reflect fitting noise rather than a pattern that would recur, and existing methods either leave the cutoff to the user or need repeated refits or a model of the joint distribution.
ideas.approach: Fit two runs of the same procedure on disjoint data and access them only through their outputs. Keep a candidate pattern only if the second run reproduces it at a minimum strength, with one multiple-testing correction setting the cutoff. A replication ratio alone was shown to admit arbitrarily weak shared patterns, so a strength floor is added.
ideas.principle: Retain a candidate structure only if an independent replicate, produced by the same procedure on disjoint data, reproduces it at a meaningful magnitude. Requiring consistency alone lets weak structure shared by both replicates pass, so a minimum magnitude is needed.

ideas.title: Area under a threshold sweep as a pairwise ordering probability
ideas.domain: Medical diagnostic test evaluation (ROC analysis)
ideas.problem: A single summary of how well a graded score separates two groups across all cutoffs is hard to interpret and to attach a reliable uncertainty to.
ideas.approach: Take the area under the curve traced by sweeping a cutoff through the scores, and read it as the probability that a random item from the positive group is ranked above a random item from the negative group. That same quantity is a rank statistic that gives closed-form variance and sample-size formulas.
ideas.principle: Sweeping a threshold over graded scores traces a trade-off curve whose area equals the chance that a random pair from two populations is correctly ordered, and that pairwise chance is a pair-averaged statistic whose sampling error has a closed form.

ideas.title: Phase-gated routing between modules
ideas.domain: Modular neural networks and compositional generalisation
ideas.problem: Modular systems do not reliably develop specialised, reusable components, and unrestricted communication between components erodes whatever specialisation does emerge.
ideas.approach: Separate each component's content from a continuously evolving phase state that is learned by coupled oscillator-style dynamics. Components can exchange information through a shared channel only when their phases are aligned, so the timing signal decides who communicates with whom.
ideas.principle: Units with fixed content and a separate, dynamically evolving timing state exchange information only when their timing states match, so routing is set by coincidence of internal rhythms rather than by explicit addresses or a central controller.

ideas.title: Greedy stagewise initialization before global refinement
ideas.domain: Deep learning for dimensionality reduction
ideas.problem: A deep multi-stage model trained end-to-end from random starting parameters often gets stuck in poor solutions, because a joint objective over many stages is hard to optimize.
ideas.approach: Each stage is pretrained greedily and separately on a simple local objective, with each stage's input being the previous stage's output. The stacked result is then used as the starting point for joint fine-tuning of the whole model.
ideas.principle: A hard nonconvex system built from a chain of stages can be made tractable by fitting each stage to a simple local target in sequence, so the global refinement begins near a good solution rather than at random.

ideas.title: Deferred batching under shared fixed charges
ideas.domain: Online algorithms and competitive analysis of request aggregation
ideas.problem: Requests arriving over time must each be served, but serving them separately repeats shared fixed costs, while postponing them adds waiting cost, and an online rule cannot see future arrivals.
ideas.approach: Postpone pending items and serve them together in synchronized periods, paying each shared charge once per batch. A fractional relaxation of the full-information problem supplies both a lower bound on the optimum and the timing of the common service periods that the online rule follows.
ideas.principle: Tasks that accumulate linear waiting costs can be grouped so that each shared setup charge is paid once per group. A fractional relaxation of the hindsight-optimal schedule gives a benchmark and fixes the common action times, and the online rule tracks those times using only known arrival rates.

ideas.title: Greedy pairwise merge hierarchy with per-stage loss tracking
ideas.domain: Statistical grouping of objects into hierarchical clusters
ideas.problem: Finding the optimal partition of many items into a fixed number of groups is intractable at large scale, and the result gives no view of how groupings relate across different granularities.
ideas.approach: Start with every item as its own set. At each stage, evaluate every pairwise union of current sets, keep the union that maximizes the chosen objective, and repeat until one set remains. The sequence of merges gives a full nested structure, and the objective change at each step measures the loss incurred at that stage.
ideas.principle: Build a nested hierarchy bottom-up by repeatedly applying the single locally best combination of two current parts, and record the objective cost of each step, instead of solving the global optimum over all partitions.

ideas.title: Threshold-triggered deferred service with reposition
ideas.domain: Online self-organizing list update with delayed service requests
ideas.problem: When items sit in ordered positions whose retrieval cost depends on position, and pending requests accrue waiting penalties until one retrieval serves them all, it is unclear when to retrieve an item and how to reposition it, since waiting longer grows penalties while delaying cheap service forgoes reorganization gains.
ideas.approach: Serve an item as soon as the accumulated waiting time of its pending demands reaches a fixed fraction (two thirds) of the cost of its current position, then move it to the most favorable position. The threshold is tied to the item's present cost, so the decision is local and needs no global planning.
ideas.principle: An element's service cost depends on its current place in an ordering, and waiting demands accumulate penalties; act once accumulated waiting reaches a constant fraction of the element's present cost, then relocate it to the front. Tuning that fraction balances penalty growth against relocation benefit and yields a constant worst-case competitive ratio.

ideas.title: Adversarial two-player training for generative modeling
ideas.domain: Machine learning, generative modeling
ideas.problem: Estimating a generative model of a data distribution usually requires explicit likelihood modeling or Markov-chain sampling, which is costly or intractable.
ideas.approach: Train a generator to produce samples and a discriminator to tell real from generated samples, with the generator updated to maximize the discriminator's error, so that the two reach a minimax equilibrium in which the generator matches the target distribution.
ideas.principle: Two adaptive agents with opposed objectives improve each other through competition: one learns to imitate a hidden target distribution while the other learns to detect imitations, and the equilibrium of this contest recovers the target without ever modeling its density directly.

ideas.title: Pareto-front search over precedence-constrained assignment with discrete billing blocks
ideas.domain: Cloud scheduling of LLM agent workflows
ideas.problem: Assigning dependent work units to shared heterogeneous capacity is usually optimized for one objective, while real costs are charged in discrete blocks and the competing goals (finish time, spend, utilization) are never treated jointly.
ideas.approach: Formulate the assignment as a joint multi-objective problem that includes block-based billing and provisioning overhead, then search for a set of non-dominated solutions with an evolutionary method (NSGA-II), comparing it against a scalarized weighted-sum search and a heuristic adapted to multiple objectives.
ideas.principle: When items with precedence constraints must be placed on heterogeneous shared capacity whose charges come in discrete blocks, evaluate the conflicting objectives together and return the whole set of non-dominated trade-offs rather than a single weighted optimum.

ideas.title: Recorded-position reconstruction after lossy selection
ideas.domain: Deep learning for semantic image segmentation (encoder-decoder upsampling)
ideas.problem: When a coarse-to-fine network restores resolution after a lossy reduction, learning how to place values back at full scale adds parameters and training cost, and the restored spatial detail is often blurry.
ideas.approach: During the reduction step, record only the positions of the winning values within each local block as a small side code. In the expansion step, place each coarse value back at its recorded position and leave the rest empty, then apply learned filters to fill in the sparse result into a dense one.
ideas.principle: A lossy compression that keeps only local winners can be inverted without learning placement by storing the winners' locations as a cheap side record. Restoration then becomes a fixed scatter into recorded slots followed by a learned densification step.

ideas.title: Exact arithmetic for order-independent, re-derivable distributed computation
ideas.domain: Neural network inference systems and numerical computing
ideas.problem: Results of optimized floating-point computation depend on hardware, compiler, and thread count because rounding depends on the order of operations, so the same computation cannot be reproduced or split across machines with identical outcomes, and a claimed result cannot be checked by an outside party.
ideas.approach: Run the entire execution path in exact integer arithmetic, confining approximate (floating-point) operations to an offline preparation step and to a separate reference used only for checking. Because the exact path gives the same bits regardless of how work is partitioned, any party can recompute the run and compare a hash of the output.
ideas.principle: If every intermediate step is computed exactly so that the result does not depend on the order or grouping of operations, then the output is identical no matter how the work is divided among parties or devices, and any party can verify a claimed output by independently recomputing it and comparing a short fingerprint.

ideas.title: Density-connected grouping with a single neighborhood threshold
ideas.domain: Spatial database clustering
ideas.problem: Grouping items into clusters of arbitrary shape in large datasets usually requires specifying the number of groups in advance or relying on shape assumptions, and existing methods do not combine minimal user input with efficiency.
ideas.approach: Define a group by local density: an item counts as a core member if its neighborhood of a fixed radius holds enough other items. Groups are formed by chaining core members that lie within each other's neighborhoods, so a group can take any shape, and items reachable from no core member are labeled as noise. Only the radius and the density threshold are needed, and the same local neighborhood queries drive both the definition and the search.
ideas.principle: Membership in a group is defined by transitive reachability through locally crowded regions. Sparse elements that no crowded region reaches are left unassigned, so the number of groups and their shapes emerge from the local density structure rather than from a preset count or global model.

ideas.title: Planner-routed specialist execution with independent validation
ideas.domain: LLM-based scientific programming agents for drug discovery
ideas.problem: Multi-stage workflows with interdependent subtasks and many specialized tools are hard to plan, to match with the right tool, and to execute reliably without errors compounding across stages.
ideas.approach: A planner breaks a complex goal into stages and routes each stage to the specialized model or tool best suited to it. The stages are executed as generated programs, and a separate collaborating agent validates the results before the workflow moves on.
ideas.principle: A coordinator decomposes a multi-stage objective, assigns each stage to the specialist whose capability fits it, runs each stage as an explicit executable procedure, and uses an independent checker to verify each output before it feeds the next stage.

ideas.title: Soft-region local linear rule blending
ideas.domain: Fuzzy system identification and control
ideas.problem: A complex nonlinear input-output relation is hard to model with a single global formula, and hard, sharp partitioning of the domain into regions produces discontinuities at region boundaries.
ideas.approach: The domain is covered by graded (fuzzy) regions, each paired with a simple linear rule fitted from observed data. A prediction is formed by blending the rules, weighting each by the degree to which the current point belongs to its region.
ideas.principle: A complicated mapping is approximated by overlapping graded regions of its domain, each carrying a simple local linear rule, with the rules combined in proportion to membership degree so that the global approximation varies smoothly.

ideas.title: Longest accepted run sets approximability regime
ideas.domain: Approximation complexity of complete symmetric minimization constraint satisfaction problems
ideas.problem: For dense, fully specified systems of group-level constraints, it is unclear which structural property of a rule determines how well the number of violated constraints can be approximated, so most rule families remain unclassified.
ideas.approach: Use the length of the longest unbroken block of consecutive accepted counts as the single parameter that sorts rules into regimes: blocks of length at most two admit near-polynomial-time approximation schemes, while longer blocks admit polynomial-factor approximations whose exponent grows with block length, with matching hardness.
ideas.principle: When every fixed-size group of items is scored by a rule on how many of its members are selected, the hardness of minimizing violations is set by how long a contiguous run of selection counts the rule accepts; short runs leave little slack to exploit and yield tight approximation schemes, while long runs force coarser approximation.

ideas.title: Attractor completion from partial cues via asynchronous local updates
ideas.domain: Neural networks and associative memory
ideas.problem: Storing information so that it can be recovered from a partial or noisy cue, and remains usable when individual components fail, usually needs central control or precise addressing.
ideas.approach: Many simple units each update asynchronously using only signals from their neighbours, with symmetric pairwise couplings set so that stored patterns become stable low-energy states. A fragment of a pattern drives the whole system downhill to the complete stored pattern, and the collective behaviour tolerates failure of individual units.
ideas.principle: A population of simple interacting elements with local, asynchronous update rules and symmetric couplings descends a global energy landscape. Designated target configurations are its attractors, so any sufficiently large part of a target regenerates the whole, and the collective result is insensitive to the failure of single elements.

ideas.title: Averaged exchange bound over guaranteed-free alternatives
ideas.domain: Parameterized approximation for geometric subset selection under pairwise energy
ideas.problem: Choosing k of n items to minimize total pairwise interaction cost is hard to search exhaustively, and the usual bounds on how many candidate representatives must be kept depend on n or are too loose.
ideas.approach: Build a well-spread greedy packing so that removing any one chosen item leaves many unblocked alternative positions. Then bound that item's interaction cost by the average cost it would incur at those free alternatives, which shrinks the candidate pool that must be searched.
ideas.principle: If a well-separated greedy net guarantees many unblocked alternatives for any single chosen element, that element's cost can be bounded by its average over those alternatives, so a small representative pool suffices for an exact-up-to-tolerance search.

ideas.title: Controlled corruption sensitivity benchmark for pairing-quality scorers
ideas.domain: Automatic piano transcription dataset alignment auditing
ideas.problem: Scorers that estimate how well two linked data streams agree are rarely validated against known ground truth, so it is unclear which kinds of mismatch they detect and how finely.
ideas.approach: Take clean matched pairs and inject controlled perturbations of distinct types (timing shifts, value changes, structural edits) at set magnitudes, then measure how sensitive each candidate scorer is to each type. Use the scorer that is most sensitive to the dominant real error type for auditing existing collections.
ideas.principle: To evaluate a consistency scorer, inject known perturbations of separate families and magnitudes into trusted reference pairs, then measure each scorer's response per family to reveal which faults it can detect and at what resolution before applying it to unverified collections.

ideas.title: Adaptive up-down probing for quantile location
ideas.domain: Psychoacoustic threshold testing (up-down staircase procedures)
ideas.problem: Locating the point where a binary-response system switches behavior usually requires either many observations spread across the range or a parametric model of the response curve, which is costly or unreliable when samples are few and assumptions are doubtful.
ideas.approach: Choose each next probe level from the outcome of the previous one: step the level down after one kind of response and up after the other, with step sizes and the placement rule tuned so the probes concentrate where the outcomes split at a chosen proportion. Estimate the location from the visited levels afterward, without assuming a response curve shape.
ideas.principle: A probe value is moved by a fixed rule after each binary result, so that the sequence of probes homes in on the value where results split in a target proportion; the final location is estimated from the trajectory, with no model of the underlying response curve needed.

ideas.title: Random-truncation anticipatory training
ideas.domain: Streaming speech recognition for voice agents
ideas.problem: Streaming predictors emit each symbol only after its unit has fully finished, adding a fixed latency delay before downstream processing can start.
ideas.approach: Train the model on inputs cut off at random points, including mid-unit, and require it to output every unit that is due by the cut in full, plus a short look-ahead guess of the next few units. Use the raw output probabilities as a confidence for the unit still in progress, so the system can act before the unit completes.
ideas.principle: A sequential predictor trained on randomly truncated streams learns to commit to the final form of partially observed items and to anticipate upcoming ones; its own calibrated output probabilities then serve as early confidence for items that have not yet finished arriving.

ideas.title: Local resonator decoupling of response scale from spacing
ideas.domain: Acoustic metamaterials (locally resonant sonic crystals)
ideas.problem: Blocking low-frequency disturbances with conventional barriers requires thickness and mass that scale with the disturbance's wavelength, so the mass-density law limits how much a thin layer can block.
ideas.approach: Embed many small resonant units, each tuned to a target band, in a periodic or disordered arrangement whose spacing is far smaller than the relevant scale. The collective response then creates a strong blocking band and effective negative parameters set by the tuning of the local units, not by the layer thickness.
ideas.principle: Many small, individually tuned local oscillators, densely packed, can impose a strong collective response in a chosen band even when their spacing is far smaller than the scale of the disturbance. The achievable blocking is set by local tuning rather than by overall size or material mass.

ideas.title: Post-hoc gated disentanglement of frozen embeddings
ideas.domain: Music similarity retrieval with pretrained audio foundation models
ideas.problem: General-purpose pretrained representations pack many factors into an entangled latent space, which limits interpretability and fine-grained control over specific attributes, while existing disentangling methods retrain the whole backbone from scratch and discard the value of pretrained models.
ideas.approach: Keep the pretrained encoder frozen and attach a small set of learned masks that gate its embedding into attribute-specific subspaces, adding only minimal trainable adaptation on top. Each attribute then gets its own similarity measure over the gated part of the shared embedding.
ideas.principle: A fixed, general-purpose representation can be retrofitted into named, controllable sub-spaces by learning lightweight selection masks over its dimensions, so that a small amount of added capacity is enough to separate factors and improve retrieval without retraining the base model.

ideas.title: Frozen random anchors with a trainable projection
ideas.domain: Neural speech codecs
ideas.problem: Discrete quantization of learned representations often underuses its vocabulary, so few entries are chosen and the encoding loses detail at low rates.
ideas.approach: The discrete vocabulary is a randomly initialized set of reference vectors that is never trained. A small learned projection maps the features into the space where these fixed vectors are matched, so only the projection adapts.
ideas.principle: A fixed, randomly drawn set of reference points serves as the discrete alphabet, and only a small learned map adapts inputs to it. Because the anchors do not move, assignments stay spread across the alphabet and the trainable parameters are concentrated in the mapping.
concepts: frozen random anchors with trainable projection

ideas.title: Periodicity-induced spectral gap
ideas.domain: Elastic phononic crystals (acoustic band structure of periodic composites)
ideas.problem: Wave propagation through a composite is usually analyzed for single directions or modes, so it is unclear whether a frequency range can be blocked for every direction at once.
ideas.approach: Compute the full band structure of the periodic composite across the whole Brillouin zone and check whether a band gap spans all directions, so that a frequency range is forbidden everywhere in the structure.
ideas.principle: A repeating arrangement of two strongly contrasting components makes waves at certain frequencies unable to propagate in any direction, because multiply reflected partial waves interfere so that no allowed state exists in that frequency range, opening a complete gap in the spectrum.

ideas.title: Modal ladder realization with projection-coupled subsystems
ideas.domain: Loudspeaker radiation impedance modeling (acoustics)
ideas.problem: A distributed system's response over a continuous surface is hard to model exactly as a lumped network, and its modes interact in ways that are unclear to represent compactly.
ideas.approach: Expand the distributed response in orthogonal modes and realize each mode's rational response exactly as a finite passive chain of alternating storage and dissipation elements. Couple the chains through ideal scaling elements set by the projection coefficients, and collapse truncated high-order modes into one residual storage element.
ideas.principle: A coupled continuous process is decomposed into orthogonal components, each realized exactly as a finite chain of alternating storage and loss elements. Components interact only through ideal scaling links set by their projection weights, and discarded components are absorbed into a single lumped residual.

ideas.title: Implosive Focusing of Transient Voids
ideas.domain: Sonochemistry (acoustic cavitation)
ideas.problem: Diffuse, slowly accumulated energy cannot reach the intense, localized peaks in temperature, pressure, or mechanical impact that drive certain reactions.
ideas.approach: A temporary void is grown by a low-intensity driving input and then collapses violently, so the energy accumulated over the whole growth phase is released into a tiny region for a brief moment. The resulting peak conditions are far above the bulk average.
ideas.principle: A transient empty region that grows slowly and then collapses rapidly concentrates energy from a wide surrounding volume into a small, short-lived zone of extreme intensity.

ideas.title: Per-measurement variance weighting instead of bias modeling or rejection
ideas.domain: Vehicle-mounted microphone array calibration for autonomous driving
ideas.problem: Calibrating sensors against a shared target fails when some readings are systematically biased by unmodeled obstructions, because straight-line models do not hold and discarding biased readings wastes data.
ideas.approach: Each reading is weighted by its own timing variance, so biased or shadowed readings are discounted rather than thrown out, and no model of the obstructing body is needed. A single target seen by every sensor, with its position measured by a reference sensor, anchors the joint registration.
ideas.principle: When many noisy readings of a common event are corrupted by unknown structured offsets, weight each reading by its own locally estimated uncertainty in a joint fit. Corrupted readings then lose influence automatically, without a model of the corruption and without hard rejection, and the fit's accuracy approaches the random-noise floor.

ideas.title: Forcing terms fixed by conservation over free solutions
ideas.domain: Electromagnetic theory (foundations of Maxwell's equations)
ideas.problem: A set of free-evolution laws does not by itself determine the coupling terms that connect the system to external quantities, so those terms must be posited rather than derived.
ideas.approach: Take the free-evolution laws as given and require that candidate coupling terms, built from quadratic, covariant densities and fluxes, satisfy local conservation and continuity for every free solution. The resulting coupling terms are unique up to the scale constants of the bookkeeping.
ideas.principle: If a system's unforced dynamics are fixed, the driving terms that exchange a conserved quantity with an outside reservoir can be inferred by demanding that the same local balance holds for every unforced solution. The inferred terms are then unique up to fixed proportionality constants.

ideas.title: Intermediate chunk granularity minimizes code length under bounded predictor capacity
ideas.domain: Information theory of speech and language units
ideas.problem: It is unclear which granularity of segmenting a sequence into symbols yields the lowest coding cost when the predictive model has limited capacity.
ideas.approach: Segment the same sequence at several granularities, from atomic symbols to multi-symbol chunks and intermediate groupings, and measure the bits needed to encode it with predictors of fixed capacity. The best granularity is the one that minimizes total bits per unit of content, not the one with the most structure.
ideas.principle: When a bounded predictor encodes a sequence, the cheapest representation is at an intermediate chunk size. Fine chunks leave too much sequential dependency for the predictor to exploit, while coarse chunks produce a sparse, hard-to-learn symbol inventory. Under a perfect predictor all granularities cost the same, so the optimum appears only under capacity limits.

ideas.title: Implosive cavity collapse for focused energy and rapid quenching
ideas.domain: Sonochemistry and materials chemistry (ultrasound-driven cavitation)
ideas.problem: Reactions that need extreme local temperature and pressure, followed by very fast cooling, usually require bulky specialized equipment, and the energy delivered is spread over the whole volume.
ideas.approach: Drive a liquid with an oscillating field so that many small enclosed voids form and collapse violently. The kinetic energy of the surrounding fluid is focused into the tiny interior of each void, creating a brief, intense hot spot that quenches almost instantly and can drive reactions or form nanostructures.
