ideas.principle: A slowly supplied, diffuse energy input is accumulated and converted into a very small, short-lived region of extreme intensity by the rapid implosion of an enclosed cavity. The resulting extreme state is then quenched almost immediately, which freezes out nonequilibrium products.

ideas.title: Paired human-reference benchmarking on identical decision points
ideas.domain: Turn-taking prediction in multiparty conversation
ideas.problem: Model scores on a prediction benchmark are hard to interpret because nobody has measured how well humans perform the same prediction on the same instances.
ideas.approach: Collect human responses on the exact same decision instances the model is scored on, and report model performance against that per-item human reference. The benchmark is built from matched events with labels that balance the two outcomes.
ideas.principle: Judge an automated predictor by collecting human answers to the identical set of balanced decision instances, so its scores are read against a measured human ceiling on the same items.

ideas.title: Localized revision with preserved anchor state
ideas.domain: Interactive expressive text-to-speech generation
ideas.problem: Refining a generated output usually means rewriting the whole instruction and regenerating everything, which discards parts that were already satisfactory and makes small corrections costly.
ideas.approach: Each revision turn rebuilds a complete specification from the accumulated dialogue, then regenerates only the requested attributes or spans while reusing the previous output as a reference for the untouched regions. Each turn therefore edits a prior version rather than starting over.
ideas.principle: An iterative generator keeps a versioned state. Each revision re-derives a full target specification from the accumulated feedback, regenerates only the components the feedback names, and carries every other component forward unchanged from the prior version.

ideas.title: Accumulation at points of greatest agitation
ideas.domain: Vibrating elastic surfaces and granular particle patterns (Chladni figures)
ideas.problem: The expected rule that loose particles collect where the surface is still (the nodal lines) does not account for the observed pattern, where light particles instead gather at the most violently moving regions.
ideas.approach: Light particles that are not themselves driven are sorted by the local intensity of motion: they are pushed away from quiet regions and collect where the oscillation amplitude is largest. The mechanism is the reverse of simple settling onto rest points.
ideas.principle: Passive, lightweight items distributed over a spatially varying oscillatory medium migrate away from zero-motion locations and accumulate where the local intensity of motion is greatest, so the final distribution maps onto the activity field rather than onto its inactive points.

ideas.title: Round-trip-verified input normalization
ideas.domain: Turkish text-to-speech synthesis
ideas.problem: A generator given compact symbolic notation (digits, abbreviations, foreign names) drops or garbles high-stakes content such as amounts and dates, and nothing in the pipeline reveals the loss.
ideas.approach: Rewrite compact notation into the fully spelled-out form a native reader would naturally produce before generation, and measure whether critical elements survive a generate-then-recognize round trip, which shows the rewrite's effect (96 digit-bearing sentences: 86 preserved with the normalizer versus fewer without it).
ideas.principle: Before generation, rewrite shorthand in the input into the fully expanded form that the output channel can faithfully realize, and verify that the essential tokens survive a generate-then-recognize round trip.

ideas.title: In-context source conditioning with a quality-cost trade-off
ideas.domain: Text-guided music generation and editing with pretrained flow-matching models
ideas.problem: Editing existing content with a pretrained generative model usually needs task-specific adaptation, and naively supplying the full source as in-context input makes long sequences computationally expensive.
ideas.approach: The source material is passed to a pretrained generator as in-context information so one model handles both generation and editing. Two conditioning variants are offered: one appends the context for better edit quality, and the other keeps the original sequence length for much lower compute.
ideas.principle: A pretrained generative model that produces structured sequences from noise can be repurposed for modification by placing the partially known original alongside the target inside its input. How that original is injected, either by lengthening the input for expressiveness or by packing it into a fixed-size slot for efficiency, sets an explicit trade-off between output fidelity and computational cost.

ideas.title: Source-class partition of an ambient aggregate signal
ideas.domain: Soundscape ecology (acoustic ecology of landscapes)
ideas.problem: Diffuse ambient signals that combine many emitters across an area are usually studied as one undifferentiated whole, so their composition and the drivers and effects of each contributing emitter type are not separated.
ideas.approach: Partition the aggregate into a small set of labeled source classes defined by origin (natural-biological, natural-physical, and human-made). Then study each class's causes and consequences and the spatial-temporal patterns of the whole, adapting an established mosaic-ecology framework to organize the analysis.
ideas.principle: A spatially spread superposition of outputs from several emitter types is decomposed into labeled classes by origin. Each class is analyzed for its drivers and effects, and the composite is studied with the spatial-structure framework of a neighboring mature field.

ideas.title: Shared trunk with hot-swappable small per-condition heads
ideas.domain: On-device multilingual speech recognition
ideas.problem: Maintaining a separate full model for each condition (for example each language or script) multiplies storage and load cost until it exceeds client-side limits.
ideas.approach: Compute one large shared representation and attach a tiny condition-specific output head for each case. Only the small head is swapped at use time, and the shared part is stored and loaded once.
ideas.principle: When many conditions share most of their computation, store one common high-capacity representation and many small readout modules. Select the readout at use time so total storage grows only by the small per-condition part.

ideas.title: Retrain downstream stage on upstream's own outputs
ideas.domain: Neural text-to-speech synthesis (acoustic model and vocoder)
ideas.problem: In a cascaded generator, the second stage is usually trained on clean reference data, but at inference it receives the first stage's imperfect outputs, so its input distribution is mismatched and errors accumulate.
ideas.approach: Fine-tune the second stage on the first stage's own generated outputs, so it learns to handle the actual artifacts and errors it will receive at inference. The same approach also exposes artifacts inherited from a teacher model, which a later step can then detect.
ideas.principle: When a later stage in a multi-stage pipeline is trained on ideal inputs but consumes an earlier stage's imperfect outputs, retraining the later stage on those outputs closes the mismatch between training and deployment conditions.

ideas.title: Transfer by shared underlying processes
ideas.domain: Music education and child development
ideas.problem: It is unclear when training in one activity should be expected to improve performance in unrelated domains, so broad claims of general benefit are hard to evaluate.
ideas.approach: Transfer from one activity to another is expected only when the cognitive or motor processes the two activities engage are similar. The benefit also depends on the training being engaging enough to be sustained.
ideas.principle: Practice in one task improves another task only to the extent that they share underlying operations, and the gains appear only when the practice is intrinsically rewarding enough to be sustained.

ideas.title: Staged broad-to-specific mixture curriculum with budget-balanced weighting
ideas.domain: Speech and audio foundation model training
ideas.problem: When one model is trained on many tasks with very unequal amounts of available material, the largest sources dominate, and specialized skills trained later tend to erase earlier general competencies.
ideas.approach: Training proceeds in ordered stages that move from broad, diverse material to narrow, specialized material. At each stage, sampling weights are set per task and per source so that small and large sources contribute in a balanced way, and weighting is chosen to protect skills learned in earlier stages.
ideas.principle: A learner that is built up in successive phases should begin with wide coverage and end with narrow targets. Each phase's sampling mix is rebalanced by source size and by how much each competency needs protection, so that scarce sources are not swamped and earlier competencies are not overwritten.

ideas.title: Unifying separately valid mechanism models into one regime-spanning model
ideas.domain: Nonlinear bubble dynamics in acoustic fields
ideas.problem: Separate models each capture one physical mechanism well, but each fails when the system is driven far from the conditions where it was derived, so no single model covers both the extreme and the moderate regimes.
ideas.approach: Derive one combined model that includes the distinct mechanisms together, then check that it reduces to each established special-case model in its valid regime and stays accurate in the large-forcing regime where the older single-mechanism model breaks down.
ideas.principle: When several independent effects each have a model that holds only in a limited range, a single combined model that keeps all the effects and is validated against each limit can remain accurate over a wider range than any of its parts.

ideas.title: Input-output coverage asymmetry
ideas.domain: Spatial audio-language question answering
ideas.problem: When a model's input contains several entities but the supervising answer describes only one, the model fails to learn the attributes that distinguish the described entity from the others, so attribute information present in the input is not usable for the answer.
ideas.approach: Diagnose the failure as a mismatch between what the input contains and what the target specifies. Fix it by either completing the target so it covers every entity in the input, or by exposing a pairwise contrast signal that makes each entity's attribute separable. Binding an attribute to the queried entity needs both. Keep the pretrained encoder and language model frozen and train only a small bridge.
ideas.principle: A learner whose supervision describes only a subset of the entities it observes cannot tie latent attributes to the subset it is asked about; restoring full coverage of the supervision and exposing a pairwise contrast cue are each sufficient to make the attribute accessible, and binding requires both.
concepts: frozen pretrained backbone with light adapter

ideas.title: Dimensionless-group inverse design with sub-diffusion-length dissipative features
ideas.domain: Acoustics: microperforated panel sound absorbers
ideas.problem: Designing a dissipative absorber for a wide frequency band usually requires trial-and-error tuning of many interacting physical parameters, with no compact rule linking the target response to the geometry.
ideas.approach: Collapse the design space into a few dimensionless groups: a geometry-to-diffusion-length ratio, a normalized resistance, and a resonance frequency. Specify the desired response in those terms and invert the formulas to get the geometry. Small features keep the dissipation effective while the reactive part stays low, which gives broadband behaviour from a shallow cavity.
ideas.principle: A system's full response family is set by a few dimensionless groups that combine feature size with the length scale over which a diffusing quantity dissipates. Choosing the target in those groups and inverting the mapping fixes the structure. Making features small relative to the dissipation length makes damping strong while the stored-energy term stays small.

ideas.title: Practice-negotiated agency across nested feedback loops
ideas.domain: AI feedback musicianship and human-AI co-performance
ideas.problem: Fixed frames that assign control to either the human or the adaptive system cannot describe how agency actually shifts in a coupled human-AI system whose internal recurrent dynamics and external interaction both feed back on each other.
ideas.approach: Treat agency as a continuous, relational quantity that is renegotiated across repeated interactions at both the system's inner feedback level and the outer interaction loop, and build shared competence by working the balance through practice rather than fixing it in the design. Reflections from each participant are read against one another to surface how agency is enacted.
ideas.principle: In a coupled system with nested feedback loops, control is not a fixed property of any one component but a quantity that emerges from repeated mutual perturbation; it is therefore sustained through ongoing adjustment and cannot be fully specified in advance.

ideas.title: Object-as-ongoing-activity reframing
ideas.domain: Musicology and ethnomusicology
ideas.problem: Traditional analysis treats a cultural practice as a fixed object, a work or text, which hides the social relationships that make it meaningful for everyone involved.
ideas.approach: Redefine the thing as an activity, a verb, that includes every form of participation. Then locate its meaning in the relationships the participants enact and in the ritual pattern those relationships form.
ideas.principle: A seemingly fixed entity is better understood as an ongoing process of participation, and its identity lies in the relational pattern that the participants continually enact rather than in the artifact itself.

ideas.title: Off-target mass as a training-free adaptation-gain forecast
ideas.domain: Spoken language diarization with pretrained speech models
ideas.problem: It is unclear in advance how much a pretrained model will gain from fine-tuning on a given dataset, and fine-tuning is costly to run only to find out.
ideas.approach: Compute, without any training, the probability mass a pretrained classifier assigns to non-target classes on the target data, and use this off-target mass as a diagnostic that predicts how much fine-tuning will improve performance.
ideas.principle: A frozen model's probability mass that leaks onto outcomes outside the intended set, measured on unlabeled inputs, signals how far its representation is misaligned with the target task, so it can forecast the benefit of adapting the model before any adaptation is done.

ideas.title: Inverse inference of hidden transient state from emitted signature
ideas.domain: Acoustic cavitation and sonoluminescence spectroscopy
ideas.problem: The internal conditions of a very brief, inaccessible extreme event cannot be measured directly with any instrument, so its peak state is hard to determine.
ideas.approach: Record the light the event emits, generate synthetic emission spectra from a forward model over candidate internal parameters, and take the parameter values whose synthetic spectrum best matches the observed one as the effective state of the event.
ideas.principle: A hidden, short-lived state is recovered by forward-modelling the signal it emits under candidate parameter settings and selecting the settings whose predicted signal best reproduces the observed signal, with each distinct internal energy mode given its own effective parameter.
concepts: indirect state inference from emission signature

ideas.title: Shift-stable feature subset selection
ideas.domain: Audio deepfake detection under codec compression
ideas.problem: Classifiers that perform well on clean in-lab data degrade when the input passes through an unseen degradation process, and the full set of candidate descriptors degrades the most.
ideas.approach: Screen many candidate low-dimensional descriptors for statistically significant, practically large association with the label, then keep only those that remain informative after a known degradation is applied. The surviving descriptors are highly redundant and collapse onto one dominant component, and a small classifier built on them loses far less accuracy under mismatch than one built on the full set.
ideas.principle: When a signal must survive an unseen corruption, selecting a small set of candidate features by their strength and their stability across the corruption, rather than by in-distribution accuracy, yields a compact predictor whose performance changes little under shift; the retained features are redundant views of one dominant latent factor.

ideas.title: Temporal group batching for streamed evaluation
ideas.domain: Real-time streaming speech enhancement and on-device inference
ideas.problem: Processing each arriving unit of a continuous stream with its own model call wastes time on fixed per-call overhead, while the throughput gained by batching is not available when the units must be handled as they arrive.
ideas.approach: Consecutive units from one stream are collected into a group and evaluated in a single call, while independent stream contexts share one model instance. Larger groups raise throughput but add the time spent waiting to collect input, so group size is a tunable parameter.
ideas.principle: Consecutive items from one ordered source are buffered and handled in one batched evaluation, so fixed per-invocation cost is spread over many items; the buffering delay grows with group size, so throughput and latency are traded against each other by a single tunable parameter.

ideas.title: Effective inertia inversion between resonances via a tuned light element
ideas.domain: Acoustic metamaterials (membrane-type sound attenuation)
ideas.problem: Sound attenuation by thin lightweight barriers is limited by the mass density law, so a light barrier cannot block low-frequency sound well.
ideas.approach: A weakly stiff, light film with fixed edges is loaded by a small concentrated mass whose placement shifts its resonant modes. At a frequency lying between two modes, where the spatial average of the response is zero, the system's effective inertia becomes negative and the structure reflects nearly all incident energy.
ideas.principle: A light compliant system with fixed boundaries and a small added point mass has resonances that can be shifted by tuning that mass. Between two adjacent resonances, where the spatially averaged response vanishes, the effective inertia of the whole system takes an opposite sign, which yields a strong global reflection despite low total mass.

ideas.title: Damping-controlled expression of a fixed bias
ideas.domain: Physics of weighted dice and rigid-body tumbling
ideas.problem: A settling process can be biased toward certain outcomes, but it is unclear how the strength of that bias in the final outcome distribution depends on the process's own loss rate, as opposed to the bias alone.
ideas.approach: Separate the bias into a fixed direction of preference and a loss rate that governs how strongly that preference shows up in the outcome distribution. Outcome probabilities then grow exponentially with the preference strength, and faster loss of a transient quantity sharpens the expression of the preference.
ideas.principle: A system that randomly transitions among discrete end states has its final distribution set by two separable parts: a fixed potential that ranks the end states, and a dissipation rate that determines how sharply the ranking translates into probability. Outcome weights scale exponentially with the potential, and the dissipation rate acts as an effective sharpness parameter.

ideas.title: Correspondence-principle operator substitution for dissipation
ideas.domain: Poroelastic wave theory (acoustic propagation in porous media)
ideas.problem: A conservative model of wave propagation cannot describe energy loss, time-dependent response, or relaxation when its material coefficients are fixed constants.
ideas.approach: Keep the solved structure of the lossless model and replace each constant coefficient with a time-dependent operator, obtained by transforming the constitutive relation so that the same solution form carries over. The operators then define relaxation spectra for different dissipation models.
ideas.principle: A system's constant coefficients can be promoted to operators acting on histories through a transform that maps time convolution to multiplication, so a solved lossless theory yields its dissipative counterpart with the same structure and new spectral content.

ideas.title: Single-mode dual sign reversal
ideas.domain: Acoustic metamaterials (effective-medium design)
ideas.problem: Engineered composites that need two coupled effective response parameters to be negative at the same time are usually built from two separate mechanisms, which makes the design complicated and hard to realize as a true effective medium.
ideas.approach: Use one tuned low-frequency mode of a small repeated element so that its response makes both effective parameters of the composite negative together. Because the two negative values come from the same structure, the design is simpler than stacking two separate mechanisms.
ideas.principle: A single low-frequency natural mode of a repeated unit can drive two coupled effective coefficients of the aggregate system to opposite-signed, out-of-the-ordinary values at once, so that one structure controls both properties instead of two independent mechanisms.

ideas.title: Direct per-source token conditioning of a pretrained generator
ideas.domain: Brain-to-audio reconstruction from fMRI with audio diffusion models
ideas.problem: Two-stage pipelines first decode measurements into a predefined intermediate representation and only then synthesize output, which limits what the generator can use from the raw multi-channel signal.
ideas.approach: Skip the intermediate supervised decoder and feed each measurement region's signal through its own projection into learned tokens, which condition a large pretrained generative transformer via a dedicated cross-attention pathway, trained end-to-end.
ideas.principle: A large pretrained generative model is steered directly by several heterogeneous sensor channels: each channel is mapped by its own learned projection into a set of trainable tokens that enter the model through a separate attention route, with no intermediate target-prediction stage.
concepts: frozen pretrained backbone with light adapter

ideas.title: Joint internal-trajectory denoising
ideas.domain: Text-to-speech waveform generation with diffusion models
ideas.problem: Multi-stage generation pipelines depend on separately trained intermediate representations, external decoders, and external alignment modules, which add error sources and break end-to-end training.
ideas.approach: A single diffusion model denoises an internal auxiliary trajectory jointly with the target trajectory, using disentangled output heads and one combined loss. The intermediate structure and input-output alignment are learned inside the model, so no separately trained stage or external aligner is needed.
ideas.principle: One generative process jointly denoises an auxiliary sequence and the target signal through separate output heads under a shared objective, so intermediate structure and alignment are learned internally rather than supplied by external stages.

ideas.title: Shared characteristic length reused for a second frequency response
ideas.domain: Acoustics of fluid-saturated porous media
ideas.problem: The frequency dependence of the bulk modulus of the fluid inside a porous material at high frequencies lacks a compact phenomenological description tied to the material's known response.
ideas.approach: The characteristic length that defines a dynamic response function for one quantity is extended to govern a second, related quantity. Reusing this single length gives a general frequency dependence for the second quantity, which is then checked against measurements.
ideas.principle: A single length scale that sets the crossover in one frequency-dependent response can be reused to set the crossover in a coupled response, so one parameter yields a consistent, phenomenological frequency dependence for both.

ideas.title: Polarity-aware contrastive directive encoding
ideas.domain: text-guided speaker extraction and speech enhancement
ideas.problem: Small text encoders often fail to distinguish instructions with opposite intent (keep vs. remove), and large language models that handle this are too computationally costly to use as conditioning front ends.
ideas.approach: A compact pretrained text-retrieval encoder is contrastively fine-tuned so that paraphrases of the same instruction map close together while instructions with opposite polarity are pushed apart. The resulting lightweight encoder conditions a single unified model that handles both keep and remove directives.
ideas.principle: A small pretrained encoder of natural-language directives is contrastively tuned so that equivalent rewordings cluster together and opposite-intent directives separate, giving a cheap, intent-sensitive conditioning signal for one shared model in place of a large language model.

ideas.title: Dimension-restricted variable exchange between systems
ideas.domain: Acoustic cloaking via coordinate transformations in fluids and elastic media
ideas.problem: Coordinate-transformation design methods that work for one wave system (electromagnetics) do not in general carry over to another (elastic media), because the governing equations are not form-invariant under the transformation.
ideas.approach: Find a variable exchange that rewrites the governing equations of one system into the exact form of another, but only in a two-dimensional geometry, and that also maps boundary conditions unchanged. Transformation-type solutions known for the first system then apply directly to the second.
ideas.principle: A change of variables can map one system's governing relations exactly onto another system's form only when the ambient dimension is special. Solutions and design rules derived for the first system then transfer to the second, provided the mapping also preserves boundary conditions; in other dimensions the transfer fails.

ideas.title: Evidence-linked supervision of judgments
ideas.domain: Automatic evaluation of generated speech with learned reward models
ideas.problem: Pairwise preference judges are trained only on the final verdict, so the connection between specific local parts of the input and the overall judgment stays implicit and cannot be inspected or verified.
ideas.approach: Build training targets that pair the final preference with a structured set of observations, each tied to a localized segment of the input, the property it affects, and the verdict it supports. Generate these reports by aligning segments, pooling analyses from several models, and resolving disagreements through targeted deliberation, then train the judge to produce the reports from the raw input pair.
ideas.principle: A judge's verdict over a pair of inputs is supervised together with a set of localized observations, each anchored to a segment of the input, a named quality dimension, and the verdict it supports, so that the path from parts to whole is explicit and checkable.

ideas.title: Linearizing lift for invariance discovery
ideas.domain: Physics-informed neural networks for symmetries and conservation laws of Newtonian dynamics
ideas.problem: Finding the symmetries and conserved quantities of a nonlinear dynamical system from noisy data requires solving nonlinear invariance conditions, which is hard to do directly and hard to validate.
ideas.approach: Embed the system in a higher-dimensional extended space where the invariance conditions become linear in the generator fields. Solve those linear conditions with a random-feature network, build the algebra and conserved quantities from the learned generators, and check consistency with an independently computed curvature-type invariant.
ideas.principle: A nonlinear invariance requirement becomes a linear one once the system is lifted into a higher-dimensional space with an added coordinate and a fixed structure. The solution space of the linear conditions is then found with a fixed random basis and trained coefficients, and an independently derived quantity tests the result.
concepts: frozen random anchors with trainable projection

ideas.title: Norm-bounded latent regularized compression for generation
ideas.domain: Live generative audio autoencoders
ideas.problem: A compressor that yields compact codes for a downstream generator often trades away reconstruction quality, and its codes can be poorly scaled or fragile for a generative model to sample from, while streaming use requires strictly causal processing.
ideas.approach: Constrain the compressed code to a fixed-radius shell by projecting it onto a hypersphere, add bounded-magnitude noise to the code during training, and align the code with pretrained representations so that one compact space serves both reconstruction and generation under causal, streaming constraints.
ideas.principle: A code that must be both faithfully decodable and easy for a generative model to sample is kept well-conditioned by fixing its norm and perturbing it within a bounded radius, so that small errors in generated codes stay within the region the decoder handles well.

ideas.title: Directional bias splits degenerate loop modes for one-way isolation
ideas.domain: Acoustic metamaterials and nonreciprocal sound transmission
ideas.problem: Isolators and circulators that block transmission in one direction normally need nonlinearity or magnetic materials, which require high power or large volumes.
ideas.approach: Build a compact closed loop resonator and circulate a fluid through it. The flow gives the loop a directional bias that splits its degenerate resonant modes by traversal direction, so a wave entering from one side couples to a resonance while the reverse direction is detuned and blocked.
ideas.principle: A symmetric closed loop of resonators has paired modes that travel in opposite directions and are degenerate. A directional bias that breaks time-reversal symmetry lifts that degeneracy, so the two traversal directions see different resonant frequencies. Coupling then depends strongly on direction, giving large one-way isolation from a small, linear, subwavelength structure.

ideas.title: Bounded arrival-order memory for streaming identity consistency
ideas.domain: Streaming speaker diarization (end-to-end neural speech processing)
ideas.problem: In streaming processing, a model that labels entities chunk by chunk tends to lose track of which label belongs to which entity across chunk boundaries, and re-processing the full history to fix this is too costly for low-latency use.
ideas.approach: Keep a fixed-size cache of embeddings for previously seen entities, stored in the order they first arrived. Each new chunk is labeled by comparing its items against this cache, so identities stay consistent without revisiting the whole history.
ideas.principle: A sequential process assigns persistent labels to recurring entities as they arrive in chunks. It stores a bounded set of representative exemplars per entity, kept in first-arrival order, and matches each new chunk against this store, so label consistency is maintained from compact state rather than full history.

ideas.title: Proportional proxy for intractable force
ideas.domain: Acoustics: acoustic radiation pressure on spheres
ideas.problem: A mean force on a body immersed in a wave-like medium is hard to measure directly, and exact solutions for it become intractable diffraction problems at high frequencies and small amplitudes.
ideas.approach: Assume the force is proportional to the local energy density near the body, so relative measurements can be made from that density without solving the full scattering problem. The proportionality is claimed to hold without restriction on scale, for both progressive and stationary regimes.
ideas.principle: A quantity that is costly to observe directly can be inferred from a locally proportional density of the medium's energy around the object, so comparisons need only the density ratio and not the exact boundary solution.

ideas.title: Anticommuting symmetries yield protected boundary modes
ideas.domain: Topological acoustics (classical wave lattices)
ideas.problem: Protected edge states are usually tied to a specific bulk topology, but a general recipe for guaranteeing robust boundary modes from a system's symmetry structure is missing.
ideas.approach: Build a time-reversal-invariant system that has both a translation symmetry and a chiral (sign-alternating) symmetry, and arrange that these two symmetries anticommute. This yields a nontrivial discrete invariant, and the resulting boundary modes are shown to survive perturbations such as paired identical defects.
ideas.principle: When two structural symmetries of a system fail to commute in a specific anti-aligned way, their interplay fixes a discrete invariant, and that invariant forces localized boundary states that persist under any perturbation respecting the symmetry structure.

ideas.title: Monotone transport for local supervision from global labels
ideas.domain: Audio-text contrastive pretraining for retrieval and temporal localization
ideas.problem: Pooling a sequence uniformly into one global embedding discards its order and timing, so short events in long sequences are lost and local localization suffers, while only coarse global labels are available for training.
ideas.approach: Align the elements of two ordered sequences with a monotone one-dimensional optimal transport plan trained contrastively, and use the learned marginals and plan as fine-grained local targets derived only from clip-level labels. At inference, skip the transport and score local elements with cheap pairwise similarities, while global matching uses pooled embeddings.
ideas.principle: A coarse global match between two ordered streams can be decomposed into a learned order-preserving correspondence that yields dense local supervision, and the correspondence is needed only during training, so deployment uses inexpensive local similarity and pooled comparisons.

ideas.title: Intersection of stability constraints defines the operating window
ideas.domain: Single-bubble sonoluminescence (acoustically driven bubble collapse)
ideas.problem: A desired concentrated output can occur only under a narrow set of conditions, and tuning one criterion alone does not reveal which operating region actually produces it.
ideas.approach: The effect is expected only where several separate stability conditions (shape stability, diffusive stability) hold together with an energy-concentration condition. The feasible region is therefore the intersection of these individual constraint regions, which fixes the parameter space where the effect appears.
ideas.principle: A concentrated output appears only where several independent stability constraints and a concentration condition hold simultaneously, so the feasible region is the intersection of the individual constraint regions.

ideas.title: Discriminator-free adversarial alignment via the predictor's own outputs
ideas.domain: Speech classification under domain shift (unsupervised domain adaptation)
ideas.problem: Adversarial adaptation to a shifted input distribution usually needs a separate critic network to tell source from target, and that extra adversary is often unstable and hard to train.
ideas.approach: The task predictor itself serves as the adversary: unlabeled inputs from the shifted distribution are aligned by minimizing a nuclear-norm Wasserstein discrepancy between the predictor's output distributions, so no separate discriminator is trained.
ideas.principle: A single model can act as both the critic and the learner: its own output responses on two unlabeled input populations are compared with a robust, structure-aware distance that the model is trained to shrink, removing the need for a second adversarial network.

ideas.title: Form-preserving reparametrization that hides a distortion in coefficients
ideas.domain: Elastodynamics and transformation-based cloaking
ideas.problem: Applying a geometric distortion to a governing law normally changes the law's form, so a distorted region becomes detectable as a deviation from the standard equations.
ideas.approach: Map the governing equations under an arbitrary change of coordinates and let the resulting extra terms and anisotropic coefficients absorb the distortion, so the equations keep their original form. An external observer then sees the transformed region as an unaltered, homogeneous system.
ideas.principle: A system governed by a fixed rule can be re-described under any invertible relabeling of its domain; if the rule's coefficients are allowed to take up the relabeling, the rule keeps its shape and a modified region cannot be told apart from an unmodified one from outside.

ideas.title: Asymmetric positional scaling for monotone cross-alignment
ideas.domain: Rap voice synthesis from beat, lyrics, and reference voice (flow-matching generative audio)
ideas.problem: When one sequence must be aligned to another of a different, externally fixed length under strong timing conditioning, cross-attention tends to skip or repeat elements, and existing remedies rely on explicit duration prediction or phoneme-level alignment.
ideas.approach: Apply rotary positional encodings to cross-attention with a scaling factor on only one side, so the conditioning sequence's positions are stretched onto the output timeline. This gives the attention a built-in positional prior for sequential correspondence, letting the output length vary without predicting durations.
ideas.principle: Aligning two sequences of different lengths by rescaling the position index of only one of them, so that a positional encoding in the attention step imposes an ordered, monotone correspondence and removes the need for an explicit length or boundary model.

ideas.title: Equation-isomorphism design transfer
ideas.domain: Acoustic metamaterials and wave cloaking
ideas.problem: A design method for shaping a field's behavior is hard to apply directly to a new physical system whose governing law differs in form, so each system would otherwise need its own design theory.
ideas.approach: The governing law of the target system is rewritten so that it takes the same mathematical form as a different, already-understood law. The design tool that works for the known law, here a coordinate transformation, is then applied unchanged to the target system.
ideas.principle: If a system's governing rule can be rewritten to have the same form as a second rule with a known design toolkit, every construction valid for the second rule carries over to the first without re-derivation.

ideas.title: Posterior-overlap continuity calibration of evidence strength
ideas.domain: Bayesian tonal-key inference from pitch evidence in music
ideas.problem: The strength of noisy local evidence that governs how sharply a sequential Bayesian state estimator concentrates its posterior is unset, and expert labels cannot fix it because they do not specify the full posterior over candidate states.
ideas.approach: Measure the overlap between posteriors of adjacent overlapping windows as a continuity score, then find the evidence-strength setting at which carrying the previous belief forward is predictively equivalent to restarting from a uniform prior. Choose settings where transitions that structurally should preserve state continuity keep the score above that threshold, using a selectivity-sweep share to locate the usable region.
ideas.principle: A sequential probabilistic estimator's observation-sharpness parameter can be calibrated without ground-truth posteriors: require that consecutive overlapping-window beliefs stay mutually consistent for transitions expected to be gradual, and pick the sharpness at which keeping the prior is no better than resetting to an uninformative prior.

ideas.title: Multi-level coupling disruption with energy-constrained perturbation
ideas.domain: Audio protection against talking-head deepfake generation
ideas.problem: A generative model that depends on precise alignment between two linked streams can be misused, but protecting the one stream against that use has been little studied and is easy to undo by denoising or adaptive attacks.
ideas.approach: Disrupt the link between the streams directly at the coupling step and also degrade the embeddings of the protected stream. Confine the perturbations to the high-energy components of a transform of the stream so that post-processing that removes them would also damage the signal.
ideas.principle: To stop a downstream system from exploiting a signal's coupling to another signal, corrupt the coupling and the signal's internal representation together, and place the corruption where removing it would also destroy the signal's own content, while keeping the signal's perceptible quality intact.

ideas.title: Loss-rate matching for maximum resonant absorption
ideas.domain: Acoustic resonator design
ideas.problem: A resonator's absorption peak is limited when its internal dissipation and its coupling to the outside channel are not balanced, so the design that maximizes absorption is unclear when several loss mechanisms act together.
ideas.approach: Model the resonator's total losses as separate internal and radiative channels, then choose geometry so these rates are equal, which gives maximum absorption at resonance. Summarize the resulting optimum across parameters in design charts.
ideas.principle: A resonant mode absorbs incoming energy maximally when its internal dissipation rate equals its rate of coupling to the external channel; competing loss sources are optimized jointly by equating these rates.

ideas.title: Reconstruct-then-condition from a cheap partial observation
ideas.domain: Room acoustic parameter mapping from floor plans and reverberant speech
ideas.problem: Dense spatial maps of environment parameters can be predicted from layout alone, but accurate prediction needs a reference measurement that is costly or impractical to obtain. Simple scalar summaries of cheap observations fail to supply the needed information.
ideas.approach: Replace the expensive reference with a cheap, easily recorded observation from a single source-sensor pair, and reconstruct from it a full intermediate representation of the missing reference. Feed that reconstructed representation, alongside the layout, into the spatial predictor as conditioning, rather than feeding raw features or a single scalar estimate.
ideas.principle: A structural prior (layout) is combined with a cheap partial signal that is first reconstructed into the full hidden reference form and then used as conditioning. The reconstructed form carries more usable information than scalar summaries, and the cheap signal mainly calibrates the global level of the output, while the spatial variation still comes from the structural prior.
concepts: indirect state inference from emission signature

ideas.title: Binding a physical sensing signature to content for live-source authentication
ideas.domain: Mobile speech interaction and voice security
ideas.problem: Watermarking schemes for speech protect offline files or label synthetic audio, so they cannot confirm at capture time that a live signal comes from the genuine source and has not been altered in transit.
ideas.approach: At capture, an active probe sends a multi-frequency signal through the source's body and reads back a source-specific response, which is fused with a content-dependent embedding. The result is a dynamic dual-layer mark: a persistent source identifier plus a per-item identifier that also detects tampering later in propagation.
ideas.principle: Authenticity of a stream is established by binding a persistent, hard-to-copy property of the emitter, measured through an active probe at the moment of creation, to the content itself, so that a fresh per-item code exposes any later modification.
concepts: indirect state inference from emission signature

ideas.title: Edge-side privacy bottleneck for split sensing
ideas.domain: Acoustic occupancy sensing in buildings
ideas.problem: Continuous sensing streams can reveal private content when raw signals are sent to a remote model, yet the remote model needs only task-relevant information.
ideas.approach: A local encoder reduces each short window of raw signal to a compact embedding or class probabilities on the device, and only that code is transmitted to a server-side temporal model that infers the state over time. Shrinking the transmitted code to fewer dimensions or to output probabilities limits how much of the original content an attacker can recover while keeping task accuracy.
ideas.principle: Split a streaming inference pipeline so that a local stage compresses each raw high-dimensional window into a low-dimensional task-relevant code, and only that code leaves the source for a remote sequence model that tracks the hidden state over time. The transmitted code is made as narrow as the decision requires, so private detail in the input is discarded before it can be exposed.

ideas.title: Lumped-network realization of a continuous transformation design
ideas.domain: Underwater ultrasound acoustic cloaking (coordinate-transformation metamaterials)
ideas.problem: Continuous coordinate-transformation designs that specify a smoothly varying material property are hard to build practically, and resonant building blocks restrict them to narrow bands with high loss.
ideas.approach: The continuous design is approximated by a discrete network of simple nonresonant elements, arranged so the composite reproduces the target response over a broad range. Because the elements do not resonate, the device stays low-loss and works across a wide frequency band, and the same design method can be scaled to other operating frequencies.
ideas.principle: A continuous target field that prescribes spatially varying response is realized by tiling a region with a discrete network of simple, non-resonant reactive units whose series and shunt couplings reproduce the target, so broadband, low-loss behavior comes from avoiding resonance in the building blocks.

ideas.title: Similarity-guided posterior sampling for missing-segment infilling
ideas.domain: Music audio inpainting with diffusion models
ideas.problem: Generative infilling of a large missing segment often produces locally plausible but globally incoherent content because the model has no direct reference to what fits the surrounding context.
ideas.approach: Retrieve candidate replacement segments from elsewhere in the same signal by contextual similarity, then use them to guide a pre-trained generative model's sampling process toward coherent completions. The guidance layer is independent of which generative model is used.
ideas.principle: A missing region in a sequence is regenerated by a fixed generative sampler whose trajectory is steered by exemplars retrieved from elsewhere in the same sequence, selected by how well their surroundings match the gap's surroundings. The sampler itself is left unchanged.

ideas.title: Folded internal path for extreme effective response
ideas.domain: Acoustic metamaterials
ideas.problem: Obtaining extreme effective material parameters usually requires local resonant subwavelength structures, which work over narrow bands and add loss.
ideas.approach: Curl the internal perforations so the propagating signal follows a coiled path within a fixed unit cell. The long folded path sets an effective response that is dispersive and extreme across a broad range, with no resonators needed.
ideas.principle: A bounded element with a long internal traversal, folded into a compact region, takes on an effective response set by its geometry rather than by resonance, and this response can be tuned across a broad band.

ideas.title: Cue-steered teacher distillation into a compact student
ideas.domain: Bioacoustic denoising of animal vocalizations
ideas.problem: Strong general-purpose separation models are too heavy for practical local use, while fast specialized denoisers remove less noise, and the best pipelines depend on a separate activity detector.
ideas.approach: A large general-purpose model is steered at inference time with coarse activity spans from a simple detector, producing high-quality outputs without any training. Those steered outputs then train a small, fast student model that needs no detector, so the student keeps most of the teacher's quality at a fraction of the cost.
ideas.principle: A slow, general system given cheap coarse hints can serve as a teacher whose hint-conditioned outputs train a compact student that runs without the hints. The student gives up a small amount of quality for a large gain in speed and independence from auxiliary components.

ideas.title: Full-distribution model with threshold summaries derived from it
ideas.domain: Environmental noise annoyance and transportation exposure
ideas.problem: Survey studies typically estimate separate threshold-based summaries (such as percent above a cutoff) for each exposure metric, so the relationships are fit piecemeal, lack a common basis, and give poorly grounded confidence intervals.
ideas.approach: Model the whole response distribution, with its mean shifting as a function of the exposure, and fit that model once to pooled data. Any cutoff-based summary is then computed from the fitted distribution, and the resulting exposure-to-summary curves are reported as low-order polynomial approximations that are easier to apply.
ideas.principle: Fit one parametric model of an entire population's response distribution whose location shifts with a driving input. Every threshold-based summary then follows from that single fit, and the implied curves are compressed into simple polynomial forms for practical use.

ideas.title: One-class normality scoring with deviation ranking
ideas.domain: Audio deepfake detection with frozen self-supervised speech representations
ideas.problem: Supervised detectors trained on known attack types learn generator-specific shortcuts and fail when new generators or acoustic conditions appear, so the detector cannot generalize to unseen anomalies.
ideas.approach: Fit a shrinkage-Mahalanobis model only on pooled hidden states from a frozen pretrained encoder, using nominal (authentic) samples alone, and flag inputs by how far they deviate from that normal distribution. The paper also finds that recalibrating the decision threshold cannot recover ranking quality lost upstream under distribution shift.
ideas.principle: A model fit only to the nominal class of a system, over features from a fixed pretrained embedding, scores new inputs by their distance from that nominal distribution. Because the score is a ranking, any later threshold adjustment is bounded by how well that ranking separates the classes, so distribution shift that degrades the ranking cannot be repaired downstream.
concepts: frozen pretrained backbone with light adapter

ideas.title: Periodicity-induced spectral gap via Bloch eigenproblem
ideas.domain: Elastic phononic crystals (periodic elastic composites)
ideas.problem: Spatially periodic composites with position-dependent material parameters have no simple way to predict which frequency ranges propagate and which are blocked across all directions of the lattice.
ideas.approach: Derive an eigenvalue equation for the periodic structure using Bloch wave vectors, so that each band's frequency is a function of the wave vector over the Brillouin zone. Then compute the band structure for lattice configurations and check whether frequency intervals with no eigenvalues remain for every wave vector.
ideas.principle: A system whose coefficients vary periodically in space splits into eigenmodes labeled by a quasi-momentum; when the resulting spectrum has intervals containing no modes for any quasi-momentum, activity in those intervals is forbidden throughout the lattice, producing a全 global gap set by the periodicity and contrast of the material parameters.

ideas.title: Expert-curated small-data specialization of generative models
ideas.domain: generative AI for culturally specific sound art
ideas.problem: Large-scale generative models trained on abundant generic data reproduce dominant biases and cannot represent niche, culturally specific material.
ideas.approach: Build a small, deliberately curated dataset chosen by domain experts and fit general-purpose generative architectures to it, so the model learns the fine-grained structure of that niche rather than the broad average.
ideas.principle: A generator fit to a small, expert-selected sample of a narrow distribution can capture fine-grained structure that a broad generator trained on abundant generic data cannot reach, because the selection and conditioning encode the specialized target directly.

ideas.title: Single-shot ensemble averaging via time integral of a deterministic probe response
ideas.domain: Room acoustics (reverberation time measurement)
ideas.problem: Estimating the average decay behavior of a system normally requires many randomized probe trials or noisy measurements, which yield jagged curves and make subtle nonexponential behavior hard to detect.
ideas.approach: Excite the system once with a short deterministic burst, then take a simple integral over its full response. The integral reproduces the average that many randomized-excitation trials would give, so a single measurement produces a smooth averaged curve.
ideas.principle: A single deterministic probe whose response is accumulated over time can stand in for the average over an ensemble of randomized probes, so one trial yields a smooth statistic that would otherwise need repeated sampling.
concepts: single-shot ensemble averaging via time integral

ideas.title: Personal low-rank adapter over a frozen shared model
ideas.domain: Automatic speech recognition for dysarthric speakers
ideas.problem: A general-purpose large model trained on typical inputs fails systematically for a minority of users whose input distribution differs markedly, and standard deployment offers no practical way to correct this for an individual.
ideas.approach: Keep the large pretrained model's weights frozen and train a small low-rank adapter on a few hours of the individual's own labeled recordings, using consumer hardware. The adapted model then runs entirely on the user's own device so no data leaves it.
ideas.principle: A large shared model that systematically fails on a minority of inputs can be corrected for one individual by freezing its weights and training a small low-rank correction on a modest set of that individual's own labeled examples, with all inference kept local.
concepts: frozen pretrained backbone with light adapter
online personalization of a shared model

ideas.title: Matched-tuning null comparison for structural claims
ideas.domain: Connectome-constrained neural circuit modelling (Drosophila)
ideas.problem: Claims that a measured structure beats shuffled or rewired alternatives are confounded, because the structure's model was tuned on its own wiring while nulls inherit nuisance parameters that were tuned for the real structure, so the apparent advantage can come from tuning effort rather than from the structure.
ideas.approach: Compare each structural variant under explicitly separated tuning protocols: parameters tuned on the reference structure and transferred to nulls, each variant tuned on its own, and the own-tuned variant restricted to parameter ranges consistent with independent data. Check whether the verdict survives across protocols, training lengths and checkpoints, and confirm that the model still functions in the regime where the verdict is decided.
ideas.principle: An advantage attributed to a fixed structural arrangement is valid only when every alternative receives the same optimisation budget and nuisance parameters are constrained by evidence independent of the comparison; otherwise the sign of the gap can be set by how the free parameters were chosen.

ideas.title: Affine relations preserved under single-channel perturbation
ideas.domain: Nonlinear population dynamics (generalized Lotka-Volterra systems)
ideas.problem: Nonlinear coupled systems with extinctions and chaos are usually assumed to respond to a local change in one component in a complicated, unpredictable way, so simple structural relations among their steady-state or time-averaged quantities are not expected to survive large changes.
ideas.approach: Treat any change to one component's dynamics as acting on every other component through a single effective scalar input. Because that input is one-dimensional, the stationary quantities stay affinely related to one another for arbitrarily large changes, holding piecewise across regime switches and as time averages on chaotic attractors.
ideas.principle: When a local modification to one unit of a coupled network reaches all other units only through one shared effective channel, the units' stationary states remain linked by fixed affine relations regardless of how strong the modification is, even through discrete regime changes and chaotic dynamics.

ideas.title: Single-statistic failure attribution with matched counterfactual controls
ideas.domain: Connectome-constrained neural network models of fly visual motion perception
ideas.problem: When a model fails on certain inputs, it is unclear which low-level signal property causes the failure, and whether the failure reflects that property or simply the inputs being unfamiliar to the model.
ideas.approach: The paper optimizes one low-level input statistic by itself, without access to the model, and checks whether this alone induces failure. It also builds counterfactual inputs that are equally distant from the training distribution but restore correct behavior, which rules out unfamiliarity as the cause.
ideas.principle: To attribute a system's failure to one shared low-level signal property, show that manipulating only that property, with no access to the system, reproduces the failure. Then use a control input matched on distance from the training distribution but differing in that property to rule out distributional novelty as the explanation.

ideas.title: Shrinkage of per-unit estimates toward a pooled trend
ideas.domain: RNA-seq differential expression analysis
ideas.problem: When many parallel units are each measured with only a few replicates, their individual estimates of effect size and variability are unstable, and extreme values from a handful of noisy samples can mislead ranking and interpretation.
ideas.approach: Fit a trend across all units to capture how variability depends on overall level, then shrink each unit's own estimate toward that trend, with the amount of shrinkage set by how informative that unit's data are. Effect sizes are shrunk the same way so that the reported magnitudes are more stable and interpretable.
ideas.principle: Many parallel noisy estimates with few samples each are stabilized by borrowing strength across all units: each estimate is pulled toward a trend fitted to the whole population, with the pull weighted by how reliable that unit's own data are.
concepts: empirical-bayes shrinkage toward a pooled trend

ideas.title: Early growth-rate bracketing of a threshold eigenvalue
ideas.domain: Bayesian inference for epidemic reaction-diffusion models
ideas.problem: Whether a spreading process persists or dies out is set by a threshold quantity that depends on several unknown rates, so early noisy observations seem insufficient to decide the outcome when each rate is uncertain.
ideas.approach: Show that the early dynamics and the threshold quantity depend on the unknown parameters only through one combined quantity, then bound the threshold quantity by the growth rate of a norm of the state measured between two early times. The lower bound holds for the full nonlinear system, and the upper bound separates transient effects from saturation.
ideas.principle: When a system's long-run threshold and its early linear growth are governed by the same combination of unknown parameters, the observed early growth rate of a state norm brackets that threshold, so the outcome can be inferred from early data without identifying each parameter.

ideas.title: Backward covector recursion for exact gradients through a latent-state filter
ideas.domain: Microbiome population dynamics inference from noisy time series
ideas.problem: Maximum-likelihood fitting of a model with latent states observed through noise needs gradients of a likelihood that is built by a sequential filter, and naive gradient methods scale with the number of parameters.
ideas.approach: Compute the likelihood with a sequential filter, then obtain the exact gradient by a single backward pass that propagates a covector through the closed-form derivative of each filter step. The cost is a small fixed number of likelihood evaluations regardless of how many parameters are estimated.
ideas.principle: When an objective is accumulated by a chain of recursive state updates, its exact gradient with respect to any number of parameters can be obtained by one reverse sweep that carries a dual variable back through each step's transposed Jacobian, so the cost is set by the chain length rather than the parameter count.

ideas.title: Symbol-specific termination ladder readout
ideas.domain: DNA sequencing by chain termination (molecular biology)
ideas.problem: Reading the ordered sequence of symbols in a long linear polymer is hard when the only available readout is the whole copied molecule, which does not reveal the identity of each position.
ideas.approach: Copy the polymer in separate reactions, each containing a rare analog that halts extension specifically at one symbol type, so every reaction yields a population of partial copies that stop at every occurrence of that symbol. Sorting the partial copies by length then reveals the position and identity of each symbol in order.
ideas.principle: A sequential builder that adds symbols one at a time can be made to reveal its order by running parallel trials in which a sparse, symbol-specific stop signal truncates partial constructions at each occurrence of that symbol; the ordered set of stopping lengths, read out by size separation, encodes the full sequence.

ideas.title: Constraint-bounded optimality as a design principle
ideas.domain: Neural coding and computation (optimization principles in sensory systems)
ideas.problem: Explaining why a system has the structure and parameters it does is usually done by fitting models with many free parameters, which gives descriptions rather than derivations and leaves open whether the observed design is special.
ideas.approach: Treat the best achievable performance under the stated physical and resource constraints as the governing principle, derive the mechanism and its functional form from that optimum with no free parameters, and check whether near-optimal performance holds over a broad region of parameter space so that finely tuned values are not required.
ideas.principle: A system's structure is derived as the best possible performance allowed by its stated constraints, with no adjustable parameters; if the near-optimal region of the parameter space is broad, the derived design works without precise tuning.

ideas.title: Consistency-preserving filtering of linked record pairs
ideas.domain: Bioinformatics: next-generation sequencing read preprocessing
ideas.problem: When each record in a linked pair is filtered independently, one mate can be discarded while the other survives, which breaks the pairing and makes the paired data inconsistent.
ideas.approach: Apply a configurable, ordered chain of per-record filters to both members of each pair. Keep a pair only when both members survive, and route each surviving member whose partner was removed to a separate orphan output.
ideas.principle: When a sequence of independent per-item filters acts on two coupled streams, the items whose partner survives are kept together as matched units and the leftover unmatched items are segregated into their own stream, so the pairing invariant is never silently broken.

ideas.title: Counting-limited directional sensing
ideas.domain: Cellular chemical gradient sensing (chemotaxis)
ideas.problem: It is unclear how many discrete absorption events a sensor must collect, and so how much energy it must dissipate, to approach the physical precision limit of estimating a directional asymmetry.
ideas.approach: Closed-form expressions link the uncertainty of a directional estimate to the number of absorbed events, with a bounded contrast factor that reflects how strongly the sensor responds to direction. In the strong-signal regime the required event count depends only on the relative change in intensity across the sensor, and the measured system sits far below the energy-limited bound, so counting noise rather than energy is the binding constraint.
ideas.principle: An observer that estimates the direction of a weak asymmetry in a flux of discrete, independent arrival events is limited by the statistics of counting those arrivals. Directional information is a bounded fraction of total-count information, so precision is set by how many events are collected and not by the energy spent collecting them.

ideas.title: Redundancy-discounted member weighting in progressive aggregation
ideas.domain: Bioinformatics: progressive multiple sequence alignment of protein sequences
ideas.problem: When a set of items is combined incrementally by merging pairs into growing partial results, clusters of near-duplicate members dominate the combined result, so the output is biased toward over-represented groups and underweights the most distinct members.
ideas.approach: Assign each member of a partial result an individual weight that falls as its similarity to the other members rises and rises as its divergence grows, so near-copies contribute little and the most distinct members contribute more. Use these weights when scoring each further merge. The scoring parameters are also varied across stages according to how divergent the items being combined are.
ideas.principle: In an incremental merge of a collection, weight each constituent by how much unique information it adds relative to the rest, so that redundant clusters do not dominate the aggregate, and tune the combination rule to the spread of the inputs at each stage.

ideas.title: State-partitioned saturation from fast-slow kinetic upscaling
ideas.domain: Mesoscopic kinetic derivation of predator-prey dynamics with refuge use and cross-diffusion
ideas.problem: Macroscopic population models usually treat total density with a single fixed crowding limit, and miss how switching between internal behavioral states changes aggregate saturation when an external driver shifts occupancy.
ideas.approach: Split the population into discrete internal states, each with its own density-dependent competition, and let a slow-fast kinetic operator move mass between states. Upscaling then yields an aggregate growth law whose effective capacity depends on the driver through the redistribution of mass across states.
ideas.principle: When a conserved quantity is partitioned among internal states that saturate at different rates, an external input that shifts the partition changes the effective aggregate capacity, which can rise non-monotonically because it reduces crowding where competition is strongest.

ideas.title: Shared-anchor multi-resolution windows with per-resolution reconstruction
ideas.domain: EEG foundation models for brain-computer interfaces
ideas.problem: Multi-scale self-supervised pre-training builds scales through feature-level operations, so the link between learned features and each scale's signal content stays implicit, and when the training objective is not matched to the multi-scale inputs, some scales receive little supervision.
ideas.approach: Represent the same segment through analysis windows of different lengths that share common temporal anchor points, then attach a scale-specific reconstruction target to each window length so every resolution is supervised during pre-training.
ideas.principle: Take one signal, view it through several windows of different spans that all start from shared reference points, and give each view its own reconstruction target so that no resolution goes unsupervised and each representation maps explicitly to its own scale.

ideas.title: Total-length-minimizing greedy pair merging from a star
ideas.domain: Molecular phylogenetics (tree reconstruction from evolutionary distances)
ideas.problem: Hierarchical structure must be recovered from a matrix of pairwise distances, but simple agglomerative clustering can be biased by unequal average distances, and exact minimum-length structure search is too expensive.
ideas.approach: Start with every item attached to one central hub in a star configuration, then repeatedly join the pair whose merge minimizes total connection length, using a correction that subtracts each item's average distance to all others. Each joined pair becomes a new node whose distances to the rest are computed from the old ones, so the hierarchy and its edge lengths come out together in a fast, deterministic pass.
ideas.principle: Given pairwise dissimilarities among items, begin with all items connected to a single hub and repeatedly merge the pair that most reduces total connecting length after correcting for each item's average dissimilarity to the rest; the merged pair is replaced by a new representative whose dissimilarities are derived from the old ones, yielding a hierarchy and its lengths in one pass.

ideas.title: Timescale-routed intrinsic noise
ideas.domain: Neuromorphic spiking excitability with memristive neuron models
ideas.problem: Noise in excitable dynamical systems is usually treated as a uniform nuisance, with no guidance on where inside a multi-timescale control structure it should act or what function each placement serves.
ideas.approach: The paper splits the system's feedback into a fast excitatory pathway and a slow inhibitory pathway and shows that noise in each has a different role: noise in the fast pathway shapes the type of excitability and the sensitivity to external or internal inputs, while noise in the slow pathway generates internal stimuli that trigger stochastic events. Noise placement is therefore chosen by which function is wanted.
ideas.principle: In a loop with a fast positive feedback channel and a slow negative feedback channel, noise injected into each channel performs a different job: fast-channel noise reshapes the system's sensitivity to its inputs, and slow-channel noise produces self-generated threshold crossings that trigger discrete events.

ideas.title: Backward-search compressed index for bounded-error matching
ideas.domain: Short-read sequence alignment to a large reference
ideas.problem: Hash-table lookup of many short queries against a very large reference is slow at scale, and seed-based hashing handles gapped (insertion/deletion) matches poorly for longer queries.
ideas.approach: The reference is reordered by a reversible, compressible transform so that all of its suffixes sharing a prefix are grouped together. Each query is then matched by narrowing a contiguous index interval one symbol at a time from the query's end, and a bounded number of mismatches or gaps is handled by branching over the same narrowing steps rather than by storing every position in a table.
ideas.principle: A very large string can be rearranged into a compressed, reversibly searchable index, so that a query is located by iteratively shrinking a contiguous range one symbol at a time, and bounded errors are tolerated by branching within that same range-narrowing process.

ideas.title: Uniqueness via a coefficient-space dual process
ideas.domain: Population genetics diffusion models (Wright-Fisher processes with tournament selection)
ideas.problem: Stochastic models with nontransitive interactions lack a tractable way to establish uniqueness of their solutions or to track their dynamics.
ideas.approach: Build the forward process independently, then define a dual pure-jump process acting on the coefficients of a polynomial basis expansion, where one operator raises the expansion degree and another lowers it. The duality is used to prove uniqueness and to derive a weak differential-equation representation.
ideas.principle: A continuous-state process can be characterized by a dual jump process on the coefficients of a basis expansion, where one operation increases the coefficient degree and another decreases it. Matching the forward process to this dual, constructed separately, certifies that the solution is unique.

ideas.title: Miscible-then-dilute phase-split extraction
ideas.domain: Biochemical lipid extraction from tissue
ideas.problem: Isolating a target component from a wet, water-containing sample usually takes many separate steps, and each one risks loss, contamination, or chemical damage to the material.
ideas.approach: Choose a solvent mixture that is miscible with the sample's own water, so the whole sample becomes one homogeneous phase. Then dilute with a second solvent and water to split the system into two layers, with the target in one layer and the unwanted material in the other, so the target is recovered in a single pass.
ideas.principle: A sample is first brought into a single homogeneous phase by a composition chosen to be miscible with its internal water. Adding a diluent then forces a separation into two phases, and the target partitions cleanly into one of them, so one isolated phase yields a purified product.

ideas.title: Precomputed differentiable surrogate for reusable modules
ideas.domain: Computational neuroscience (biologically detailed cortical circuit modeling)
ideas.problem: Simulating a large network built from many repeated local subnetworks is too expensive to run the many comparisons needed to test competing structural hypotheses, and the simulations give no derivatives for analyzing stability or tracing perturbations.
ideas.approach: Simulate each small local module once in advance, fit a smooth neural-network surrogate to its input-output response, and reuse that surrogate across the full composed system. The differentiable surrogate gives fast steady-state evaluation, linear stability from its Jacobian, and a way to trace how a perturbation propagates through each pathway.
ideas.principle: A large coupled system made of repeated identical units can be evaluated quickly by replacing each unit with a precomputed, smooth learned map; the smoothness yields derivatives that expose stability and show how a disturbance routes through the couplings.

ideas.title: Ranked-list subset enrichment scoring
ideas.domain: Genomics: interpreting genome-wide gene expression profiles
ideas.problem: Measurements of thousands of individual items are noisy and individually weak, so single-item tests find little overlap between independent studies even when the underlying biology is shared.
ideas.approach: Rank all items by their measured association with the condition, then score predefined, biologically coherent sets of items by how concentrated their members are at one end of that ranking, using a running-sum statistic whose significance is assessed by permutation. Sets are tested as units rather than gene by gene.
ideas.principle: Weak, noisy per-item signals become detectable when predefined coherent subsets of items are tested as a group by whether their members collectively cluster at the extreme of a ranked list, so that reproducible group-level effects surface even when individual items disagree across studies.

ideas.title: Null-normalised functional preservation audit
ideas.domain: Connectome-scale neural network operations (compression, alignment, transport, local plasticity)
ideas.problem: Structural operations on a complex system, such as compression, cross-instance transfer, or rule-based rewriting, are often claimed to keep its function, but there is no single behaviour-based measure that separates real preservation from chance agreement.
ideas.approach: Score each operation by how much of the original input-output behaviour the transformed version reproduces, normalised against a null baseline so that chance-level agreement scores zero. Apply the same score to every stage of a multi-stage pipeline to see which stage fails and whether the failures share a cause.
ideas.principle: Judge any structural transformation of a system by how much of its observable input-output behaviour survives it, measured relative to a chance baseline, and apply the same measure at every stage of a pipeline to localise where preservation breaks.

ideas.title: Validated machine proxy for costly human labels
ideas.domain: Naturalistic neuroimaging (fMRI during movie watching)
ideas.problem: Labeling rich, dynamic content with human judgments is labor-intensive, which limits how far it can scale for linking content to measured responses.
ideas.approach: A multimodal model generates the labels at scale. Its labels are checked against human ratings and against an independent measured response, and each label family is compared by the unique predictive variance it adds in an encoding model, so the proxy is treated as a complement to human labels rather than a replacement.
ideas.principle: An expensive expert annotation step is replaced by an automated proxy, and the proxy is trusted only to the extent that it matches expert labels and predicts an independent measured outcome. Competing label families are ranked by their unique contribution to that prediction.

ideas.title: Maximal-match seeding with cluster-and-stitch alignment
ideas.domain: RNA-seq read alignment to a reference genome
ideas.problem: Aligning a long query to a large reference with gaps (such as spliced or rearranged segments) is slow and error-prone when methods rely on short fixed-length seeds or fail to handle discontinuous matches.
ideas.approach: Repeatedly find the longest exact match starting at the current position of the query, then continue from where that match ended, which yields a set of maximal anchors. Cluster the anchors by locality and stitch compatible clusters into a single alignment that allows gaps, with non-canonical or long-range jumps recognized as valid links.
ideas.principle: To align a long sequence containing discontinuities against a large indexed reference, greedily collect maximal exact anchors in sequence, group them by proximity, and chain the consistent groups into one path that tolerates breaks.

ideas.title: Out-of-sample selection of memory order in a structured forecaster
ideas.domain: Epidemiological forecasting with fractional-order SIR models
