ideas.problem: Extra memory terms added to a structured dynamical model are usually justified by in-sample fit, yet it is rarely checked whether they improve forecasts on unseen data, and their benefit may vary across settings.
ideas.approach: A latent rate is reconstructed from observed counts through the structural model, then forecast forward. The added memory parameter is chosen by rolling-origin out-of-sample error, compared against integer-order, classical, neural and ARIMA baselines across many forecast origins and settings, rather than by in-sample fit.
ideas.principle: When a model gains an extra history-dependent parameter, its value should be judged by held-out predictive error over many rolling origins, not by how well it fits the past, because the benefit can reverse across regimes.
concepts: indirect state inference from emission signature

ideas.title: Staged hierarchical decomposition of chance-driven events
ideas.domain: Ecological encounter modeling
ideas.problem: Models of chance-driven outcomes often assume uniform random mixing with a single aggregate rate, which mismatches heterogeneous real-world structure and cannot use multi-level observational data.
ideas.approach: Split the process into ordered stages (how often agents come together, what happens given a meeting, and what outcome follows from that interaction), and fit them jointly as one hierarchical Bayesian model so each stage's rate can depend on individual and context-level covariates and be informed by fine-grained tracking data.
ideas.principle: A compound event is decomposed into a chain of conditional stages, each with its own parameters that vary across units and are pooled through a shared hierarchical structure, so a single aggregate rate is replaced by estimable, context-dependent components.

ideas.title: Core-plus-extensions plugin architecture
ideas.domain: Molecular structure visualization software design
ideas.problem: Specialized analysis software is hard to extend, because outside developers must either modify a monolithic codebase or build separate tools, so new features are hard to add and share.
ideas.approach: Split the system into a small core that supplies basic services and rendering, plus independently developed extensions that add higher-level functions through a defined extension mechanism. The interface is designed so that outside developers can add features without changing the core.
ideas.principle: A minimal shared base supplies common services and a stable interface, and separately built add-on modules attach through that interface. New capabilities can then be added independently without altering the base.

ideas.title: Multi-scale conditional uncertainty of a mapping between sequences
ideas.domain: Orthography and reading research (spelling-to-sound predictability)
ideas.problem: A single aggregate score of how predictably one representation maps onto another can hide how the answer changes with the chunk size used, and totals that depend on where the chunk boundaries are placed can be mistaken for evidence of the underlying process.
ideas.approach: Measure the leftover uncertainty of the target given the source at several chunk sizes, one for each unit of segmentation, and compare systems only on matched sample sizes. Treat any sum that depends on fixed boundaries as descriptive rather than diagnostic, and state the exact identity that shows when discarding boundary information could reverse a trend.
ideas.principle: Quantify how well one symbol sequence determines another by the residual uncertainty of the target given the source, computed at several segmentation granularities. Compare systems only at equal sample size, because totals that depend on fixed segmentation boundaries can change direction when the segmentation changes.

ideas.title: Boundary-localized sink replacing well-mixed decay
ideas.domain: Indoor airborne infection transmission modelling
ideas.problem: A model that treats a diffusing quantity as uniform over a space and removes it with a single global decay rate, and that reduces the space to two dimensions, underestimates the concentration where exposure actually occurs.
ideas.approach: Extend the model to the full three-dimensional volume and replace the global decay term with a Robin boundary condition, so that loss happens only where the quantity meets the boundary surfaces, at a rate set by a flux balance.
ideas.principle: A quantity that spreads through a bounded region and is lost at its edges should be modelled with a flux condition at those edges and with the full dimension of the region. Averaging the loss over the whole volume and dropping a dimension biases the predicted level at the locations that matter most.

ideas.title: Tree-guided bipartition refinement
ideas.domain: Protein multiple sequence alignment
ideas.problem: A hierarchical merge built bottom-up fixes early local decisions, so errors made when small groups were joined cannot be corrected once the overall structure exists.
ideas.approach: Use the merge tree to pick each internal edge, split the current full solution into the two groups that edge separates, re-optimize how those two groups are arranged relative to each other while holding the rest fixed, and keep the change only if the global score improves. Repeat across edges until no split yields a gain.
ideas.principle: Given a hierarchical assembly built from pieces, repeatedly cut the whole along one edge of its hierarchy into two blocks, re-solve only the interface between the blocks, and accept the rewrite only when a global objective improves; this local, structure-guided re-partitioning corrects errors that greedy bottom-up construction cannot undo.

ideas.title: Coupled latent inference via alternating feedback
ideas.domain: Visual cortex modelling of natural image segmentation
ideas.problem: Models of sensory representation treat latent features as inferred in a single pass and ignore the time course of inference when two interdependent hidden structures, such as part-level content and how that content is grouped, must be estimated together.
ideas.approach: Infer the element-level latent variables and the grouping latent variables jointly by iterating between them, each update conditioned on the current estimate of the other, so that the inference trajectory itself produces gain changes and variability decay across iterations.
ideas.principle: Two interdependent hidden variables are estimated by alternating updates in which each is conditioned on the latest estimate of the other; the resulting iterative trajectory generates time-varying gain and shrinking variability that are organized by the inferred higher-level grouping.

ideas.title: Resample-independent-evidence consensus confidence
ideas.domain: Phylogenetic systematics (statistical confidence for inferred trees)
ideas.problem: Inferred tree structures (groupings) are reported without any measure of how much they depend on sampling noise in the underlying evidence, so their reliability is unknown.
ideas.approach: Resample the independent units of evidence with replacement while keeping the set of items being structured fixed, rebuild the structure from each replicate, and keep only the groupings that recur in a large majority (95% or more) of replicates, using a majority-rule consensus to summarise them.
ideas.principle: To attach confidence to a structure inferred from independent pieces of evidence, redraw the evidence with replacement, reconstruct the structure for each redraw, and accept only the elements that reappear in a supermajority of the reconstructions.

ideas.title: Service-coupled self-reinforcing recruitment with congestion trade-off
ideas.domain: Honeybee colony food distribution via trophallaxis
ideas.problem: Distributing a resource across many agents that must find a limited number of service points, without a central controller, risks either wasted search or crowding at the service points.
ideas.approach: Agents that have just been served linger near the service point and leave a persistent marker that draws new searchers toward it, so recruitment strengthens where service is fast. Because lingering also occupies the access point and slows service, an intermediate lingering time maximizes overall throughput, and the faster of two competing sites attracts more searchers.
ideas.principle: Completed units of work deposit a decaying attractant at their location, which draws new arrivals; the same depositing behavior occupies the access channel, so the attractant strength and the blockage it causes trade off, and the system's throughput peaks at an intermediate dwell level with no central allocator.

ideas.title: Shared anchors with instance-specific grouping and weight modulation
ideas.domain: Brain network analysis from resting-state fMRI for disease prediction
ideas.problem: Fixed group-level partitions of units wash out individual differences in community structure, while fully individualized partitions need long measurement times and cannot be compared directly across instances.
ideas.approach: Keep a shared set of anchor units with common definitions, derive discrete multiscale groupings of those anchors separately for each instance from its own signal, and adapt the shared unit weights to each instance's group context so that models are individualized yet still comparable at the population level.
ideas.principle: A fixed common set of reference elements is partitioned differently for each individual case into multi-level groups derived from that case's own data, and shared parameters are modulated by each case's grouping, so individual structure is captured while the common frame keeps cases comparable.

ideas.title: Shrinking per-item dispersion toward a pooled trend
ideas.domain: Bioinformatics, differential expression of sequencing count data
ideas.problem: When many features are each measured with very few replicates, estimates of each feature's noise level are unreliable, which makes per-feature significance tests unstable.
ideas.approach: Model each feature's count variability with an overdispersed count model, then use empirical Bayes to pull each feature's dispersion estimate toward a value pooled across all features. This borrows strength across features so that inference remains reliable even with minimal replication.
ideas.principle: Each unit's noise parameter is estimated from very little data, so it is shrunk toward a precision-weighted consensus learned from all units jointly. Shared structure across many parallel units stabilises individual estimates when each has little information.
concepts: empirical-bayes shrinkage toward a pooled trend

ideas.title: Hedged minimization across rival criteria via fragmentation
ideas.domain: Philosophy of mind and AI architecture design
ideas.problem: A system may carry an unverifiable property whose presence depends on which of several rival theories is correct, so no single design criterion can be trusted to keep it low.
ideas.approach: Choose an architecture that sits near a configuration already minimal under every candidate criterion, and break the system into parts so that no part carries the coupling the property seems to require.
ideas.principle: When a hidden quantity's definition is uncertain across rival hypotheses, minimize it robustly by moving the system toward a reference configuration that scores low under all hypotheses at once, and by partitioning the system so that no single component integrates the components the hypotheses require.

ideas.title: Empirical-Bayes variance moderation across parallel tests
ideas.domain: Gene expression differential analysis (RNA-seq and microarray statistics)
ideas.problem: When many items are each tested with only a few replicates, their individually estimated variances are unstable, which inflates false discoveries and weakens power.
ideas.approach: Each item's variance estimate is shrunk toward a prior value fitted from the pooled behaviour of all items, and the moderated statistic is then used for the test. This borrows information across the whole family to stabilise per-item inference when per-item sample sizes are small.
ideas.principle: When many parallel units each supply too few observations to estimate their own noise level reliably, pull each unit's noise estimate toward a common value learned from the whole collection, with the pull strength set by how much data each unit has, so that the resulting statistics are stable even when per-unit evidence is thin.
concepts: empirical-bayes shrinkage toward a pooled trend

ideas.title: Ablation-based joint-signature mechanism attribution
ideas.domain: Spiking neural network models of brain turbulence and neural avalanches
ideas.problem: Macroscopic summaries of a system's dynamics, such as defect counts, rates, or power-law tail fits, are often computed after coarse-graining and cannot show which micro-level mechanisms generate them.
ideas.approach: Build a generative micro-level model, convert its output to a coarse-grained field, and then selectively remove candidate mechanisms (delays, filtering, timing). Credit a mechanism only if removing it destroys several joint signatures, and compare against randomized-structure nulls that keep some signatures but lose the spatial and propagation structure.
ideas.principle: A coarse-grained observable counts as evidence for a generating mechanism only when selectively disabling each candidate mechanism removes a set of linked signatures together, and when simple null structures are shown to reproduce only the individually weaker parts of the pattern.

ideas.title: Kernel-factored sensitivity propagation
ideas.domain: Online training of leaky recurrent neural networks
ideas.problem: Exact online gradient tracking through a recurrent system with memory needs full sensitivity matrices over all parameter pairs, which is too costly in computation and memory, and existing approximations are inaccurate.
ideas.approach: Exploit the fixed exponential (leaky) memory kernel of each unit to propagate a small set of kernel gains forward in time instead of the full sensitivity tensor. The only approximation is this factorization, and the paper analyzes when it keeps gradients accurate.
ideas.principle: When a system's memory of past inputs has a known fixed decay kernel, its sensitivity to earlier parameter changes can be tracked online by propagating per-unit kernel weights rather than full pairwise sensitivity arrays, trading one controlled factorization approximation for a large reduction in cost.

ideas.title: Frozen-nonlinearity eigenvalue fixed-point construction
ideas.domain: Mathematical biology (population density models with horizontal transfer)
ideas.problem: Existence of a non-trivial self-consistent solution to a nonlinear, non-local equation is hard to establish when the linear operator is non-self-adjoint and lacks regularity, and standard positive-operator theorems do not apply in the chosen function space.
ideas.approach: Freeze the nonlinear coupling terms, solve the resulting linear eigenproblem, and tune its principal eigenvalue so that the frozen problem is consistent with the original nonlinearity. This defines a custom map whose fixed point is the desired solution, and a compactness-based fixed-point theorem (Leray-Schauder) then gives existence.
ideas.principle: For a self-consistent nonlinear system whose linear core lacks the usual positivity or regularity, fix the coupling to get a tractable linear eigenproblem, use its leading eigenvalue as a tuning knob to close the loop, and read off a fixed point of the resulting compact map.

ideas.title: Quality-flagged sub-range re-solving with reinsertion
ideas.domain: Multiple sequence alignment software for molecular biology
ideas.problem: A global solution produced in one pass can contain locally poor sections and errors that are hard to fix without redoing the whole result.
ideas.approach: Score the quality of each part of the existing solution, flag low-scoring segments or outlier elements, then select a sub-range or subset, re-solve only that portion, and splice the improved piece back into the full solution. The user can also reorder or choose subsets interactively.
ideas.principle: A large structured solution can be improved by scoring local quality, isolating the weakest contiguous region or subset, re-optimizing it independently while its boundaries stay fixed, and reinserting it into the whole, with a human able to direct which parts are revisited.

ideas.title: Size-matched rarefaction for comparing distinct-type counts
ideas.domain: Population genetics (allelic richness and private allele statistics)
ideas.problem: Counts of distinct types observed in groups of unequal size are not directly comparable, because the number of distinct types rises with sample size.
ideas.approach: Estimate the expected number of distinct types in random subsamples drawn at a common size from each group, so every group is compared at the same effective sample size. The same logic extends to counting types shared only by a chosen subset of groups.
ideas.principle: To compare how many distinct kinds appear across collections of unequal size, compute each collection's expected distinct-kind count at a fixed common subsample size, so differences reflect composition rather than size.

ideas.title: Conserved adjacency motifs for function inference
ideas.domain: Genome annotation and biological pathway databases
ideas.problem: Many components in a system have unknown function, and single-item annotation transfers poorly when each item is judged alone.
ideas.approach: Track groups of items that repeatedly appear together as short, contiguous blocks across many independent systems, store these recurring blocks as motifs, and use a match to a known motif to infer the role of an unannotated member.
ideas.principle: When items that jointly serve a function repeatedly sit side by side across many independent instances, a recurring local arrangement becomes a motif, and finding that motif in a new instance lets you infer the role of its uncharacterized parts.

ideas.title: Latency-modulated diffusion lift for timed sequences on a hierarchy
ideas.domain: Clinical assessment of verbal memory retrieval for Alzheimer's disease
ideas.problem: Timed sequences of items drawn from a branching hierarchy are hard to model because the meaning of each event's timing depends on where the item sits in the hierarchy, and standard representations treat order, delay, and category structure separately.
ideas.approach: Each timed event is lifted by running heat diffusion on the hierarchy graph for a duration set by that event's latency, so one operator yields a vector that reflects multi-scale structural position and continuous timing together. The resulting representation is shown to split into structural and temporal parts with selectivity across levels.
ideas.principle: Each timed event on a branching structure is encoded by letting a quantity spread over the graph for a duration set by that event's delay, so the resulting vector jointly captures local position at several coarseness scales and the timing itself, with the two separable in first order.

ideas.title: Calibration-free ratio from threshold-crossing offsets
ideas.domain: Real-time RT-PCR gene expression quantification
ideas.problem: Relative quantification of a target against a reference normally needs a standard curve for each run, and run-to-run variation in starting material, loading, and reaction efficiency degrades accuracy.
ideas.approach: The expression ratio is computed directly from each sample's per-cycle amplification factors and the offset between its threshold-crossing point and a control's, with control levels included in each run to normalize integrity, loading, and inter-run variation. No calibration curve is used.
ideas.principle: When two quantities grow geometrically from unknown starting amounts and cross a fixed detection threshold, the ratio of their starting amounts follows from their growth factors and the difference in crossing times relative to a within-run control, so a standard curve is unnecessary.

ideas.title: Deterministic envelope from symmetric and skew parts of a linear operator
ideas.domain: Ecology: stability and oscillation of ecosystem responses to perturbation
ideas.problem: Statistical predictions of ecosystem response from random matrix theory describe large random ensembles well but can fail for any individual finite system, leaving no guaranteed bounds on that system's short-term stability or oscillation rate.
ideas.approach: Split the linear response operator into its symmetric and skew-symmetric components and use the geometric numerical range (field of values) to bound decay and transient amplification from the symmetric part and the maximum oscillation frequency from the skew part. The bounds hold for any finite size without assuming randomness.
ideas.principle: For any linear dynamical system, a deterministic geometric envelope built from the symmetric part of the operator bounds its decay and transient growth, and the skew-symmetric part bounds its maximal rotation rate, so structural constraints on a specific system can be stated without statistical assumptions about its entries.

ideas.title: Mixed-membership latent-profile inference over independent categorical features
ideas.domain: Population genetics (population structure inference from multilocus genotypes)
ideas.problem: Individuals drawn from a mixed sample cannot be reliably assigned to their source groups when the groups are unknown in number and the observations are many weakly informative categorical markers.
ideas.approach: Model the sample as coming from K latent profiles, each defining its own probability distribution over every categorical marker, and assign each unit a probabilistic membership that can be split across several profiles. Infer the profiles, the memberships, and (when unknown) the number of profiles from the data, treating markers as conditionally independent given the profile.
ideas.principle: Each unit is a probabilistic blend of a small number of latent prototypes, and each prototype is a distribution over many conditionally independent categorical features. Prototype parameters, blend weights, and the number of prototypes are inferred jointly from the observations, so mixed units are represented without forcing a hard label.

ideas.title: Fixed-size latent codebook for variable-size interacting groups
ideas.domain: Mouse behavior foundation models from pose data
ideas.problem: Models of multi-agent behavior usually encode each agent separately, which discards interaction signal, and they hard-code the number of agents so a checkpoint cannot handle a different group size.
ideas.approach: A fixed set of learned latent slots cross-attends over the per-unit embeddings of whatever group is present, and the slots then model interactions among the units. Because the parameter count depends only on the number of latent slots, a single trained checkpoint works for any number of units without retraining.
ideas.principle: A fixed-size set of learned summary slots reads from a collection of tokens of any length and mixes information across them, so parameter count is tied to the slot count rather than the collection size, and one trained network generalizes to any collection size.
concepts: variable-cardinality set encoding via fixed latents

ideas.title: Centred smoothing window to remove detection lag
ideas.domain: Eye-movement signal classification (fixations, saccades, post-saccadic oscillations)
ideas.problem: A rule-based event detector that smooths its input with a one-sided (causal) filter reports event onsets and offsets late relative to human-labelled boundaries, and when many algorithm changes are bundled together, the source of each performance difference is unclear.
ideas.approach: Centre the smoothing filter on the current sample so its delay is removed, then attribute the performance gain by reverting each bundled change in turn and measuring agreement with the reference labels after each reversion.
ideas.principle: When a sliding smoothing window is offset to one side of the point it estimates, it adds a fixed lag that shifts every detected transition; re-centring the window cancels that lag, and isolating changes one at a time shows which ones actually move agreement with the reference.

ideas.title: Randomly switching environment modulating concurrent event streams
ideas.domain: Stochastic epidemic modelling (Markov chains)
ideas.problem: Mean-path models of event counts miss the randomness of the external conditions that drive them, so they cannot quantify the likelihood of rare, severe peaks.
ideas.approach: An unobserved random environment that switches over time scales the rates of several concurrent event streams inside one continuous-time Markov chain. The joint distribution of the stream counts and the distribution of the running maximum are then derived analytically to give tail-risk probabilities.
ideas.principle: A hidden random regime that switches over time multiplies the rates of several coupled counting processes. Risk of extreme cumulative outcomes is read from the joint distribution of the counts and the distribution of their running peak, not from the average trajectory.

ideas.title: Chain-structured constraint propagation decides feasibility
ideas.domain: Phylogenetic network algorithms (computational complexity of tree containment)
ideas.problem: Deciding whether a structure can be realized under many interacting per-item requirements is generally NP-hard, and the known tractable cases excluded the general setting of multifurcations and high-indegree junctions.
ideas.approach: Show that each requirement's feasible placements lie on a single ordered chain, so the requirements form a constraint network of width one. Local arc-consistency propagation then decides global feasibility without any search or backtracking.
ideas.principle: When each local choice must be made from options that all lie along one ordered sequence, pairwise interactions only link neighbours in that sequence, so local consistency pruning alone settles whether a global assignment exists.

ideas.title: Stationary-mean arithmetic in noisy dynamics
ideas.domain: Stochastic chemical reaction networks for molecular computation
ideas.problem: Analog computation is usually designed for deterministic dynamics, but at low copy numbers intrinsic noise dominates, so a computed value can no longer be read from a single measurement.
ideas.approach: Encode each value in the stationary mean of a noisy process and build elementary modules (identity, addition, multiplication) whose stationary means realize the arithmetic. Readout is done by repeated sampling, and the wiring of the modules is chosen to control the sampling variance, with a tree-shaped arrangement cutting variance for sums but inflating it for products.
ideas.principle: A quantity is stored in the long-run average of a randomly fluctuating system built from simple interacting units. Composing such units into different topologies changes how much sampling noise a readout accumulates, and the best topology depends on the operation being composed.

ideas.title: Single-pass fusion of multiple stream operations
ideas.domain: bioinformatics sequencing-read preprocessing (FASTQ quality control and trimming)
ideas.problem: Preprocessing a large data stream with a separate tool for each operation forces the data to be read and loaded repeatedly, which makes the pipeline slow and I/O-inefficient.
ideas.approach: Perform quality control, trimming, filtering and pruning in one traversal of the data, applying every per-item check and transformation as the item passes through, and parallelize across threads in a compiled language.
ideas.principle: When many independent per-item checks and transformations are applied in sequence to a large stream, fuse them into a single traversal so each item is loaded and handled once, rather than making a separate pass per operation.

ideas.title: Pairwise state feedback with negative coupling
ideas.domain: Evolutionary game theory on networks
ideas.problem: Models of interacting agents usually treat the rules of interaction as fixed, so they miss how the joint actions of two agents can change the shared context they interact in, and how that change feeds back on their own behavior when the interaction structure is dense or sparse.
ideas.approach: Attach a binary state to each pairwise link that the joint choices of its two endpoints update, with the state then selecting the outcome rule those endpoints face. Because the endpoint that acts well degrades its own incentive, the coupling is negative. Analyze the aggregate with a mean-field closure and a pair-level closure that tracks link states, and vary connection density to see whether the system settles at a fixed point, becomes bistable, or oscillates.
ideas.principle: Agents coupled pairwise carry a shared memory on each coupling that their joint actions write and that then changes the rule governing their own future joint outcomes; when this write-read loop is negatively signed, it yields bistability or oscillation in the aggregate, and reducing the number of couplings can remove bistability and stabilize intermediate levels.

ideas.title: Per-parameter tying across heterogeneous subsets
ideas.domain: Bayesian phylogenetic inference software
ideas.problem: Heterogeneous data types, each following its own generative process, are usually modeled separately or forced into one shared model, so there is no principled way to decide which parameters should be common and which should vary.
ideas.approach: Each subset of heterogeneous data gets its own sub-model, and the user chooses parameter by parameter whether it is shared across subsets or unique to one. This lets a single framework range from fully pooled to fully separate models.
ideas.principle: Several heterogeneous observation streams each have their own generative process, and a user-specified pattern of equality constraints decides which parameters are pooled across streams and which stay stream-specific.

ideas.title: Frozen embeddings with typed-graph context for pair prediction
ideas.domain: Protein-protein interaction prediction from sequence and multispecies networks
ideas.problem: Predicting whether two entities interact from their content features alone is hard, and the context carried by an existing relation network is either unused or mixed in without distinguishing its edge types and propagation depth.
ideas.approach: Each node keeps fixed features from a frozen pretrained encoder, and a heterogeneous graph transformer propagates information along typed edges (direct interactions, cross-network group links), so pair scores combine content with multi-type neighborhood context. Generalization is then tested separately for held-out edges and for held-out nodes absent from training edges.
ideas.principle: Pairwise relation scoring is improved by pairing fixed, pretrained item representations with message passing over a graph that has several relation types, where the number of propagation steps determines how far distant relation types can contribute; held-out-link and held-out-item evaluations are kept distinct because they test different kinds of generalization.
concepts: frozen pretrained backbone with light adapter

ideas.title: Uncertainty-gated lexicographic switching between information gathering and reward exploitation
ideas.domain: Animal active sensing and embodied exploration (hawkmoth flower probing)
ideas.problem: Exploit-only, fixed-schedule, and epsilon-greedy controllers either waste effort or act on unreliable estimates when the agent's perception is ambiguous, and non-lexicographic trade-off objectives can let reward dominate information needs.
ideas.approach: The agent computes a perceptual uncertainty estimate from its learned action-conditioned uncertainty-reduction map and uses it as a gate: when uncertainty exceeds a threshold, it strictly prioritizes information-gathering actions; otherwise it exploits reward. The gate is applied lexicographically rather than as a weighted sum of the two objectives.
ideas.principle: An agent with an internal estimate of its own uncertainty chooses between two goals by a strict priority rule: while the uncertainty estimate is above a set level, it pursues the action that most reduces that uncertainty, and only below that level does it pursue the payoff, so the choice is made by threshold ordering rather than by blending the two goals into one score.

ideas.title: Auto-generated assumption captions for computed results
ideas.domain: Molecular evolutionary genetics software
ideas.problem: Analysis tools often output numerical results without making the modelling assumptions behind them visible, so users may not understand what the results depend on.
ideas.approach: The software generates a natural-language, figure-legend-style caption for each analysis that describes the models and methods used, so the assumptions are stated alongside the results.
ideas.principle: Every computed output is shipped with an automatically generated plain-language account of the choices that produced it, so the assumptions travel with the result and are not left implicit.

ideas.title: Gradient-term attribution of enabling versus driving factors
ideas.domain: Evolutionary biology of learning and phenotypic plasticity
ideas.problem: A state observed at the end of a process cannot show whether a contributing factor drives the state's rise or only keeps it from disappearing, so end-state measurements credit the wrong causal role.
ideas.approach: Write the expected objective as a function of the state and split its gradient into separate terms: one from the external driver that creates benefit, and one from the enabling channel that appears only as a cost. The enabling factor's role is then read from which terms it enters, not from how much of the state survives.
ideas.principle: When a quantity's persistence and its push are both present in the outcome, decompose the rate of change of the objective into one term that rewards the state and another that only penalizes its removal; a factor that appears only in the penalty term enables persistence without causing change, and end-state snapshots cannot reveal this.
concepts: gradient-term attribution of enabling versus driving factors

ideas.title: Symmetry-coordinate gate-and-tuning factorisation of a discrete rule space
ideas.domain: cellular automata (life-like rule spaces)
ideas.problem: A discrete space of update rules is organised by a coarse one-dimensional parameter, which fails to show which rules can support which capabilities.
ideas.approach: Index the rule space with coordinates derived from its symmetries, including one that is odd under swapping two rule components. Treat one component as a necessary gate for the capability and the other as a tuning knob for persistence. Certify capability from the table, and estimate its realised expression only from dynamics.
ideas.principle: When a system's behaviour is fixed by a discrete specification with a two-part structure, organise the specification space with symmetry-derived coordinates. One part acts as a necessary gate on whether a capability can occur, the other tunes how it persists. Capability can be verified from the specification, while how often it is realised must be estimated by simulation.

ideas.title: Fidelity-sweep bottleneck localization
ideas.domain: Vision-language models and visual theory of mind
ideas.problem: When a system fails on a task that combines perception and reasoning, the failure is usually attributed to the reasoning component by default, so the real bottleneck can go unidentified.
ideas.approach: Hold the downstream reasoning task fixed and vary the fidelity of the input from fully unstructured to fully specified across several intermediate levels. Quantify each level by the share of the performance gap between the best and worst conditions that it closes, which reveals whether the bottleneck lies in extracting the state or in reasoning over it.
ideas.principle: To find which stage limits a composite pipeline, keep the later stage's task fixed, sweep the quality of the earlier stage's output across graded levels, and measure the fraction of the total performance gap each level recovers; a large recovery from better intermediate representations locates the bottleneck upstream.

ideas.title: Discoverable basics with scriptable expert layer
ideas.domain: Structural biology software for macromolecular model building
ideas.problem: Interactive tools for complex technical work are hard for novices to learn, yet experts need deep customization, and a single interface often fails both groups.
ideas.approach: Common tasks are made discoverable through familiar visible elements (menus, toolbars) and intuitive direct manipulation, so newcomers can learn by looking. Advanced users are then served by a second layer of customizable key bindings, extensions, and an extensive scripting interface added on top of the same tools.
ideas.principle: A system serves users of widely different skill by keeping every common action visible and directly manipulable, while layering a programmable, customizable interface over the same actions for advanced use. Both layers act on one shared set of operations, so the simple surface and the expert surface never diverge.
concepts: layered interface for novice and expert users

ideas.title: Progressive self-feeding to close the teacher-forcing gap
ideas.domain: Long-horizon forecasting of neural population activity
ideas.problem: Autoregressive predictors trained with ground-truth history (teacher forcing) are evaluated on their own outputs during rollout, so the input distribution shifts at inference and errors compound over long horizons, while standard teacher-forced metrics hide this.
ideas.approach: Train the predictor with a schedule that gradually replaces ground-truth inputs with the model's own predictions, so the decoder is progressively exposed to the inputs it will see at rollout. The approach pairs this with a memory that keeps recent predictions in full detail and compresses older ones into summaries.
ideas.principle: A sequential predictor whose training inputs are true past values but whose deployment inputs are its own outputs is trained with a growing share of self-generated inputs, so the training input distribution moves toward the deployment distribution; the history is kept at multiple resolutions, with recent items detailed and older items summarized.

ideas.title: Soft-power weighted similarity graph with eigengene module summaries
ideas.domain: Gene co-expression network analysis in bioinformatics
ideas.problem: Hard thresholding of pairwise correlations discards graded association strength, and clusters of highly correlated variables are hard to summarize and relate to external traits.
ideas.approach: Raise the absolute pairwise similarity to a soft power to form a continuous weighted graph, detect clusters of densely connected items in that graph, then summarize each cluster by its leading principal component and by its most connected member.
ideas.principle: Convert pairwise similarities into a continuously weighted network using a power transform instead of a cutoff, group densely linked elements into modules, and represent each module by one dominant latent vector and one central element so that modules can be compared with each other and with outside variables.

ideas.title: Cross-configuration component swap for attributing a behavioral gap
ideas.domain: computational cognitive neuroscience, visual working-memory models
ideas.problem: When a learned system diverges from a reference behavior, it is unclear whether the gap comes from its trained core or from the input interface it receives, so the cause of the divergence cannot be located.
ideas.approach: Train two configurations that differ only in the input interface, then transplant the trained core from one into the other and drive it with the alternate inputs. If the transplanted core reproduces the target behavior, the gap lies in the interface; if not, it lies in the core.
ideas.principle: To find which stage of a two-stage pipeline causes an output discrepancy, hold one stage fixed from one setting and feed it the other setting's upstream signal, then check whether the discrepancy follows the swapped stage or stays with the original.

ideas.title: Key-partitioned blocked interval counting
ideas.domain: Genomic read summarization (sequence read counting)
ideas.problem: Counting how many short sequence reads overlap each annotated feature is a large, memory-heavy task, and existing tools are slow and need much RAM.
ideas.approach: Partition the feature index by a coarse key (the chromosome, via hashing) and group features into blocks, then stream the query intervals through one small block index at a time, so only a bounded slice of the index is held in memory.
ideas.principle: To match many query intervals against many labeled intervals, split both sets by a coarse coordinate key and into fixed-size blocks, then process one partition at a time with a small in-memory lookup structure, so memory stays bounded and each query is only checked against nearby candidates.

ideas.title: Two-timescale local rebuild with rare anchor relocation
ideas.domain: Viral quasispecies evolution and genotype network dynamics
ideas.problem: A population of mutationally linked variants has a hierarchical structure, but it is unclear how that structure responds to selective pressure, and whether adaptation is a single process or several.
ideas.approach: Structure is modelled as a hierarchy with a dominant root. Simulations on rugged landscapes are checked against longitudinal sequencing data. The population is found to rebuild quickly around the current root, while the root itself is replaced only occasionally, when a better variant appears. This separates fast local reorganisation from slow stochastic relocation.
ideas.principle: A population of mutually linked configurations forms a rooted hierarchy around its highest-scoring member. Under changing conditions, the local arrangement is continually rebuilt around that member, while the anchor shifts only rarely, when a configuration exceeds the incumbent's score. The overall behaviour is either stasis or relocation, depending on how the environment changes.

ideas.title: Composable interval-set operators chained as streams
ideas.domain: Genomic feature comparison software (bioinformatics)
ideas.problem: Answering complex overlap questions over very large feature datasets is slow and inflexible when each query needs a bespoke, monolithic tool.
ideas.approach: Provide a small suite of single-purpose operators that each take sorted position-tagged records and emit records in the same format, so their outputs can be piped into one another and into standard UNIX commands to build multi-step queries.
ideas.principle: Complex queries over large keyed record collections can be built from a set of simple, uniform stream operators whose outputs share the input format, so that composition replaces custom monolithic programs.

ideas.title: Differential-transport destabilization of a conserved cycle
ideas.domain: Plankton ecosystem pattern formation (reaction-diffusion modelling)
ideas.problem: Spatial transport is usually assumed to stabilize a uniform equilibrium, so it is unclear how a mass-conserving multi-stage cycle can develop spatial patterns from a state that is stable without transport.
ideas.approach: Linearize the well-mixed equilibrium of a closed cycle whose components move at different rates, and find the parameter conditions where the perturbation growth rate becomes positive at some spatial wavenumber. A holding stage that delays the recycling of mass is treated as the source of the lag, and numerical simulations then check the predicted patterns.
ideas.principle: A uniform equilibrium of a mass-conserving chain of coupled compartments, stable with equal mixing, can become unstable at finite spatial scales when its compartments spread at unequal rates, provided an intermediate holding stage introduces a lag in the feedback loop.

ideas.title: Predictive model selection for learned pairwise interaction laws
ideas.domain: Collective cell migration and active matter
ideas.problem: Interaction rules that produce collective group behavior are hard to measure directly, and fitting them to local dynamics alone does not show whether the learned rules reproduce the emergent group-level behavior.
ideas.approach: Learn candidate interaction models from short-time increments of individual agent trajectories using a many-body stochastic inference framework. Choose among the candidates by how well each one predicts the emergent collective behavior of the system, then keep the minimal model that does so.
ideas.principle: Infer the local rules of a many-component stochastic system from brief transitions, then select the simplest candidate rule set according to its out-of-sample prediction of the aggregate behavior that the rules are supposed to generate.

ideas.title: Hill-climb with stochastic kicks under a stopping rule
ideas.domain: Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree inference
ideas.problem: Fast heuristic searches over a huge discrete structure space can settle in local optima, and there is no way to tell whether the best solution found is actually the best one.
ideas.approach: Repeatedly run greedy hill-climbing to a local optimum, then apply a random perturbation to jump out of it, keeping the best solution seen so far. Search stops once a run of perturbations fails to improve the best score, which ties the search effort to a fixed time budget.
ideas.principle: Alternate greedy local improvement with random bounded disruptions, retain the best-so-far state, and halt when a streak of disruptions yields no gain, so that search escapes local optima within a fixed computational budget.

ideas.title: Exposure-weighted common-shock contrast with joint instrumentation of the shared path
ideas.domain: Macroeconomic policy evaluation using cross-sectional regional data
ideas.problem: Comparing units with different exposure to a common shock estimates the dynamic effect of a treatment, but the estimate is biased when exposures correlate with shared confounders or when those confounders feed back into the treatment, so the within-system feedback is mixed into the direct effect.
ideas.approach: Instrument both the unit-level treatment and the shared confounder trajectory with proxies built by weighting a common external shock by each unit's exposure, then estimate the dynamic response per horizon by local projections. This holds the common path fixed while contrasting units, isolating the effect that excludes system-wide feedback.
ideas.principle: When many units respond to one common disturbance with heterogeneous sensitivities, the sensitivity-weighted disturbance can serve as an instrument for both the focal variable and the shared background trajectory, so that cross-unit differences identify the local effect while the common background is held fixed and system-wide feedback is excluded.

ideas.title: Sample-split double projection for estimated latent confounders
ideas.domain: Econometrics of panel data with interactive fixed effects
ideas.problem: When latent confounders are estimated from the same data used to estimate a low-dimensional effect, their estimation errors leak into the residuals and bias the effect estimate, so standard debiased machine learning gives invalid inference.
ideas.approach: Remove the contribution of every estimated latent subspace jointly with a projection that accounts for their interaction, and estimate each subspace on data partitions disjoint from those where its errors would otherwise pair with the target. Separate partitions keep the leading error components from aligning with the sample used for the final estimate.
ideas.principle: When several noisy estimated low-rank structures must be removed from a signal, estimate each one on held-out partitions and project out their combined span, so that the errors in the estimates cannot correlate with the quantity being measured.

ideas.title: Surplus-constraint specification test
ideas.domain: Econometrics of dynamic panel data (GMM estimation)
ideas.problem: A model estimated from more constraints than it has free parameters gives no direct check on whether its assumptions hold, so misspecification can go undetected.
ideas.approach: Estimate the parameters using every valid constraint available, then test whether the leftover constraints that the fitted model did not need are satisfied by the fitted residuals. A large weighted discrepancy in those surplus constraints signals that some assumption is false. The same logic is applied to a residual-based check for a specific violation.
ideas.principle: When a model is fit using more conditions than it has parameters, the surplus conditions act as a built-in test: if the model is correct, their sample averages at the fitted solution should be near zero, and a quadratic form in those averages follows a known chi-squared distribution.

ideas.title: Independence point estimate with sharp joint bounds from unlinked marginals
ideas.domain: Development economics: multidimensional poverty measurement
ideas.problem: A joint quantity that depends on how two attributes co-occur cannot be computed when each attribute is observed only in a separate data source that cannot be linked at the unit level.
ideas.approach: Report a point estimate that assumes the two attributes are independent, alongside sharp lower and upper bounds on the joint quantity taken over every joint distribution consistent with the observed marginals. The bounds show how much the conclusion depends on the unknown dependence structure.
ideas.principle: When a joint quantity is needed but only the separate marginal distributions of its components are observed, give a baseline value under independence together with the sharpest extremes attainable over all couplings compatible with those marginals, so that conclusions are reported as robust to the unobserved dependence.

ideas.title: Stationary-combination equilibrium with error-correction feedback
ideas.domain: Econometrics (time series analysis of cointegrated economic variables)
ideas.problem: Individually non-stationary quantities that drift without bound can still be tied to each other, but standard differencing discards that long-run linkage and so misrepresents their joint dynamics.
ideas.approach: Find linear combinations of the drifting quantities that are stationary and treat them as equilibrium errors. Model each quantity's change as partly driven back toward equilibrium in proportion to the current deviation, which gives a model that is both short-run and long-run consistent.
ideas.principle: When several wandering signals share a common stable relation, the residual of that relation is bounded and acts as a restoring signal that pulls each signal's motion back toward the relation, so the joint system's motion is governed by the bounded deviation.

ideas.title: Nuisance-orthogonal evaluation moment
ideas.domain: Financial risk forecast backtesting with high-dimensional estimation
ideas.problem: When the forecasting model and the evaluation target are both estimated from high-dimensional data, first-order estimation error in those nuisance components distorts the test statistic, so conventional checks overreject correct models.
ideas.approach: Build the test from a moment condition whose sensitivity to the estimated nuisance components is zero at the truth, so that first-order estimation error drops out. Estimate the nuisance parts with regularized regression and use the orthogonalized moment as the test score.
ideas.principle: A hypothesis check that relies on plug-in estimates of auxiliary quantities can be made robust by replacing its score with one whose derivative with respect to those auxiliary quantities vanishes at the true values. Then the check's size is controlled even when the auxiliary quantities are estimated flexibly from many variables.

ideas.title: Ongoing relational embedding over atomized or fully-scripted agents
ideas.domain: Economic sociology (economic action and social structure)
ideas.problem: Models of decision-making either treat actors as isolated, self-interested units or as fully determined by shared norms and categories, so they miss how ongoing relational structures shape choices.
ideas.approach: Treat each actor's choices as conditioned on the persistent network of its existing ties, and evaluate any account by whether it captures that ongoing structure, rejecting both the isolated-unit and the fixed-norm extremes.
ideas.principle: Units acting within a persistent web of pairwise links are constrained by that evolving link structure; models that either strip the links away or assume every unit's behavior is fixed by global rules both omit the mechanism that actually shapes choices.

ideas.title: Random-audit-backed self-report elicitation
ideas.domain: Economics: regulation and information institutions in network games
ideas.problem: A principal needs information about a state that only the reporting party knows, but continuous direct monitoring of that state is costly, and unverified reports are not credible.
ideas.approach: The principal offers a self-report channel backed by a committed random audit: reports are checked with a set probability, and detected misreports are penalized. Truthful reporting then becomes the rational choice, so the costly monitoring is replaced by a cheaper, sampled verification.
ideas.principle: An informed party reports a private state to an uninformed party, who commits to verifying a random subset of reports and punishing detected falsehoods. Sampled, enforceable verification makes honest reporting self-enforcing, so the private state is revealed at lower cost than full observation.

ideas.title: No-arbitrage replication pricing
ideas.domain: Financial economics: option and corporate-liability valuation
ideas.problem: A derived claim whose value depends on an uncertain common driver has no direct way to be assigned a consistent value relative to the components it is built from.
ideas.approach: Form a combination of linked components whose exposure to the common driver cancels out, so the combination is effectively risk-free. Consistency then requires the derived claim to equal the cost of that replicating combination, since any mismatch would allow a guaranteed gain with no net exposure. Complex claims are decomposed into simpler pieces, each valued this way.
ideas.principle: If a target quantity is a function of a shared random driver, a weighted mix of related quantities can cancel that driver, and any gap between the target's value and the cost of that mix would let an agent extract a sure gain; requiring the absence of such sure gains pins the target's value to the mix's cost.

ideas.title: Escapability condition for avoiding lock-in in sequential aggregation
ideas.domain: Sequential observational learning and herding in economics
ideas.problem: In sequential processes where each agent acts on private evidence plus the visible history of earlier actions, the group can lock into a uniform action that never corrects, and it is unclear which information structures prevent this for every starting belief.
ideas.approach: Require that private signals can provide arbitrarily strong evidence that any given option is currently suboptimal, so that no option is a permanent trap. A pairwise version of the same requirement, comparing only two options at a time, is shown to be enough to rule out lock-in under any full-support starting belief.
ideas.principle: In a sequential process where each participant combines a private noisy observation with a public record of past choices, the aggregate converges to the correct choice only if every possible choice can be overturned by sufficiently strong private evidence; if some choice cannot be overturned, the process can lock in on it, and a pairwise test of this property is sufficient for lock-in to fail under any generic starting state.

ideas.title: Rate-induced rent shifting in competitive slot allocation
ideas.domain: Blockchain-based exchange market microstructure
ideas.problem: When a shared resource is allocated in discrete slots, it is unclear how raising the allocation rate changes competition among bidders, who captures the surplus, and whether the resulting provision of liquidity has an optimal rate.
ideas.approach: Model the rate at which slots are allocated as a control variable. Faster allocation cuts the bidding competition each slot faces, so surplus moves from the slot allocator to the fast competing agents. Provision of the shared good then peaks at an interior rate, and beyond a threshold an active provider extracts value from passive participants, who withdraw.
ideas.principle: Speeding up the sequence of discrete allocation events reduces the competition per event, which transfers surplus from the party controlling the sequence to the fastest responders; the overall supply of the shared good is therefore non-monotone in the rate, with an interior maximum and a threshold beyond which a fast insider displaces slow passive capital.

ideas.title: Obviousness-restricted coalitional robustness
ideas.domain: Mechanism design for housing allocation (Shapley-Scarf markets)
ideas.problem: Robustness criteria either guard only against single-actor deviations or demand protection against all coordinated group deviations, and neither captures which joint deviations are realistically detectable by the participants.
ideas.approach: Define a group-level robustness condition that protects only against joint deviations whose gain is evident from the participants' immediate outcomes, making it stronger than the individual-level version and weaker than full group-level robustness. Use it to characterize a specific procedure.
ideas.principle: A guarantee against coordinated deviations is restricted to those whose benefit is self-evident from immediate local outcomes, placing the robustness level between single-actor and full-coalition requirements and yielding characterizations of a specific procedure.

ideas.title: Boundary of internal direction versus market exchange by marginal coordination cost
ideas.domain: Economic theory of the firm
ideas.problem: Economic theory treats market price coordination as the default and has no account of why some coordination is instead carried out by directed authority inside a unit.
ideas.approach: Treat each coordination link as either an external exchange, costed by search, negotiation and contracting, or an internal directive under a bounded employment-style agreement, costed by organizing overhead. Internalize a link when the cost of directing it is lower, and stop expanding the unit where the marginal cost of internal direction equals the marginal cost of the market.
ideas.principle: Agents that must coordinate can do so by decentralized signal-based exchange or by a directed hierarchy under a general agreement. Each link is internalized when the overhead of the signal-based channel exceeds the overhead of direction, so the boundary of the directed unit sits where the marginal costs of the two channels are equal.

ideas.title: Coarsening an upstream signal to protect downstream credibility
ideas.domain: Strategic communication and feedback design in organizations
ideas.problem: When a designer releases an upstream signal that also shapes later strategic messages, more informative disclosure can raise the incentive to distort those messages, so naive full disclosure may reduce overall decision quality.
ideas.approach: Choose the informativeness of the first-stage disclosure jointly with its effect on the second-stage message game, rather than maximizing first-stage information alone. The optimal policy is typically full disclosure only at extreme conditions, with partial or coarse disclosure elsewhere, and the number of distinguishable message levels can vary with the belief state.
ideas.principle: An upstream designer who reveals information shifts the incentives of a downstream sender who controls a second channel. Maximal upstream transparency can destroy the credibility of that channel, so the best policy is a graded, belief-dependent coarsening of the revealed signal.

ideas.title: Symbiotic constraint-actor feedback with perception-gated change
ideas.domain: Institutional economics
ideas.problem: Standard theory predicts that inefficient rule systems should be quickly replaced, yet many persist, so a model is needed that explains both growth and the persistence of inefficiency.
ideas.approach: Model the rule framework and the agents who act within it as a coupled pair, where each shapes the other. Agents make incremental changes to the framework only when they perceive an opportunity, and that perception depends on how complete their information is and on the mental models they use to interpret it. Shifts in relative prices supply the pressure for change, and switching costs can stop that pressure from being fully used, so the path taken depends on history.
ideas.principle: A set of shared constraints and the actors who operate within them co-evolve through mutual feedback. Change in the constraints happens only when actors recognize an opportunity, and what they recognize is limited by their information and interpretive models. Pressure from shifting external conditions is partly absorbed by the cost of changing the constraints, so the system can stay locked in a suboptimal state along a path-dependent trajectory.

ideas.title: Coarsened binary grouping of multi-level options
ideas.domain: Causal inference with instrumental variables for multi-valued treatments
ideas.problem: Many interventions have several unordered options, and analysts often merge them into a few broad clusters and treat each cluster as a single binary exposure. It is unclear what such a coarse comparison actually identifies when the assumptions hold only at the fine-grained level.
ideas.approach: Treat each broad cluster as a binary exposure and run the standard two-group comparison at that level. Show that the result recovers a weighted average of the fine-grained within-comparison effects, and where the fine-grained choices are observed, derive testable necessary conditions for reading the coarse estimate causally.
ideas.principle: Collapsing several discrete options into two super-groups and running a binary contrast yields a weighted average of the underlying pairwise contrasts. When the fine-grained choices are observed, the coarse contrast's validity can be checked with necessary consistency conditions.

ideas.title: Calibrated self-selection over risk tiers
ideas.domain: Behavioral labor economics of task-complexity choice
ideas.problem: When agents pick among options that trade a higher payoff for a lower success probability, overestimating their own odds pushes choices toward the riskiest option, so the benefits of letting agents self-select are lost to costly overreach.
ideas.approach: Keep the menu of options with differing payoff-risk tradeoffs and let agents choose, but supply information and feedback that helps each agent judge its own chance of success. The self-selection benefit is kept while the upward bias in self-assessment is reduced.
ideas.principle: An agent chooses among options that pair higher reward with lower success odds, using its own estimate of its success odds. When that estimate is biased upward, the mistakes all point toward the riskiest option. Calibrated feedback on the agent's actual success rate keeps the value of self-selection while curbing the overreach.

ideas.title: Directional decomposition of a bidirectional coupling spectrum
ideas.domain: Econometrics, time-series causality analysis
ideas.problem: When two mutually influencing variables are observed, the direction of influence and the presence of feedback are hard to determine, and apparent instantaneous influence can be an artifact of slow sampling or an incomplete set of candidate drivers.
ideas.approach: Define testable directional criteria, then split the joint frequency-domain coupling between the two signals into one part per direction of the feedback loop. From these parts, derive a lag and a strength for each direction.
ideas.principle: A symmetric coupling measure between two interacting signals, resolved across frequencies, can be partitioned into separate contributions, each attributable to one directed arm of a two-way loop. Each contribution then yields its own delay and magnitude, so directionality can be read from a symmetric joint measure.

ideas.title: Conformal widening of simulated predictive intervals
ideas.domain: Financial econometrics (volatility forecasting)
ideas.problem: Prediction intervals built by simulating a fitted model's future paths tend to undercover, especially when errors are heavy-tailed or the model is misspecified.
ideas.approach: Build multi-step intervals by resampling the model's fitted residuals forward through the simulated path, then correct undercoverage by widening the interval using quantiles of held-out nonconformity scores, so that the nominal coverage is met empirically.
ideas.principle: A predictive model's uncertainty is estimated by replaying its own fitted errors forward through time, and the resulting band is then stretched by the empirical quantile of out-of-sample misses so that the target coverage holds even when the model's assumed error law is wrong.

ideas.title: Extremal-case bracketing of test thresholds
ideas.domain: Econometrics: testing for long-run level relationships among time series with unknown integration order
ideas.problem: A test for a long-run relationship has a non-standard null distribution that depends on whether each component is stationary or non-stationary, and that classification is often unknown in advance, so a single exact critical value is not available.
ideas.approach: Compute significance thresholds for the two extreme cases, one where every component is in the first group and one where every component is in the second, and use them as lower and upper bounds. Reject when the statistic exceeds the upper bound, fail to reject when it falls below the lower bound, and treat the in-between region as inconclusive.
ideas.principle: When a test's null distribution depends on an unknown discrete classification of its nuisance components, the thresholds for the two extreme classifications bracket every possible threshold, so the test decides conclusively outside the band and is explicitly inconclusive inside it.

ideas.title: Stake-tracking test for strategic favoritism
ideas.domain: Sports judging and expert-panel favoritism
ideas.problem: When evaluators have ties to one candidate, favoritism is hard to separate from shared taste or better information, so the bias cannot be confidently attributed to strategic intent.
ideas.approach: Use a randomly assigned processing order to isolate the favoritism effect, then check whether the bias rises with the favored party's live chances of winning, appears when rivals have their own representatives among the evaluators, and disappears once the favored party is out of contention. Each of these patterns is predicted by strategy and not by honest taste.
ideas.principle: Random assignment of processing sequence identifies a bias, and a bias that tracks the beneficiary's stake and the opponents' connections to the decision group, and vanishes when the stake is gone, signals deliberate strategy rather than sincere preference.

ideas.title: Self-exciting conditional variance with fixed long-run level
ideas.domain: Econometrics: modeling time-varying variance of regression disturbances (ARCH)
ideas.problem: Standard models assume a constant one-period-ahead variance, so they cannot capture noise whose magnitude comes in bursts and clusters over time.
ideas.approach: Let the current variance of each disturbance be a linear function of the recent squared disturbances, so large shocks raise the expected size of the next shock, while the unconditional variance stays fixed. Estimate the parameters by maximum likelihood and detect the effect with a test based on the autocorrelation of the squared residuals.
ideas.principle: A noise process has a fixed long-run spread, but its instantaneous spread is an autoregressive function of its own recent squared deviations, so disturbances cluster in volatility; this clustering is detected by checking whether the squared deviations are serially correlated.

ideas.title: Nonlinear pricing rule via monotone set-function extension
ideas.domain: Cooperative game theory and asset pricing
ideas.problem: The nonemptiness of the core for infinite cooperative games lacked a unified derivation, and earlier routes required extra assumptions such as bounded variation or a sigma-algebra of coalitions.
ideas.approach: Extend a set function to simple measurable payoffs by a Choquet-type integral, so that a nonlinear pricing rule replaces a linear price. Balancedness of the collection is then read as absence of arbitrage, and a dominated linear functional yields a feasible allocation via duality.
ideas.principle: A monotone set function is extended to a nonlinear valuation on simple functions of a measurable space. Covering conditions on the family of sets become no-exploitable-combination conditions, and a dominated linear representative supplies a certificate that a feasible allocation exists.

ideas.title: Separable factorization of multi-index coefficients with robust inference
ideas.domain: Structural vector autoregressions for multidimensional panel data
ideas.problem: When data are indexed along several dimensions, the number of model coefficients grows multiplicatively, making estimation intractable and making it hard to impose the restrictions needed for identification.
ideas.approach: Constrain the full coefficient array to a Kronecker product of small factor matrices, so each dimension gets its own low-dimensional component. Estimate the factors by minimum distance, and build confidence intervals that stay valid when the exact product structure holds only approximately.
ideas.principle: A large array of coefficients over several coordinates is restricted to a separable product of small factors, so the free parameter count grows additively instead of multiplicatively and the factor structure supplies identification. Inference is then made valid under small departures from exact separability.

ideas.title: Layered assumption decomposition with a shared coordinate system
ideas.domain: Causal inference under interference (econometrics and experimental design)
ideas.problem: Estimating effects when one unit's outcome depends on others' treatments requires reducing an exponentially large set of potential outcomes, and the modeling assumptions are tangled together so their costs and validity are hard to separate.
ideas.approach: Separate the modeling assumptions into three ordered layers (which dependencies matter, how the dependencies are summarized, and what functional form the outcome takes), then decompose any outcome into orthogonal main-effect and interaction components that give one common coordinate system for nonparametric, semiparametric, and parametric models. Estimands are then split by whether they condition on fixed conditions or on an expected allocation policy, and the estimator variance is bounded by how much the dependency structure overlaps.
ideas.principle: When a system's responses depend on many interacting inputs, first state which inputs each response may depend on, then how those inputs are compressed into summaries, then the functional form; express every candidate model in one shared additive basis of separate main and interaction terms, so that estimation error can be bounded by the overlap structure of the dependencies and by the distribution of the sampling design.

ideas.title: Nonparametric variance-corrected persistence test
ideas.domain: Econometrics: unit root testing in time series regression
ideas.problem: Standard tests for whether a sequence is persistent (a random walk) assume a specific parametric dependence structure, so their null distributions break when the errors are weakly dependent or heterogeneously distributed.
ideas.approach: The test statistic is built from the raw sum-of-deviations and then corrected with a nonparametric estimate of the accumulated long-run variance, so the nuisance dependence never has to be modelled. The resulting statistic has a fixed null limit distribution across a wide class of dependence structures, and its local-alternative behaviour gives power functions for comparison.
ideas.principle: A hypothesis that a process accumulates shocks without reverting is tested by a partial-sum statistic whose variance is corrected by a kernel-estimated long-run quantity; this correction makes the null reference distribution pivotal across all weakly dependent noise models, so no noise model is specified.

ideas.title: Orthogonality-of-difference misspecification test
ideas.domain: Econometric specification testing (Hausman-style tests of model misspecification)
ideas.problem: Given a model, there is no direct check of whether its assumptions hold: a fully efficient procedure is only trustworthy if the assumptions are true, and a robust procedure is trustworthy regardless but wastes information.
ideas.approach: Compare the efficient procedure with a robust but less efficient one. Under the null that the assumptions hold, the efficient result has zero covariance with the difference between the two, so a test statistic built from that covariance (or its failure to vanish) detects misspecification without needing to estimate the alternative model.
ideas.principle: If one optimal inference under a restrictive assumption and a valid but suboptimal inference that needs no such assumption are both computed from the same data, then under the assumption the optimal result is uncorrelated with their difference; a nonzero measured correlation is a test that the assumption fails.

ideas.title: Welfare-neutral split decoupling optimum from stability
ideas.domain: Game theory of shared resource allocation under institutional asymmetry
ideas.problem: When a shared resource is divided, an aggregate objective may be indifferent to how the division is made, yet the division still determines which configuration each participant finds self-consistent, so the best aggregate outcome may not be a stable one.
ideas.approach: Separate the aggregate objective into a term that only redistributes value among participants and a term that changes total value. Then analyze the self-interested configurations under each split to see when the aggregate optimum and the stable configuration coincide or diverge.
ideas.principle: A reallocation that leaves the total unchanged can still alter each component's local gain from deviating, so the globally best configuration and the self-consistent configuration can differ even when the total objective is unaffected by the split.

ideas.title: Targeted-input leakage through shared allocation
ideas.domain: Public finance and philanthropic fiscal additionality
ideas.problem: Rules that require a targeted addition to one component of a shared pool to add to that component, rather than displace other funding, can fail when a central allocator pools the inputs and reshuffles the freed capacity. A guarantee that protects one component's baseline does not ensure its net provision.
ideas.approach: Compare each component's outcome under the pooled allocation with a reference outcome, and treat each protection as a floor on the allocator's choice. Targeted additions raise the allocator's discretionary level for every component and shrink the slack left for protection. This yields an exact feasibility test: a component's floor below its post-addition discretionary level forces a loss relative to the reference, and a Pareto-improving protection reform exists exactly when every maximal floor reaches the reference.
ideas.principle: When several sources of a shared resource are pooled and a central allocator distributes the total, an input aimed at one use lowers the constraints on every other use. A per-use guarantee holds only if its floor is at or above the level the pool would supply without the targeted input.

ideas.title: Direct-link recovery via low-rank-plus-diagonal precision estimation
ideas.domain: Macroeconomic time series and Bayesian factor modelling
ideas.problem: In a set of mutually correlated variables, raw correlation cannot tell which pairs are directly linked, and the inverse covariance needed to answer this is hard to estimate when the dependence is entangled with temporal dynamics and the number of variables is comparable to the number of observations.
ideas.approach: Jointly estimate the dynamic dependence and an innovation precision (inverse covariance) matrix constrained to a shared-factor structure, then read direct links off the fitted precision's partial correlations instead of imposing a sparsity pattern or thresholding correlations.
ideas.principle: To separate direct from indirect coupling among many correlated units, model the inverse of their joint dependence as a shared low-rank component plus individual terms, estimate it together with the temporal dynamics, and read the direct couplings from that inverse rather than from the raw correlations.

ideas.title: Nonrival partially excludable input under increasing returns
ideas.domain: Growth economics (endogenous technological change)
ideas.problem: When a reusable, non-depleting input is produced by deliberate investment, competitive pricing at marginal cost cannot cover its creation cost, so standard competitive models cannot explain how such inputs are sustained.
ideas.approach: Treat the input as nonrival but partly excludable, so each creator can protect a distinct variant with a margin. The accumulated stock of reusable inputs then feeds back to raise the rate of new creation, which is what makes sustained growth possible.
ideas.principle: A non-depleting output that its creator can partly withhold from others creates increasing returns, so pricing at marginal cost fails. The system then runs on protected differentiated margins, and the growing pool of reusable outputs feeds back to raise the rate at which new ones are made.

ideas.title: Probabilistic propagation of an expert-specified tail-event path
ideas.domain: Macroeconomic scenario analysis for central bank inflation risk
ideas.problem: Narrative stress scenarios are usually run through linear models, which cannot say how likely extreme outcomes are or how they are distributed.
ideas.approach: A hand-authored path for a rare shock is fed into a nonparametric model of the underlying system and nonlinear response equations. The output is a full predictive distribution for each downstream variable, from which summaries such as peaks and exceedance probabilities are derived.
ideas.principle: A user-specified trajectory for a rare exogenous shock is passed through a learned nonlinear response model of a coupled system, so that a narrative scenario yields a complete probability distribution over downstream outcomes instead of one linear point path.

ideas.title: Pivotality-discounted participation calculus
