ideas.domain: Rational choice theory of voting and turnout
ideas.problem: A participant's act of contributing to a large collective outcome seems to have negligible expected payoff, so a purely instrumental calculation predicts that almost no one should participate, which fails to explain observed participation.
ideas.approach: Model each contribution's value as the probability that the act is decisive multiplied by the benefit of the outcome, then subtract the cost. Because that decisiveness probability shrinks as the group grows, the net expected value is usually negative, and persistent participation must come from an added non-instrumental payoff term.
ideas.principle: When an agent's act matters only if it is decisive among many, expected net benefit is the chance of being decisive times the outcome value minus cost; this chance vanishes as the population grows, so sustained participation requires a separate payoff that does not depend on decisiveness.

ideas.title: Budget-constrained reward with state-adaptive detection accuracy
ideas.domain: Governance incentive design for cooperation in repeated social dilemmas
ideas.problem: Reward schemes for a desired behavior are often analyzed with fixed or perfect monitoring, so they miss how the reward needed, the monitoring cost, and a fixed budget interact when detection is error-prone and the current rate of the desired behavior changes over time.
ideas.approach: Fund the reward from a levy on participants' gains, and treat the reliability of identifying compliers and non-compliers as a control variable that is adjusted as a function of the currently observed rate. The required reward depends on both reliability and current rate, so the budget caps the attainable target, and adjustment policies determine how high the rate can get.
ideas.principle: A fixed-budget incentive is funded by a levy on each unit's returns and paid to units that take a desired action. The payout needed depends jointly on how reliably the action is detected and on the current prevalence of the action, so the detection effort is itself a feedback-controlled quantity. Perfect prevalence becomes infeasible under the budget, but high prevalence is reachable with the right state-dependent detection policy.

ideas.title: Data-estimated aggregation curvature
ideas.domain: Social network peer effects in microfinance adoption
ideas.problem: Models of how interacting units respond to their neighbours usually fix the combination rule for neighbour signals (average, sum, or extreme value) ex ante, so the rule is ad hoc and misspecification biases the estimated coupling strength.
ideas.approach: Replace the fixed combination rule with a single parametric family whose curvature parameter nests the mean-like and max-like rules, then estimate that curvature jointly with the coupling strength so the data select how the collective signal is formed.
ideas.principle: When a unit's response depends on an aggregate of many others' states, parameterize the aggregation operator by a curvature term that interpolates between averaging and extremal selection, and estimate that term from data rather than assuming a rule in advance.

ideas.title: Own-report locality under a shared budget
ideas.domain: Mechanism design and fair division of a fixed total under joint feasibility constraints
ideas.problem: When a fixed total must be split among symmetric participants with single-peaked preferences, it is unclear which splitting rule is the only one that is efficient, symmetric, and resistant to misreporting, especially when the feasible set is general.
ideas.approach: Require that each participant's own portion depend only on her declared best point, not on the rest of her declared report, and combine this with efficiency, symmetry, and no gain from unilateral misreporting. The full outcome is then rebuilt by an induction over the portions reachable through one participant's unilateral change and through feasible transfers between participants.
ideas.principle: When a shared total is divided among interchangeable units whose declared targets are private, requiring each unit's share to depend only on its own declared target, together with full use of the total and no benefit from misdeclaring, pins down a unique division; the division is recovered by inducting over the configurations reachable from a baseline through single-unit changes and transfers.

ideas.title: Residual-flattening test under a two-indicator proxy
ideas.domain: Empirical asset pricing (cross-sectional stock returns)
ideas.problem: A widely used risk measure appears to explain outcome variation on its own, but it is unclear whether its explanatory power comes from its own content or from being correlated with other easily measured characteristics.
ideas.approach: Split the candidate predictor into the part shared with a pair of cheap, easily measured indicators and the part unrelated to them. Test whether the residual part still relates to the outcome. The shared part carries the explanatory power, and the pair of indicators is enough to capture the cross-sectional variation.
ideas.principle: When a candidate signal is decomposed into a component shared with a simple pair of observable tags and an independent residual, the apparent link between signal and outcome sits in the shared component. If the residual shows no link, the tags alone account for the variation.

ideas.title: Surplus-resource disgorgement via binding fixed obligations
ideas.domain: Corporate finance and agency theory
ideas.problem: When an agent controls resources beyond what productive uses justify, its discretion over that surplus drives it to waste the surplus on low-return expansion, and the principal cannot easily monitor or prevent this.
ideas.approach: Replace discretionary control of the surplus with a mandatory, recurring outflow that the agent must meet. The commitment forces the surplus to leave the agent's control, which reduces the room for waste and substitutes for direct monitoring of how it is spent.
ideas.principle: An agent with discretion over unneeded surplus will misuse it, so binding it to a fixed recurring outflow that drains the surplus back to the principal limits misuse without requiring the principal to observe or police each decision.

ideas.title: Common-driver decomposition of apparent persistence
ideas.domain: Empirical finance: mutual fund performance persistence
ideas.problem: Repeated high performance by the same units over time can look like individual skill, but it may simply reflect a shared external driver that the units all happen to be exposed to.
ideas.approach: Measure the shared drivers and their exposures, then remove their contribution from the persistence. If little persistence is left in the residual, the apparent individual effect is explained by the common component. Any residual that remains is then tested separately.
ideas.principle: A consistent ranking across agents can be split into a component shared by all agents and an individual component. Removing the shared component shows whether the individual component carries any independent signal.

ideas.title: Divergence-ball worst-case duality
ideas.domain: Decision theory: rational inattention under distributional ambiguity
ideas.problem: Choosing a policy that performs well when the nominal probability model is uncertain leads to a max-min problem over an infinite-dimensional set of alternative distributions, which is generally intractable and gives no clear criterion for when robustness changes the optimal choice.
ideas.approach: Define the uncertainty set as all distributions whose phi-divergence from a nominal distribution is bounded, then apply Lagrangian duality to turn the inner worst-case minimization into a finite-dimensional concave maximization. The dual yields explicit conditions for when robustness alters the solution and reduces to a one-dimensional problem for a broad family of divergences.
ideas.principle: When an adversary may reweight a nominal distribution only within a bounded divergence ball, the worst-case expectation can be exchanged with the outer choice and dualized into a low-dimensional concave program whose multiplier controls the size of the ball.

ideas.title: Staggered-rollout separation of model effect from environmental drift
ideas.domain: Property tax assessment and housing markets
ideas.problem: A model deployed once and frozen between updates is evaluated against a moving environment, so its measured gains or harms mix its own effect with changes the environment produced during the same period.
ideas.approach: Roll the new rule out to different units in different periods, then compare outcome changes between early-updated and not-yet-updated units over the same calendar window. The difference isolates the rule's effect from drift that affects all units alike.
ideas.principle: When a fixed decision rule is applied to a system that keeps changing, its performance can only be attributed correctly by staggering the rule's adoption across independent units and differencing outcomes across adoption timing, so that common environmental shifts cancel out.

ideas.title: Incentive-aligned delegation under hidden information
ideas.domain: Organization theory and agency theory
ideas.problem: When one party delegates action to another whose goals diverge and whose effort or information cannot be fully observed, the delegate may pursue its own interests at the delegator's expense.
ideas.approach: The delegator designs a payoff schedule tied to observable outcomes so that the delegate's self-interested choices also serve the delegator's objectives. The framework is applied to cooperative problems where this structure appears, and it is paired with complementary perspectives when testing it.
ideas.principle: One party hands decision authority to another with divergent interests and private information. Tying the second party's reward to observable results makes its self-interested choices match the first party's goals, without direct monitoring of its actions.

ideas.title: Sampled-cut multistage decomposition for irreversible sequential commitment
ideas.domain: Power system generation expansion planning under uncertainty
ideas.problem: Sequential, irreversible capacity investment under correlated demand and regime-switching supply shocks cannot be optimized exactly when the scenario tree grows exponentially with the number of stages, and deterministic or single-scenario plans underestimate the cost of shortfalls.
ideas.approach: Represent the future as a Markov-modulated process and solve the multistage problem by iteratively sampling forward trajectories and building piecewise-linear cost-to-go approximations from backward passes, so each stage's commitment is chosen against a learned estimate of the value of waiting.
ideas.principle: A sequential commitment problem under Markov-switching random shocks is solved by sampling trajectories forward and adding supporting linear bounds on the future-cost function backward, so the exponentially large branching structure is never enumerated.

ideas.title: Local decomposition of a global association index
ideas.domain: Spatial statistics and exploratory geographic data analysis
ideas.problem: A single global index of association can show that units are related overall while hiding where the association is concentrated and which individual units drive the total.
ideas.approach: Write the global index as a sum of per-unit terms, each measuring how strongly one unit agrees with its neighbours. Each term then serves two purposes: it flags local clusters or hot spots, and it measures how much that unit influences the overall value, which exposes outliers.
ideas.principle: A global dependence measure that is a sum over items can be split into one local term per item. Those terms localize where the dependence sits and show how much each item pulls the total, so one quantity serves both pattern detection and influence diagnosis.

ideas.title: Cross-sectional average augmentation for removing a hidden common shock
ideas.domain: Panel econometrics: unit root testing under cross-section dependence
ideas.problem: When many coupled series share an unobserved common shock with unit-specific strengths, per-series tests are distorted, and the usual remedies require estimating those unknown strengths.
ideas.approach: Add the cross-sectional average of each series' lagged level and first differences as extra regressors in that series' own test regression. The averages proxy the shared shock, so each individual statistic becomes asymptotically free of the unknown strengths and can be averaged across series.
ideas.principle: When many coupled sequences are each tested with a local statistic, a hidden common driver can be absorbed by augmenting each sequence's own regression with the group mean of its lagged state and changes. The resulting per-sequence statistics no longer depend on the unknown coupling strengths, so they can be pooled.

ideas.title: Local-pattern conditional moment test for generative models
ideas.domain: Econometrics of network formation
ideas.problem: Parametric generative models of pairwise-interaction structure are widely used, but there are few tests of whether they are correctly specified beyond checking individual pairwise probabilities.
ideas.approach: Test the model against the frequencies of small multi-element configurations (not just single pairs), conditional on observed covariates. Compare a nonparametric local kernel estimate of each configuration's frequency with the probability the fitted model implies for it, and use a weighted integrated squared distance between the two as the test statistic, whose null distribution is derived asymptotically.
ideas.principle: A fitted generative model implies a probability for every small local configuration of its units. If it is correct, the observed frequency of each configuration within any covariate-defined stratum should match its implied probability. The mismatch, measured as a weighted integrated squared gap between a nonparametric local estimate and the model prediction, gives a test that catches misspecification invisible to single-element checks.

ideas.title: Fair-game validation of period-by-period fitted coefficients and residuals
ideas.domain: Empirical asset pricing (finance)
ideas.problem: A fitted model that claims a trade-off between payoff and exposure to risk needs a check that its estimates are not systematically wrong and that any leftover error carries no exploitable pattern.
ideas.approach: Estimate the model separately in each period across many units, then test whether the period-by-period coefficient estimates and residuals are unpredictable from information available before each period. If they are, the model is not missing a predictable structure, and the stated trade-off is taken to hold.
ideas.principle: A model fitted repeatedly across many parallel units is validated when its successive parameter estimates and errors cannot be forecast from information known beforehand, so any remaining pattern is evidence of misspecification or of an exploitable gap.

ideas.title: Marginal-contribution capped equalizing allocation
ideas.domain: Combinatorial auction design and cooperative bargaining
ideas.problem: An efficient, stable allocation of a jointly produced surplus can give the central coordinator nothing, and it is unclear how to share the surplus as equally as possible while still blocking every subgroup's objection.
ideas.approach: Restrict the stable set to individual caps: each participant may receive the central party's payoff, capped at that participant's marginal contribution to the total. The most equal stable division is the unique one that lies within these caps, which gives the central party at least an equal share without losing efficiency or stability. A sequential proposal game with exit payments to rejecters then implements this division.
ideas.principle: When a group-stability constraint defines a feasible region, the most equal point in that region is found by capping each member's share at the value that member adds to the whole. Each member's cap is the marginal gain from their inclusion, and the hub's share is limited only by those caps, so the resulting division is both fair and stable.

ideas.title: Unrestricted joint model over doubtful exclusion restrictions
ideas.domain: Macroeconomic econometrics (identification in large-scale structural models)
ideas.problem: Claimed identification of a large interrelated system depends on many zero or exclusion restrictions that are not credible, so the restricted structure's parameters cannot be taken seriously.
ideas.approach: Drop the incredible restrictions and estimate a less restricted, fully unrestricted joint model of all the interrelated measured series, then derive the quantities of interest (dynamic responses, forecasts) from that estimated system instead of from imposed structural parameters.
ideas.principle: When an inferred internal structure rests on restrictions that cannot be justified, estimate the full joint dependence among all observed quantities with minimal imposed constraints and compute the answers from that estimate, so the data rather than doubtful assumptions determine which relationships appear.

ideas.title: Normalized co-mention frequency index for a latent state
ideas.domain: Economic policy uncertainty measurement from news text
ideas.problem: A hard-to-observe latent state, such as policy-driven uncertainty, has no direct measure, and existing proxies are narrow, slow, or unvalidated over long periods.
ideas.approach: Build a time series by counting documents in a high-volume stream that jointly mention terms from several required categories (the condition, the domain, and the relevant institutional actors), normalize by total stream volume, and scale to a baseline. Validate the index with independent human coding of a sample and with its association to downstream outcomes.
ideas.principle: An unobservable intensity can be tracked by the volume-normalized rate at which a large stream of items co-mentions markers from several required categories, provided the resulting series is checked against independent human judgments and against the outcomes it should predict.

ideas.title: Threshold-triggered self-reinforcing concentration
ideas.domain: Economic geography (location of manufacturing in general equilibrium)
ideas.problem: Models that place agents across two locations with symmetric costs cannot explain why a balanced distribution can suddenly collapse into a lopsided one, or when that collapse happens.
ideas.approach: Each mobile agent chooses a site based on the current share of demand there, so a larger share attracts more agents. When the coupling parameters cross a critical boundary, the symmetric split becomes unstable and the whole population tips to one site.
ideas.principle: When each unit's choice of state is pulled toward whichever state already holds more of the population, and this pull exceeds a critical strength set by the coupling parameters, the uniform configuration loses stability and the system locks into a single concentrated state.

ideas.title: Polynomial-closed linear lifting of stochastic recursions
ideas.domain: Discrete-time stochastic volatility modelling and derivative pricing
ideas.problem: Nonlinear stochastic recursions generally lack exact, tractable formulas for multi-period moments and cross-moments, which makes them hard to analyse and fit.
ideas.approach: Choose state dynamics whose transition maps every polynomial of bounded degree to a polynomial of the same bounded degree. The expectations of a finite basis of monomials then evolve under one fixed finite-dimensional matrix, so exact statistics at any order and horizon come from a matrix power. Scaling limits of the same recursion yield continuous-time polynomial diffusions.
ideas.principle: If a stochastic state update keeps a finite set of polynomial functions closed under its transition, the expected values of those functions obey a linear recursion on a finite-dimensional vector, so all of their values at any future step follow from a matrix power of the initial vector.

ideas.title: Group-balanced reweighting with zero-mean invariance
ideas.domain: Econometrics: cluster-robust inference for Z-estimators under heterogeneous cluster sizes
ideas.problem: When an estimator pools per-unit conditions with raw counts as weights, a few very large groups can dominate the solution, so standard group-robust inference becomes unreliable.
ideas.approach: Replace raw counts with a deterministic size-adjusted weight for each group so that no group dominates. If each group's total contribution has a zero common mean, the target is unchanged by this reweighting, so identification holds. Inference then resamples whole groups with random multipliers.
ideas.principle: When a population of nested units is aggregated with weights that scale with group size, a few large groups can control the result. Replacing those weights with deterministic group-level rescalings leaves the solution unchanged whenever each group's expected contribution is zero. Uncertainty can then be assessed by resampling whole groups with random sign multipliers.
concepts: reweighting invariance under zero group moment

ideas.title: Learn-then-commit selection under sunk entry
ideas.domain: International trade and industry dynamics (heterogeneous firms)
ideas.problem: Standard aggregate models treat a population of units as one representative unit, so they cannot explain how exposure to a wider market reshuffles resources among heterogeneous units or how that reshuffling raises average performance.
ideas.approach: Each unit pays a sunk cost to enter while uncertain of its own quality, then observes its quality and chooses among tiered irreversible options: keep operating, take on a costlier expansion stage, or exit. Increasing the shared environment's openness moves resources toward higher-quality units, and the resulting reallocation raises the population average.
ideas.principle: Agents with unknown intrinsic quality make an irreversible up-front commitment, then learn their quality and choose among staged irreversible options. Expanding the shared opportunity set shifts resources toward high-quality agents, so the population mean improves without any agent changing its own quality.

ideas.title: Cross-fitted pivot inference with learned intermediates
ideas.domain: Econometrics: weak-instrument-robust inference in instrumental-variables models with machine-learned nuisances
ideas.problem: Inference that uses machine-learned intermediate functions can be biased or invalid, because the same data used to fit those functions also feeds the test statistic, and weak signal can make standard tests misleading.
ideas.approach: Fit each learned component on held-out folds and evaluate the test statistic on the other folds, pooling the per-fold terms. Build the test so that its null distribution is valid even when the signal is weak, then invert it to get confidence sets.
ideas.principle: A statistic that depends on learned intermediates stays valid when each intermediate is fitted on data disjoint from the points where it is evaluated and the per-partition terms are pooled. Its null behaviour is designed not to depend on how strong the underlying signal is, so the resulting confidence sets remain reliable across signal regimes.

ideas.title: Movement-versus-shift decomposition of a mapping
ideas.domain: Aggregate production function and technical change
ideas.problem: When an observed output changes, it is unclear whether the change comes from moving along a fixed input-output relationship or from the relationship itself shifting, so the two effects get conflated.
ideas.approach: Introduce an explicit apparatus that separates changes caused by varying inputs along a fixed mapping from changes caused by the mapping itself moving, and uses that separation to read off the nature of underlying change.
ideas.principle: An observed change in a system's output can be split into a part due to varying the arguments of a fixed mapping and a part due to the mapping itself changing; separating these two parts makes the source of change identifiable.

ideas.title: Hybrid costly verification of self-reported classes
ideas.domain: Optimal tax enforcement with self-reported data
ideas.problem: When an agent can misreport a class label that drives how it is treated, a principal who checks reports through costly channels lacks a principled rule for which reports to check, through which channel, and how far the check should reach, so differentiating by class can be undone by strategic reporting.
ideas.approach: Verify every report below one shared frontier, using either an expensive direct inspection of the underlying outcome or a cheaper check on the reported label. Within each label group, use direct inspection only up to a group-specific cutoff, and switch to label verification beyond it.
ideas.principle: A receiver faces a sender who can misreport a categorical signal, and can verify each message through one of two costly channels. The optimal rule checks all messages below a common boundary, assigns the costlier channel to a subset of categories up to category-specific limits, and uses the cheaper channel beyond those limits, so the verification budget constrains how much differentiation is achievable.

ideas.title: Trailing-rank persistence harvesting
ideas.domain: Empirical asset pricing (stock market momentum)
ideas.problem: Standard efficiency accounts imply that past relative performance carries no information about future relative performance, yet the paper observes that it does, and it is unclear whether this reflects compensation for risk or a mispricing that can be exploited.
ideas.approach: Rank units by their trailing performance, hold a long position in the top-ranked group and a short position in the bottom-ranked group over several horizons, then test whether the resulting spread survives adjustment for shared exposures and whether it fades over longer horizons.
ideas.principle: When a population of units is ordered by a past outcome measure, the ordering persists over subsequent periods; a ranking-based long-short spread captures that persistence, and it counts as a genuine anomaly only if common-exposure adjustment leaves it unexplained and its decay pattern over time is checked.

ideas.title: Mutual proxy-reinforcement lock-in with basin-boundary recovery
ideas.domain: Evolutionary game theory applied to scientific publishing and peer review
ideas.problem: When two interacting groups each adapt to cheap, visible proxy signals, the system can settle into a self-sustaining state that scores well on those signals while the underlying value quietly declines, and partial fixes do not dislodge it.
ideas.approach: Model the two groups as coupled evolutionary populations, where cheap production raises pressure on the evaluators and proxy evaluation rewards cheap production. Find the basin boundary between the proxy-locked state and the value-preserving state, and show that only a temporary intervention large enough to push the system across that boundary restores the valuable regime. Audits and rewards for verified contributions are the proposed reversal mechanism.
ideas.principle: Two coupled adaptive populations each respond to a cheap surrogate signal set by the other, so their mutual reinforcement creates a stable lock-in state whose visible output rises while hidden quality falls. Escaping requires a transient push past the separatrix between basins, since incremental corrections are absorbed back into the locked state.

ideas.title: Context-selected type dominance
ideas.domain: Behavioral economics of fairness, bargaining, and voluntary cooperation
ideas.problem: Observed behavior that looks contradictory across settings (exploiting bargaining power in markets but not in bilateral bargaining, exploiting free-riders yet sustaining cooperation when punishment is possible) lacks a single common explanation.
ideas.approach: Assume a mixed population in which some agents have a concern for equity and the rest are purely self-interested. The payoff structure of each setting then determines which type governs the equilibrium outcome, so one latent trait reproduces the different patterns.
ideas.principle: A population mixes two latent response types, one that weighs the relative payoffs of others and one that maximizes its own payoff. Which type dominates the aggregate outcome is set by the structure of the interaction, so a single hidden trait can yield opposite observed patterns in different configurations.

ideas.title: Dispersion-versus-revision decomposition of variation
ideas.domain: Electricity market price analysis
ideas.problem: Variation in a measured quantity is treated as one phenomenon, so spread across simultaneously fixed targets gets mixed up with changes in one target over time, and the causes of each are misattributed.
ideas.approach: Separate the observed variation into two components: the spread among targets that are all fixed at one decision point, which persists because the targets cannot be substituted for one another, and the revisions of each single target as new information arrives. Give each component a formal definition, decompose the total, and attribute the first to the structural constraint and the second to uncertainty.
ideas.principle: When distinct targets must be committed at one instant and cannot be exchanged after that, their differences persist as a structural spread. Any change in a single target after commitment comes only from new information. Observed variation can therefore be split into a structural spread across targets and an information-driven revision over time, and each part has its own driver.

ideas.title: Exemplar-proximity scoring in a frozen embedding space
ideas.domain: Labor economics and hiring measurement using computer vision
ideas.problem: A latent trait that is hard to quantify, such as attractiveness, is usually measured with costly human raters, hand-built features, or task-specific training, which makes measurement expensive, hard to scale, and hard to reproduce.
ideas.approach: Map each item into the embedding space of a generic pretrained model and score it by its proximity to a fixed reference set of exemplars that represent the trait at its high end. No training, labels, or raters are needed, and the score is continuous and reproducible.
ideas.principle: An unlabeled item's position on a graded dimension can be estimated as its similarity to a fixed set of exemplars, measured in a representation learned once by a general-purpose model, so the measure needs no new fitting.

ideas.title: Dependence-confined grouping for variance estimation
ideas.domain: Econometric standard errors for panel data in finance
ideas.problem: Observations arranged on a two-dimensional grid can have correlated errors along one or both axes, so naive variance estimates are biased, and the standard fixes used in different literatures give different answers without a clear account of why.
ideas.approach: Group observations into blocks along the axis where dependence is confined, so that block-level totals are approximately independent and the variance is estimated from those totals. When dependence runs along both axes, no single block partition removes it, and the competing estimators diverge.
ideas.principle: For data indexed by two coordinates, correlation that is confined to one coordinate can be absorbed by aggregating along that coordinate, and the aggregated units then support valid inference. When correlation spans both coordinates, the aggregation choices disagree and must be reconciled explicitly.

ideas.title: Poissonized linear projection for pairwise functionals
ideas.domain: Econometrics: asymptotic inference for integrated kernel-based pairwise-difference statistics
ideas.problem: Standard limit theory covers statistics that integrate a nonlinear functional over a single point, but a statistic built from pairs of points is dependent in a way that breaks those results, so its normal approximation is not available.
ideas.approach: Replace the fixed number of units with a Poisson-distributed number, which makes contributions from disjoint regions independent. Then approximate the pairwise statistic by its first-order Hájek projection, a sum of independent single-unit terms, whose variance gives a feasible normal limit.
ideas.principle: A statistic that depends on all pairs of random items can be made tractable by randomizing the item count so that disjoint parts become independent, then replacing the statistic with its best linear approximation, which is a sum of independent terms and therefore yields a normal limit.

ideas.title: Pairwise-complete recovery through shared-plus-idiosyncratic decomposition
ideas.domain: Econometrics of panel local projections with missing data
ideas.problem: Standard estimation of a regression target needs complete cases across all variables at each date, so incomplete records can make the target unidentified even when the underlying quantity is still recoverable.
ideas.approach: Split each unit's record into a shared low-dimensional component, filled in from a fully observed auxiliary set of units, and a unit-specific remainder whose covariances are estimated from whichever pairs of entries happen to be jointly observed. Combine these pieces into bias-corrected moments and a joint score, with resampling for inference.
ideas.principle: A target built from incomplete multivariate records can be recovered by modelling the entries as a shared low-rank signal plus unit-specific noise. The signal is imputed from a complete reference population, and the noise covariances are read from whatever entry pairs are jointly observed, so no full record is needed.

ideas.title: Exit-versus-voice response to decline
ideas.domain: Economic theory of organizational decline, consumer and member responses to deteriorating quality
ideas.problem: When a system deteriorates, members who are dissatisfied can leave, which removes the signal that would prompt repair, so the system has no reliable way to learn it is failing and correct itself.
ideas.approach: Treat a member's response to decline as a choice between withdrawing and speaking up from within, and model how an easy withdrawal option weakens the voice channel while loyalty to the system raises voice and delays withdrawal.
ideas.principle: When participants facing a worsening system can either detach or signal dissatisfaction from inside, an easy detachment route starves the internal feedback channel, while attachment to the system redirects effort toward repair and postpones detachment.

ideas.title: Sign-determined feasibility of trusted coordination
ideas.domain: Mediated communication in strategic games (game theory)
ideas.problem: When participants hold private information, a trusted coordinator can only steer them toward a better joint outcome if they will honestly report to it, and it is unclear in general when such coordination is feasible at all.
ideas.approach: Classify participants by whether their private parameter pushes them toward higher own choices and whether the spillover from others' choices reinforces or opposes that push. If the spillover opposes it, coordination is infeasible whatever the parameter distribution; if it reinforces it, coordination is feasible only when the most extreme private parameter lies far enough from the population average.
ideas.principle: A central recommender can move self-interested, privately informed participants off their uncoordinated outcome only when their incentive to misreport is aligned in a specific sign direction with the coupling between them, and then only if the private values are dispersed far enough from the group mean to make the honest-report constraint non-binding.

ideas.title: Rule-reversed causal ordering of linked quantities
ideas.domain: Macroeconomics of banking and monetary institutions
ideas.problem: Models that treat the causal link between two accounting-linked quantities as fixed miss that the direction of dependence can flip when the governing allocation rules change, so the same bookkeeping relation supports opposite causal stories and the system's behaviour is misread.
ideas.approach: Identify the institutional rule that decides which of two identity-linked quantities acts as the binding constraint on the other, then treat a change in that rule as reversing the direction of dependence rather than as a change in magnitude. Compare the two regimes by their ordering, not only by their parameters.
ideas.principle: Two quantities tied together by a fixed identity can each constrain the other; which one drives and which one responds is set by a gating rule in the system. Switching the rule reverses the causal ordering while leaving the identity unchanged, so regimes must be compared by their direction of dependence.

ideas.title: Representation-gated sign reversal of extra processing time
ideas.domain: Behavioral economics of prosocial choice
ideas.problem: A single average relationship between extra deliberation time and an outcome hides why the effect differs across people, so it cannot say whether more processing helps or hurts.
ideas.approach: Treat the effect of additional processing as conditional on whether the needed information is already readily represented. When it is, extra processing mainly surfaces competing considerations; when it is not, extra processing helps build the missing representation. Test this by moderating the time-outcome link with a measure of how readily that information is represented.
ideas.principle: The effect of extra processing time on an outcome depends on whether the input it works on is already available: where the input is present, extra time can surface competing costs and lower the outcome, and where it is absent, extra time can construct it and raise the outcome. The sign of the effect is therefore set by a moderator that measures the availability of the input, not by the processing itself.

ideas.title: Causal valuation of randomized interventions along unfolding trajectories
ideas.domain: AI agent evaluation and causal inference
ideas.problem: Static benchmarks cannot tell whether an intervention at a given point in a sequential process, such as a check or a correction, improves the final outcome, because its effect depends on the current context and on what happens afterward.
ideas.approach: Randomly assign interventions in logged sequential runs, then estimate the dynamic causal effect of contextual intervention policies from a comparatively small dataset. The fitted per-state effect parameters can also rank states by risk to prioritize limited audit resources.
ideas.principle: When a costly optional action is taken at each step of an unfolding sequence, its value can be recovered from a small randomized log by estimating the long-run effect of state-dependent action rules, and the same estimates yield a ranking of states by risk for allocating scarce checks.
concepts: dynamic causal effect estimation from randomized logs

ideas.title: Diagnosis-driven withdrawable scaffolding
ideas.domain: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for language models
ideas.problem: Outcome-only feedback compresses each attempt into a single score, so most of the information in a learner's experience goes unused, and hand-designed support for learning is slow to build and tied to specific domains.
ideas.approach: A frozen overseer periodically reviews the learner's recent attempt records, diagnoses the main bottleneck, and writes temporary support at two levels: general strategies shared across a class of tasks and specific hints for individual hard tasks. The support is revised as the learner improves and is removed before unaided performance is measured.
ideas.principle: A fixed overseer reads a learner's recent outcome records, identifies the dominant failure mode, and issues temporary guidance at both class and item level that is revised as the learner improves and withdrawn before unaided testing.

ideas.title: Locally managed turn allocation without a central controller
ideas.domain: Conversation analysis of turn-taking in talk
ideas.problem: Explaining how many participants keep an orderly exchange of speaking turns, with minimal overlap and gaps, without any central authority assigning who speaks next.
ideas.approach: The idea models turn-taking as a system where each participant monitors local cues for completion points and decides whether to speak next, with the rules applied by the parties themselves and adjusted to each recipient. Ordering emerges from these local decisions rather than from a scheduler.
ideas.principle: A group of independent agents can allocate a shared, single-use channel in sequence by each monitoring local transition cues and applying common rules, with no central controller and with the rules adapted to the specific receiver.

ideas.title: Contrast-set belief redistribution
ideas.domain: LLM-agent open-ended scientific discovery
ideas.problem: Evaluating a hypothesis only against its complement tells an evaluator that the hypothesis is unlikely when evidence rejects it, but not which alternative the evidence actually favors, so inquiry stalls after a rejection.
ideas.approach: Replace the single hypothesis with a set of mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive competing explanations for one question. Score each piece of evidence by how it redistributes belief across that whole set, and treat the question as resolved once belief concentrates on one alternative.
ideas.principle: Instead of testing one claim against its negation, score each observation by how it reallocates probability across a complete partition of rival outcomes, and stop when that allocation becomes concentrated on a single cell.

ideas.title: Graded threat-mitigation selection
ideas.domain: Pragmatics of polite language use across cultures
ideas.problem: The wide variety of polite utterances across languages and cultures appears to have no common explanation, so each culture's forms look like unrelated conventions.
ideas.approach: Treats the diverse forms as outputs of one shared motive: protecting a mutually recognized social self-image. The choice of mitigation is modeled as a function of a threat estimate built from a few weighted relational variables (social distance, relative power, and size of the imposition), and the available strategies are ordered from direct to maximally indirect.
ideas.principle: An agent that must perform an act threatening a mutually valued standing picks among graded mitigation options; the amount of mitigation scales with a threat estimate formed from a weighted sum of relational distance, relative status, and cost of the act, so one underlying motive yields many surface forms.

ideas.title: Observation-bounded complementary verification
ideas.domain: LLM analytics agent evaluation (enterprise)
ideas.problem: Checking whether a complex multi-step system behaved correctly is hard when the checker sees only final outputs, and no single checking method reliably finds both routine faults and adversarial ones.
ideas.approach: Compare checkers that see different information: one that reviews the full execution record, one that reviews only the final output with adversarial probing, and one that applies deterministic rules. Measure each for stability, false alarms, and missed faults. Recommend pairing the checker with the richest observation for routine validation and the adversarial probe for security, because their detected faults barely overlap.
ideas.principle: A verifier's detection quality is capped by how much of the system's internal process it can observe, and two verifiers that probe different aspects of a system catch largely disjoint faults, so combining them covers more than either alone.

ideas.title: Recursive mechanism inference with external test
ideas.domain: Mechanistic interpretability of neural networks, compared with neuroscience
ideas.problem: Local observations of a complex opaque system (units, features, circuits, population patterns) do not add up to cumulative, precise mechanistic knowledge, and the resulting mechanism claims are too vague to yield testable predictions beyond the system itself.
ideas.approach: Identify the recurring inferential bottlenecks in going from observed components to mechanism, then organize five principles into a recursive procedure: each round turns local findings into a more precise mechanistic account, which is then used to generate hypotheses that are checked against evidence outside the system.
ideas.principle: A hidden mechanism in a complex system is established by repeatedly converting local observations into a precise, checkable account whose refinement is driven by its own failures, and by requiring that the account make predictions verified by evidence from outside the system it was inferred from.

ideas.title: Operating-curve selection of cheap binary screeners
ideas.domain: Automated machine translation quality evaluation with LLM judges
ideas.problem: Low-cost automated judges used for binary triage are often configured by prompt and model choice without a principled way to compare candidates across all decision cutoffs, so a configuration may look good only at one arbitrary threshold.
ideas.approach: Choose the judge prompt and model by comparing their ROC curves, which summarize the full trade-off between catching positives and false alarms across every cutoff. The cutoff is then set afterward for the required operating point, using a cheap, customizable configuration.
ideas.principle: When a cheap scorer must make a binary keep-or-discard decision, evaluate each candidate scoring configuration by its full error trade-off curve over all cutoffs, select on that curve, and fix the threshold only after selection.

ideas.title: Frozen multi-retriever fusion with once-fitted feature reranker
ideas.domain: Text-to-SQL table retrieval over large pooled database catalogs
ideas.problem: Selecting the relevant subset of items from a large pooled catalog usually depends on generative model calls for keyword extraction and selection, which are costly, hosted, and slow.
ideas.approach: Fuse several fixed, off-the-shelf retrievers into a candidate pool, describe each candidate with many engineered features, and reorder the pool with a lightweight learned ranker that is fitted once on one collection and applied unchanged to others.
ideas.principle: A fixed set of cheap, heterogeneous scorers produces a broad candidate set; a small supervised reranker over hand-built per-candidate signals, trained once on one source, reorders that set and generalizes to unseen sources without any expensive generative step.

ideas.title: Targeted code with universal fallback
ideas.domain: Byte-level language model text encoding
ideas.problem: A single general-purpose encoding can be inefficient for some symbol subsets, and specialized encodings that improve efficiency usually fail to cover every possible input.
ideas.approach: Build a hybrid code that uses a tailored, compressive mapping for the target symbol subset and falls back to a universal general-purpose code for everything else, so coverage stays complete. Measure how much each subset benefits, which shows that gains concentrate where individual units carry the most information.
ideas.principle: A representation tuned to a target subset of symbols, with a universal code as fallback for all other symbols, keeps full coverage while concentrating efficiency gains where each unit carries high information. Where units are individually low-information, the choice of representation matters little.

ideas.title: Cost-matched allocation between precision and repeated passes
ideas.domain: Quantized small language models with option-order averaging
ideas.problem: When a fixed resource budget can be spent either on lower-precision storage or on repeated evaluation passes, it is unclear which spending is cheaper, because the two knobs consume resources measured in different units.
ideas.approach: Both knobs are converted into a single machine-independent cost unit (storage read per pass multiplied by the number of passes). Options are then compared in pairs at equal total cost, which yields a decision rule for which knob to spend on first and how much of the rest to put into repetition.
ideas.principle: Two levers that draw on different resources can be compared fairly by pricing both in one shared unit, matching them at equal total cost, and reading off which lever gives more quality per unit. The comparison depends on where the base quality level sits, so the best allocation can change at a threshold.

ideas.title: Exact path-weighted objective for sequential acceptance
ideas.domain: Large language model inference acceleration (speculative decoding)
ideas.problem: Training objectives that approximate a sequential payoff, such as the expected number of consecutive successes before the first failure, average later outcomes over the wrong distribution. The mismatch creates a covariance gap that can reverse the gradient direction.
ideas.approach: Optimize the exact expected payoff by weighting each possible continuation path by its probability of being reached under the actual selection rule, rather than by the unconditioned process. Reduce estimator variance by analytically averaging over the randomness that can be integrated out (Rao-Blackwellization).
ideas.principle: When a sequential payoff depends on which branches a stopping rule selects, a surrogate that averages later terms under the unselected distribution is biased. Weighting each path by its reach probability under the true selection rule gives an unbiased gradient of the exact objective, and conditioning out inner randomness lowers its variance.

ideas.title: Relational-structure mapping with systematicity
ideas.domain: Cognitive science of analogy (structure-mapping theory)
ideas.problem: A theory of analogy must explain how the meaning of a cross-domain comparison is derived from its parts without relying on the specific content of either domain, and must separate analogy from mere similarity or category application.
ideas.approach: Transfer only the relational structure from a base to a target by content-blind syntactic rules, and select which relations to carry over by preferring those embedded in higher-order relational systems that constrain one another.
ideas.principle: Correspondences between two structured systems are established by copying the connections between elements rather than their surface features, and the connections kept are those that sit inside the largest interlocking network of mutually constraining relations.

ideas.title: Readiness-gated overlap of sequential iterative stages
ideas.domain: Diffusion language model inference (block-wise iterative decoding)
ideas.problem: In a chain of iterative stages, each stage must wait until every element of the previous stage has converged, so the whole chain runs only as fast as its slowest element and the next stage cannot begin until then.
ideas.approach: Run the current stage and the next stage concurrently within one shared computation, and open the next stage early using an on-the-fly readiness signal from the model itself, with no extra training or tuned hyperparameters.
ideas.principle: A sequence of iterative refinement phases that each wait for their slowest component can be overlapped: the successor phase starts inside the same computational pass as soon as an internal self-consistency signal indicates it can usefully begin, removing the hard barrier between phases.

ideas.title: Mediating representational interface between micro and macro levels
ideas.domain: Critical discourse analysis and social theory
ideas.problem: Relations between large-scale power structures and small-scale text or talk are asserted but cannot be stated explicitly, because no account links the individual and the social, or the micro and macro levels, of a system.
ideas.approach: Insert an explicit intermediate layer of stored models, attitudes, and shared representations between the observable micro-level activity and the macro-level structure. Route every cross-level claim through this layer so that each link is stated and can be examined.
ideas.principle: When two levels of a multi-level system influence each other only indirectly, an explicit intermediate layer of internal state that both levels read and write makes the coupling between them specifiable and testable, rather than leaving it implicit.

ideas.title: State-replay boundary evaluation with history-conditioned checklists
ideas.domain: AI research-agent benchmarking
ideas.problem: Standalone, cleaned-up evaluations of a sequentially built system can overstate its reliability, because they ignore the accumulated history and leftover state that real follow-up requests depend on.
ideas.approach: Each evaluation item is anchored at a real intermediate step. The full accumulated state is replayed up to that boundary without cleanup, earlier decisions are summarized as background, and checklist items include requirements that depend on that history, with any valid solution credited.
ideas.principle: To judge an agent that acts step by step within an evolving process, reproduce its full accumulated state at an intermediate decision point and score it against both immediate and history-dependent requirements. Scores that omit the history-dependent requirements inflate apparent competence and hide real differences between agents.

ideas.title: Attention-gated intake conversion
ideas.domain: Second language acquisition and psychology of consciousness in input processing
ideas.problem: It is unclear whether incoming information is stored through passive exposure, whether awareness or attention is required for that storage, and whether any resulting regularities are consciously held or abstracted without awareness.
ideas.approach: Treat conversion of incoming signal into durable internal state as gated by a single awareness condition. The condition is held to be necessary and sufficient, and task demands that direct attention to the target can switch it on without the intent to learn.
ideas.principle: A stream of inputs is retained only when an internal flag marks it as salient. Passive exposure without the flag leaves no trace, and the flag can be set by the structure of the task rather than by a deliberate intention to store.

ideas.title: Moving-standard drift in absolute ratings
ideas.domain: Human evaluation of large language model chatbots
ideas.problem: Absolute ratings of an unchanged system can appear to decline over time because the raters' implicit standard rises, so the decline is wrongly read as degradation in the system.
ideas.approach: Hold the rated items fixed, track how often raters give the most negative verdict over time, and compare against the rating of a shared control or other fixed items. The drift in absolute verdicts is then separated from any change in the items themselves, while relative comparisons among items are checked to remain stable.
ideas.principle: When the judge's reference standard for a fixed object rises with the progress of its whole class, absolute scores fall even though the object has not changed. Pairwise or ranked comparisons stay stable, and a shared control reveals the drift.

ideas.title: Local-first correction precedence
ideas.domain: Conversation analysis of repair in talk-in-interaction
ideas.problem: When a communicative system detects a fault, it is unclear who should be given the first opportunity to fix it, and an external correction applied too early can disrupt the flow of the interaction.
ideas.approach: The system gives the agent that produced the fault the first opportunity to correct it. External correction is reserved for cases where the originator does not repair it, so most faults are fixed locally and cheaply.
ideas.principle: In a shared process, errors are most cheaply resolved by the component that generated them, so a corrective system should default to self-correction and invoke outside correction only when the originator fails to act.

ideas.title: Point-in-time vintage chain for leakage-free backtesting
ideas.domain: Financial text retrieval and earnings-call NLP
ideas.problem: Backtesting a model on past periods leaks information when the model was trained on data written after the evaluation date, so its historical performance overstates what could have been known at the time.
ideas.approach: Train a series of model snapshots, each restricted to data dated on or before its own yearly cutoff, and chain each snapshot to continue from the previous one. Evaluate each historical period with the snapshot whose cutoff matches that period, so every prediction uses only information available then.
ideas.principle: To evaluate a learned system at past times without look-ahead, build a sequence of versioned components each trained only on information up to its own timestamp, warm-started from the prior version, and route each evaluation point to the version that was current at that time.

ideas.title: Source-grounded recomposition for contamination-resistant evaluation
ideas.domain: LLM decision-model benchmark construction
ideas.problem: Benchmarks built from existing material let evaluated systems rely on prior exposure, so scores can reflect memorization instead of the ability to generalize.
ideas.approach: Build test items by recombining and rewriting structure from source material into fresh contexts, so the surface instances are new while the underlying decision structure is preserved. Pair this with stress-testing for long inputs, large option spaces, and interdependent constraints.
ideas.principle: To test whether a system has learned a procedure rather than stored instances, regenerate each test case by recombining the underlying relations of known material into new surface forms, and vary the complexity of those relations.

ideas.title: Reduced-cue amplification
ideas.domain: Computer-mediated communication and interpersonal relations
ideas.problem: The common assumption that a medium which strips away personal cues only weakens interpersonal connection fails to explain why some reduced-cue interactions produce impressions and relationships stronger than face-to-face contact.
ideas.approach: The idea treats cue reduction as a condition that can exceed the baseline rather than fall short of it: observers fill missing information with favorable projections, and the resulting exchanges reinforce those projections over time. It also treats the same channel as usable for either depersonalized or intensified interaction, depending on what the situation needs.
ideas.principle: Reducing the observable signals from a counterpart can intensify the relationship the observer infers, because the observer supplies missing information with favorable assumptions and an asynchronous feedback loop reinforces those assumptions until they exceed what fuller information would yield.

ideas.title: Content-preserving path certification
ideas.domain: Logical semantics of question answering and justification chains
ideas.problem: Given a question and an answer, it is unclear how to find the set of supporting facts and present them as a connected sequence, and how to verify that the connected sequence actually preserves the justification.
ideas.approach: Model the available material as a graph of partial statements in which a parent statement can express relations among its children and a preserving edge certifies that a child's content can be recovered inside its parent. Search outward from the seed elements, and treat a conclusion as justified once a path of preserving edges connects the seed to a root that covers the target; the links are then assembled along that path with per-step support checks.
ideas.principle: Partial claims form a directed graph where a node's full form contains the content of its children; starting from given seeds, a bounded search that follows only content-preserving links certifies that a target is entailed by the connected structure, and any chain of such links can be checked step by step for preservation.

ideas.title: Self-contained relational description
ideas.domain: Structural linguistics (distributional analysis of phonemes)
ideas.problem: Elements of a system are often described through external labels such as history, meaning, or function, which mixes separate sources of organization and leaves unclear whether the system is structured in any particular respect.
ideas.approach: Treat a set as structured with respect to a chosen feature, and describe every member solely by how it occurs relative to the other members. Show that this description is complete on its own, with no appeal to other features, and test for structure in each feature by investigation.
ideas.principle: A set of items can be fully characterized by the pattern of how each item appears relative to the others, and that pattern alone is enough to organize the set, so any other organizing principle can be assessed separately rather than assumed.

ideas.title: Segment-isolate-label screening pipeline
ideas.domain: Anti-corruption expert review of draft legislation (legal/regulatory text screening with LLMs)
ideas.problem: A monolithic model prompt given a whole long document with the full review methodology tends to blur which passage triggered a concern and what kind of defect it is, so flags are hard to localize, check, and trust.
ideas.approach: Split the input deterministically into discrete units, have a model judge each unit alone against a narrow criterion, assign the final defect category with fixed rules rather than free generation, and keep a human reviewer as the final check on the flags.
ideas.principle: A long artifact is cut into fixed, individually addressable units by a deterministic procedure; each unit is judged in isolation for one narrow property, its labels are mapped to outputs by explicit rules, and a human checks the resulting flags.

ideas.title: Constraint-release configuration shift
ideas.domain: Psychology of computer-mediated communication
ideas.problem: Behavior that changes sharply under a new context is often explained as the unmasking of a fixed hidden default, which hides the interacting conditions that produce the change.
ideas.approach: Treat the change as a move of the whole system into a different configuration of its components, driven by several interacting factors that each remove a constraint, rather than as the revealing of an underlying fixed state. Individual traits then modulate how strongly the shift occurs.
ideas.principle: When several conditions that each suppress a component's behavior are removed together, the system can settle into a different stable arrangement of its components; the new arrangement is a distinct configuration, not an exposed original state, and the size of the shift depends on the system's own sensitivities.

ideas.title: Sign-coded vectors with separate magnitudes, trained through the compressed form
ideas.domain: Russian sentence embedding for retrieval (NLP)
ideas.problem: High-quality contextual encoders are too costly to run on CPUs or refresh often, and naive compression of their vectors degrades retrieval quality.
ideas.approach: Each vector's direction is stored as one sign bit per coordinate and its magnitude as a separate scalar. Items are combined by averaging magnitude-scaled sign patterns, and a final contrastive training stage optimizes that exact compressed aggregation rather than the original full-precision vectors.
ideas.principle: Store a vector as a binary sign pattern plus an independent scalar magnitude, aggregate the set by averaging magnitude-weighted sign patterns, and train the objective directly on that lossy representation so the compression error is learned around rather than merely added afterward.

ideas.title: Failure-driven problem reformulation
ideas.domain: Conversation analysis (closings in conversation)
ideas.problem: A partial solution to a hard empirical problem can leave unexplained residues, and it is unclear how to turn those residues into a better-posed next question.
ideas.approach: Start from the most basic known features of the phenomenon to pose an initial problem, build a partial solution, then use the specific ways that solution fails to derive a second, more discriminating problem. Relate the two problems and state the domain where the formulation applies.
ideas.principle: Each partial solution's systematic failures become the specification of a sharper successor problem, so the sequence of problems tracks the residual structure of the phenomenon, and the scope of validity is stated at the end.

ideas.title: Analytically decomposed stagewise learning curve
ideas.domain: Transformer learning dynamics on synthetic context-free grammars
ideas.problem: Learning curves of a complex adaptive system are usually opaque, so it is unclear what internal structure is acquired at each stage of training or why.
ideas.approach: Build a controlled synthetic generative model with analytically known statistics so that each plateau or loss stage of training can be computed in closed form and tied to the acquisition of one specific hidden latent variable. Probing the internal representations then shows when and where that latent structure appears during training and across depth.
ideas.principle: A learning process that passes through discrete stages can be interpreted stage by stage when each stage's loss is analytically computable from known data statistics and each stage corresponds to one hidden latent component becoming represented. The internal organization then shows an ordered progression from shallow local cues to abstract latent content and back to refinement.

ideas.title: Clustered versus dispersed fault budget in sequential chains
ideas.domain: Autoregressive LLM reasoning under attention-head dropout
ideas.problem: Fault-tolerance studies usually compare disruptions by total amount and ignore when they occur, so it is unclear whether the same budget of disruption does different damage depending on how it is timed across a sequential process.
ideas.approach: Hold the total disruption budget fixed and compare two schedules: one that concentrates the disruption into consecutive bursts and one that spreads it uniformly across steps. Paired trials then show that the concentrated schedule causes much larger degradation.
ideas.principle: In a chain where each step conditions on the outputs of earlier steps, a fixed total perturbation does more damage when packed into consecutive steps than when spread evenly, because each local failure propagates forward and the chain has no point at which it can recover.

ideas.title: Stable thresholded sparse units with cross-level composition
ideas.domain: Interpretability of neural network internal representations
ideas.problem: A high-dimensional learned representation is hard to interpret because there is no principled definition of its basic building blocks, and no criterion for judging whether candidate blocks are faithful and reproducible.
ideas.approach: Define basic units by two criteria: fidelity (how well they reconstruct the original signal) and stability (whether they recur consistently across resampling or perturbation). Identify them with a sparse, threshold-activated decomposition, then compose the stable units across levels to recover higher-level organization.
ideas.principle: A complex system's primitive components can be defined as sparse, thresholded elements that both reconstruct the observed signal accurately and recur reliably under resampling; stacking these reliable primitives across levels reveals the system's higher-order structure.

ideas.title: Graded cluster categories replacing discrete class inventories
ideas.domain: Thematic roles in linguistic theory (proto-role theory)
ideas.problem: Discrete, hand-listed inventories of categories are ad hoc, their membership criteria are unclear, and the number of categories is open-ended.
ideas.approach: Replace the long list of discrete categories with a small number of broad cluster-concepts. Each item gets a graded degree of membership in each cluster, set by how many of that cluster's defining properties it has. Finer and coarser classes then follow automatically from these graded memberships, and the graded values can serve as defaults when the item's category is learned.
ideas.principle: Instead of a long list of primitive discrete types, use a few broad prototype dimensions. Each item's membership in each dimension is graded by the count of defining features it satisfies. Finer and coarser groupings, and default inferences, emerge from these graded counts rather than being stipulated.

ideas.title: Frozen-embedding distance as a generalization predictor
ideas.domain: Word extension and artificial word learning
ideas.problem: It is unclear how much the similarity between new items and taught examples explains how far a learned name is extended, and what the composition of the teaching examples adds beyond that similarity.
ideas.approach: Each test item's distance to the examples is measured in the feature space of a frozen, self-supervised encoder, and that distance is used to predict extension. The composition of the example set (narrow versus broad) is then tested as a separate factor that the distance does not capture.
ideas.principle: A tag applied to a set of exemplars spreads to new items in proportion to their distance from those exemplars in a fixed, pre-trained feature space, and the way the exemplar set is sampled independently controls how widely the tag spreads.

ideas.title: Repeated-input context recovery for one-way readers
ideas.domain: Hallucination-span detection in vision-language models
ideas.problem: A one-directional (causal) model reading a single copy of its input cannot use later material when it represents an earlier position, so per-position features lack the context needed for accurate labeling.
ideas.approach: Place the candidate content twice in one input and take features from the second copy, which has already seen the entire first copy. Every position then gets approximate access to context on both sides within a single forward pass, with no extra model or extra passes.
ideas.principle: A one-way sequential reader can approximate full two-sided context at every position by being shown the material twice in succession and reading features only from the second pass, which has access to the whole first pass.

ideas.title: Explicit reference point for deviation claims
ideas.domain: Critical analysis of language model bias and positionality
ideas.problem: Calling something deviant or biased is only meaningful relative to a standard, but the standard is often left silent, and where no external standard exists the claim has no stated basis at all.
ideas.approach: Require any deviation judgment to name the position it is relative to, and where no outside standard can be supplied, have the judgment declare the vantage point it is made from so it can be examined and contested.
ideas.principle: A judgment that something departs from a norm is incomplete until its reference point is named. When no external reference is available, the judgment should state its own point of view and stay open to challenge.

ideas.title: Relational category construction from contrastive positioning
ideas.domain: Sociolinguistics of identity in interaction
ideas.problem: Identity is often treated as a fixed internal property of a speaker, which fails to explain how identities are produced, negotiated, and attributed during interaction.
ideas.approach: Identity is treated as a product of interaction, built relationally through contrasts between a participant and a counterpart (similarity/difference, genuineness/artifice, authority/delegitimacy) and signaled through several overlapping cues, some intentional and some habitual, some negotiated and some imposed by observers or by wider structures.
ideas.principle: A category assigned to one party is not an intrinsic property but an emergent position defined by contrasts with a counterpart, conveyed through several overlapping signals and co-constructed by both sides, with observers' readings and wider systems contributing to the result.

ideas.title: Hidden-control audit of blinded graders
ideas.domain: LLM-judged evaluation of medical question answering
ideas.problem: Scores from automated or blinded graders are averaged and reported without evidence that the graders reliably track quality.
ideas.approach: Mix items of known quality into the blinded scoring stream without telling the graders which items they are. Check whether the graders score these controls as expected, and use that result to judge whether their scores on the unknown items can be trusted.
ideas.principle: When an evaluator's judgments on unlabeled items are hard to verify, seed the stream with items whose true quality is known and treat the evaluator's accuracy on those seeds as a measured reliability check on the rest.

ideas.title: Conserved-budget thermalization with low-state condensation
ideas.domain: Quantitative linguistics: word frequency distributions
ideas.problem: Empirical rank-frequency patterns in text (Zipf, Lorenz, Pareto-like curves) are described case by case without a single generative mechanism that explains why a large share of mass sits in the rarest categories.
ideas.approach: Model the discrete categories as units that exchange a conserved total quantity and a conserved count under effective pairwise interactions, and treat their observed frequencies as the equilibrium occupancy of a thermalized system. When the effective conserved budget is low relative to the number of units, the equilibrium condenses a macroscopic fraction of the total mass into the lowest-cost states, which predicts the observed skewed distributions.
ideas.principle: Many discrete units that randomly exchange a conserved amount while preserving their number relax to an exponential-weight equilibrium; when the conserved budget per unit is small, a finite fraction of the total weight piles into the lowest-cost level instead of spreading across levels.

ideas.title: Context-indexed variant explanation
ideas.domain: Social-semiotic functional linguistics (register and text analysis)
ideas.problem: Variation in the form of produced outputs is often described case by case, with no account of why each variant takes the shape it does or how it relates to the situation that produced it.
ideas.approach: Treat each variant of an output as explained by the external situations in which it occurs. Organization and coherence are then read as functions of the setting's position and value, while each instance remains individually unique.
ideas.principle: Structured outputs that differ in form can be explained by the external situations that select them, so each instance is unique yet its organization is systematically tied to its surrounding environment.

ideas.title: Separating executable procedure from descriptive text for patchable evolution
ideas.domain: LLM agent skill evolution
ideas.problem: Reusable knowledge stored as a single natural-language document mixes procedural logic with descriptive content, so each revision from feedback must rewrite the whole artifact, which makes it hard to maintain and evolve.
ideas.approach: Store the procedural part of the knowledge as separate executable components linked to the descriptive text, and apply feedback-driven changes as targeted patches to those components rather than full rewrites of the document.
ideas.principle: Split a stored knowledge artifact into a runnable procedural core and a descriptive layer, then revise only the core units that feedback implicates. Localized edits to a separated, executable component are easier to test, keep stable, and reuse than wholesale revisions of a mixed text.

ideas.title: Covarying-bundle latent dimension explained by function
ideas.domain: Grammatical transitivity and discourse foregrounding in language use
ideas.problem: A construct is often defined by one surface marker, which misses that its several component attributes are what make it coherent, and leaves unexplained why the construct is so prominent in the system's structure.
ideas.approach: Treat the construct as a latent dimension defined by a bundle of distinct graded attributes that co-vary across many independent instances, then explain its prominence by the functional role it plays in directing attention (high in the focal case, low in the background case).
ideas.principle: A hidden composite dimension is identified from several separate graded attributes that rise and fall together across many independent cases; its dominance in the system's organization is explained by the function it serves in allocating focus between salient and backdrop elements.

ideas.title: Single-probe source fingerprinting by aggregating weak biases
ideas.domain: Language model identity verification via numerical-choice outputs
ideas.problem: A black-box generator's identity cannot be reliably verified from one small probe, because each individual output reveals only a weak, noisy trace of its source.
ideas.approach: Ask the source to produce one long, fixed-length structured output that contains many weak choices at once, then combine the aggregate frequency profile of those choices with their local sequential patterns in a small classifier to identify the source.
ideas.principle: A single long sample from a hidden generator carries many weak, low-cost biases; pooling their overall distribution with their order-dependent structure lets one observation identify the generator, and adding more independent samples sharpens the identification.

ideas.title: Shared-prior action channel for guided learning
ideas.domain: On-policy distillation for language-model agent memory
ideas.problem: Guidance from a teacher is weak when the learner must act through an interface that neither the teacher nor the learner was trained on, because the teacher cannot advise on unfamiliar actions and the learner rarely takes the actions that the guidance is meant to shape.
ideas.approach: Route the learned behavior through a generic, pre-existing action channel that both guide and learner already handle competently, rather than a bespoke tool or protocol. This lets the guide give informative feedback and lets the learner produce enough relevant actions for that feedback to take effect.
ideas.principle: A learner improves from an external guide only when the guide understands the channel through which the learner acts and the learner uses that channel often enough; choosing a channel both already command makes the guidance both informative and frequently exercised.

ideas.title: Artifact-mediated self-regulation
ideas.domain: Sociocultural theory of second language learning
ideas.problem: Higher-order capacities are usually explained as products of individual biology alone, leaving out how shared external structures shape what an agent can do.
ideas.approach: Treat an agent's activity as mediated by externally available artifacts that the agent uses and also creates, so the artifacts become the means by which the agent regulates its own behavior. Development then happens through participation in structured shared settings, with biology as a necessary but insufficient base.
