ideas.principle: An agent's self-control is built by using externally supplied intermediary tools that it can internalize and extend, so capability grows through participation in structured shared contexts rather than from the agent's internal makeup alone.

ideas.title: Preservation objective over conformity objective
ideas.domain: Education and culturally responsive pedagogy
ideas.problem: Approaches that adapt minority practices toward a dominant standard stop at accommodation and do not ensure that the diversity of the existing community is maintained over time.
ideas.approach: Reframe the goal from making inputs relevant or responsive to a fixed reference toward actively sustaining and fostering the existing plurality of practices as the target state. The essay pairs this goal with an explicit stance that resists policies pushing toward uniformity.
ideas.principle: When a system is judged by how closely its components match one reference, its variety erodes; setting the objective as maintaining the existing variety, and treating it as the asset to protect, keeps the system heterogeneous and robust.

ideas.title: Usage-weighted unit pruning with per-module balance
ideas.domain: Mixture-of-Experts language models (neuron-level specialization and pruning)
ideas.problem: When a modular system is compressed, deciding which internal units to keep is hard because unit importance is often judged globally, which can erase capabilities that only a few modules handle and lets one module dominate the retained set.
ideas.approach: Score each unit by its activation magnitude measured under mixed-context calibration data, weighted by how often the routing mechanism sends inputs to the module that contains it. Then select units across all modules so every module and every context keeps a balanced share of retained units.
ideas.principle: Rank the components of a modular system by their contribution to each input class, weighted by how often the selector activates their module, and keep components across all modules in a balanced way so that every input class stays covered after reduction.

ideas.title: Consecutive-change anomaly scoring for latent negative states
ideas.domain: Detecting user dissatisfaction in human-AI dialogue
ideas.problem: A latent negative state that the observer does not report directly is hard to detect from absolute content, because the level of a single signal does not reliably indicate it.
ideas.approach: Score each observation by how much it departs from the immediately preceding observation, and treat large departures as anomalies. Use anomaly-detection methods on these local changes to flag the hidden state.
ideas.principle: A hidden unfavorable condition in a sequence is better revealed by the local change between consecutive elements, scored as deviation from what the immediately prior element predicts, than by the absolute value of each element.

ideas.title: Prerequisite threshold gating of an added component
ideas.domain: Bilingual education and second-language acquisition
ideas.problem: Evaluations of a new add-on resource often report uninterpretable results because they assume its effect is uniform across participants and ignore that the base competence may need to reach a critical level before the add-on helps.
ideas.approach: Model the outcome as a function of the interaction between the base competence and the added component, with a threshold below which the added component gives no benefit or even harm. Design the evaluation so that this interaction is measured rather than averaged away.
ideas.principle: A secondary input improves an outcome only after a prerequisite foundation crosses a critical level, and the size of its effect depends on that foundation's state. Studies that average over the foundation's state hide this dependence and produce inconsistent findings.

ideas.title: Exhaustive subset testing of causal group necessity
ideas.domain: Mechanistic interpretability of language models
ideas.problem: A single intervention showing that a group of components changes an outcome does not reveal how much of that group is needed, whether other groups could produce the same effect, or whether the effect generalizes beyond the tested inputs.
ideas.approach: Enumerate every subset of the candidate group and test each one under the same intervention, including replacing components with their values from other cases. Then check whether disjoint alternative subsets can each reproduce the effect, and whether the effect holds across different inputs.
ideas.principle: A component group that appears causally responsible may be redundant, with many interchangeable minimal subsets each sufficient on their own. Necessity should therefore be measured by exhaustive subset enumeration and cross-input replacement, not by one whole-group intervention.

ideas.title: Boundary-free resource pooling over a fluid repertoire
ideas.domain: Translanguaging theory of multilingual language use
ideas.problem: Modeling an agent's resources as a set of separately bounded, named subsystems misrepresents how they are actually used, because the boundaries between subsystems are dynamic and ideologically imposed, which splits the study of the agent's behavior into disconnected cognitive and social frameworks.
ideas.approach: Treat all of the agent's available resources as one dynamically pooled repertoire, drawn on flexibly within an interaction space, with the labeled subsystems treated as emergent or post hoc descriptions rather than as the basic units. Bridge the separate explanatory frameworks by locating both cognitive dispositions and social context within this single interaction-defined space.
ideas.principle: A system's resources form one continuous, context-shaped pool rather than discrete, pre-bounded compartments, so the units of analysis are defined by the interaction in which the resources are used, not by the labels assigned to the compartments.

ideas.title: On-policy dense reference distillation
ideas.domain: continual pre-training of large language models
ideas.problem: Fixed offline targets are trained with teacher forcing, so the learner never sees the states it will actually visit, and the same data can help one model while harming another.
ideas.approach: The learner generates its own trajectories at selected points, and each generated step gets a dense score from a frozen reference model. This replaces the fixed target with feedback on the learner's own behavior.
ideas.principle: A learner improves most when it is trained on the states its own policy produces and receives dense feedback on each step from a fixed reference, rather than imitating a fixed external sequence.

ideas.title: Blinded cross-generator label agreement filter
ideas.domain: Multilingual benchmark construction for typed-decision routing in text classification
ideas.problem: Labels for a generated evaluation dataset are unverified, and a test set may quietly overlap its training data, so reported scores can reflect label noise or leakage rather than real capability.
ideas.approach: Each candidate item is labeled by one generator, then re-labeled blind by a second, independent generator; only items where the two agree are kept. Test items are also checked against training items with a maximal overlap score, and the agreement rate and overlap bound are reported alongside the leaderboard.
ideas.principle: A generated labeled collection is trusted only where an independent, blinded producer reproduces the assigned label, and evaluation items are certified distinct from training items by a bounded maximal similarity score.

ideas.title: Correlated-proxy filtering inflates test scores
ideas.domain: LLM-based label validation for minimal-pair grammaticality benchmarks
ideas.problem: Automated proxy judges are cheap substitutes for costly human validation of benchmark items, but if the proxy shares failure modes with the system being evaluated, using it to filter items can silently change which items remain and make the benchmark easier for that system.
ideas.approach: Measure the proxy's filter against held-out human majorities and check whether the items it flags differ systematically from those humans accept. The check shows that the proxy removes items the evaluated systems get wrong but humans find valid, so accuracy rises more than under random removal of the same size.
ideas.principle: A filter built from a judge that shares error patterns with the system under test removes that system's hard cases selectively, so the retained test set is easier for that system than a random subset of equal size, even when the judge looks accurate on average.

ideas.title: Orthogonal-axis taxonomy with explicit separation criteria
ideas.domain: Speech act theory (pragmatics)
ideas.problem: An earlier taxonomy of communicative act types was defective because it lacked clear criteria for telling one kind apart from another, so its categories could not be reliably separated.
ideas.approach: Build the taxonomy from a small set of independent dimensions, chosen as the most important differences between instances, and define each resulting class by its position on those dimensions. Each class is then separable by explicit criteria rather than by a list of examples.
ideas.principle: Sort a set of goal-directed actions into a few kinds by fixing a small number of mutually independent axes: the purpose the action serves, the direction in which a mismatch between the action and the world is resolved, and the internal state the action presumes or expresses. Define every class by its coordinates on those axes so that membership can be decided by explicit tests.

ideas.title: Unique-anchor segmentation for aligning permuted sequences
ideas.domain: OCR post-processing and word-level alignment of text
ideas.problem: Aligning a noisy sequence to its reference fails when block-level permutations break the order, and a monotone aligner that tracks position locally loses its place after large displacements.
ideas.approach: Find elements that occur exactly once in both sequences and use them as fixed anchors. Assign the chunks between anchors to matching windows independently, so each block is aligned locally and the global order is not assumed.
ideas.principle: Two sequences that have been reordered by block moves can be realigned by fixing the items that are unique on both sides as landmarks, then solving each bounded segment between landmarks as its own small matching problem.

ideas.title: Compliance-invariant penalty from observer-side categories
ideas.domain: Language education and raciolinguistic ideology
ideas.problem: Evaluation against a standard presented as objective and neutral can keep penalizing members of a group even when they follow the standard's rules, because the judgment depends on how observers perceive the group rather than on the behavior measured.
ideas.approach: Locate the penalty in the evaluator's perception of a pre-assigned category instead of in the performance itself, and treat the reference standard as a constructed category to be exposed and denaturalized rather than a neutral yardstick.
ideas.principle: A fixed reference standard is treated as neutral, yet the penalty each member receives is set by a group label held by the evaluator, so meeting the stated criteria never removes it; the remedy is to reveal how the standard and its categories were built and to stop treating them as natural.

ideas.title: Matched random-subspace control for direction removal
ideas.domain: Interpretability of language model internal representations
ideas.problem: Removing a candidate meaningful direction from a high-dimensional representation and seeing performance drop does not show that the direction itself carries the information, since any removal of comparable size may disrupt the system.
ideas.approach: Ablate the candidate direction and, for comparison, ablate an equal-dimensional isotropic random subspace of the same size, then report the excess loss of the candidate over the random control, with multiple-comparison correction across conditions.
ideas.principle: To credit a specific direction in a high-dimensional system with an effect, compare its intervention against size-matched random directions in the same space and attribute only the excess effect beyond that generic-disruption baseline.

ideas.title: Layered design-realization feedback across parallel channels
ideas.domain: multimodal discourse and communication theory
ideas.problem: Theories of meaning-making treat one dominant channel as the carrier of meaning, which misses how several channels with different properties jointly produce a message and how the physical means of producing it shape what gets expressed.
ideas.approach: Separate the planning of intended meaning from its concrete realization in specific materials, and treat each parallel channel as contributing its own meaning that interacts with the others. Realization constraints are then allowed to feed back and revise the plan.
ideas.principle: A composite output is built from several parallel signal channels, each with its own expressive properties. Planning an abstract intent and realizing it in particular materials are distinct stages, and the constraints met in realization feed back to revise the plan.

ideas.title: Shared-projection retrieval with query-conditioned compression in a frozen dense space
ideas.domain: Retrieval-augmented language model input compression
ideas.problem: Bounded sequential input channels force lossy or irreversible compression of retrieved material, so retrieval-augmented systems trade fine-grained information for a limited budget, and bridging a query to a different representation usually requires costly paired training.
ideas.approach: Re-encode the source material into a higher-density representation from a frozen encoder, map the query into that encoder's feature space through a single projection that is shared with the compressor, retrieve by similarity in that space without contrastive training, and then distill the retrieved content into a small set of query-conditioned prefix entries via a lightweight cross-attention compressor.
ideas.principle: Retrieve from a frozen dense encoding by projecting the query into its feature space through one projection that is reused by a downstream compressor, then condense the retrieved set into a few query-specific summary slots, so that no new paired training is needed and the compression is chosen by changing the channel rather than by discarding content.

ideas.title: Recipient-driven adaptation with strategic absent-reference targeting
ideas.domain: Sociolinguistics of speech style and audience design
ideas.problem: Variation in a communicator's output within a single agent is treated as a separate phenomenon from variation across agents, and it is unclear why output changes with context, so the style dimension lacks a unifying explanation.
ideas.approach: Treat within-agent variation as a mirror of between-agent variation, with the primary recipient of the output as the main driver of adjustment and secondary observers exerting weaker effects. Distinguish responsive adjustments, triggered by a change in the situation, from initiative adjustments that deliberately redefine the situation by moving away from the recipient toward an absent reference group.
ideas.principle: An agent's output is shaped mainly by its primary recipient, with other observers contributing less. Changes can be reactive to context or proactive, deliberately reframing the context by shifting toward a group that is not present.

ideas.title: Expert-curated interpretable profile matching
ideas.domain: Stylometric attribution of early Chinese Buddhist translations
ideas.problem: Attributing an item of disputed origin usually relies on opaque trained classifiers, whose decisions scholars cannot trace back to concrete evidence, and which need task-specific training data.
ideas.approach: Build a reference profile for each candidate source from items with confirmed origin, using a fixed set of indicators chosen and vetted by domain experts. Score each disputed item by its similarity to each profile, so every attribution can be inspected feature by feature.
ideas.principle: Assign an unknown item to a source by comparing its indicator vector against profiles built from verified members of each source, using expert-vetted indicators whose individual contributions to the match can be read directly. No parameters are fitted to the disputed cases.

ideas.title: Cheap gated intervention control with shortlist-then-score and cooldown ledger
ideas.domain: LLM agent runtime design for experience reuse
ideas.problem: Reusing past experience in an agent normally requires a large model to generate a diagnosis before each retrieval, which adds inference cost, and the system can repeat the same corrective hints without limit.
ideas.approach: A lightweight control layer first uses explicit rules to shortlist relevant candidate corrections, then a small fine-tuned classifier scores those candidates instead of generating new ones. A ledger of past injections enforces cooldown and budget checks so the same correction is not repeated, and simple interface checks constrain what gets injected without dictating the full procedure.
ideas.principle: A cheap supervisory layer decides whether and which corrective signal to inject into an ongoing process: explicit filters cut a candidate pool, a small learned scorer ranks the survivors in place of costly generation, and a ledger of past injections with cooldown and budget limits prevents repetition.

ideas.title: Investment over fixed drive
ideas.domain: Second language acquisition and social identity
ideas.problem: Motivation-based accounts treat a person's effort toward a practice as a single, fixed, unidimensional drive, which cannot explain ambivalent participation or the role of unequal access to resources.
ideas.approach: Model sustained effort as an investment: a commitment whose expected returns depend on the person's multiple, shifting self-conceptions and on the power relations that control access to those returns. The construct explains reluctance and resistance as well as engagement.
ideas.principle: An agent's sustained effort toward an access-gated practice is best modeled as an investment, whose expected returns depend on several shifting self-conceptions and on unequal control over access, rather than as one fixed internal drive.

ideas.title: Empirically weighted corruption synthesis with edit-bounded correction
ideas.domain: OCR post-correction for mixed-script Uzbek text
ideas.problem: Correctors trained on synthetic noise often miss the error types that actually occur, and unconstrained corrections can introduce as many new errors as they remove.
ideas.approach: Synthetic training corruptions are sampled with weights estimated from a small set of manually classified real error events, so the generated noise matches the observed failure mix. At inference, the corrector's output is accepted only within a fixed edit-distance bound from the input, which keeps its changes conservative.
ideas.principle: Train a corrector on synthetic perturbations whose type frequencies are fitted to a small set of observed failure events, and cap how far its output may move from the input so that the net error count cannot grow.

ideas.title: Atomic interface swap with self-generated recovery
ideas.domain: Subword-to-byte tokenization conversion of a trained language model
ideas.problem: A trained system's coarse input/output units fragment fine-grained content and hide the internal structure that the system would need to work with directly.
ideas.approach: Replace the coarse interface with the smallest atomic units the system already encodes, shrink the interface to just those units, and leave all internal parameters untouched. Recover lost ability by continuing training on supervision the original system generates itself, first on the new encoding and then on general content.
ideas.principle: A fixed internal computation can be re-exposed through a finer, lower-level alphabet by replacing only its boundary mapping. Its original behavior is then restored by training on examples the unmodified system produces for itself.

ideas.title: Apparent-time inference from age cohorts in a single snapshot
ideas.domain: Sociolinguistics of New York City English
ideas.problem: Tracking how a variable changes over time usually requires longitudinal data, which is costly or unavailable when only one snapshot of a population exists.
ideas.approach: Sample members of different ages at one moment and read the differences between age cohorts as a time series, so that each cohort stands in for the state the population was in when that cohort was formed. Change in the variable is then inferred from the cross-cohort gradient.
ideas.principle: A single cross-section of a population whose members were formed at different times can encode its own history: each subgroup's state records the conditions at its formation, so the gradient across subgroups reconstructs the trajectory of change.

ideas.title: Supply precomputed joint relations, not isolated attributes
ideas.domain: Language-model systems for rule-governed calendrical and chart reasoning (Chinese sexagenary system, BaZi analysis)
ideas.problem: A reasoner paired with a deterministic supporting component fails when the answer requires combining several attributes under a rule, and it is unclear which information that component should supply.
ideas.approach: Have the deterministic component compute the interactions among attributes (the combined relations), and filter that list to the items relevant to the query, instead of handing over the individual attribute values. Measuring error by the kind of combination required shows that giving attributes alone leaves accuracy near zero, while giving computed relations restores it.
ideas.principle: When an answer depends on a rule that combines several independent properties of the same items, a helper should return the precomputed combinations relevant to the question rather than the raw properties, because the combining step, not the property lookup, is where the reasoner fails.

ideas.title: State-Conditional Invariance for evaluator reliability
ideas.domain: Vision-language model evaluation for embodied tasks
ideas.problem: Aggregate accuracy or consistency cannot show whether an automated evaluator changes its output for the right reason, so a high score can hide reliance on superficial cues.
ideas.approach: Require the evaluator to stay stable under meaning-preserving changes to how the input is presented, and to respond when an intervention actually changes the underlying outcome. Test both with paired variants and report stability and causal sensitivity alongside correctness.
ideas.principle: A scorer is reliable only if its output is invariant to transformations that leave the hidden state unchanged and varies with interventions that do change that state; correctness, invariance, and sensitivity should be reported together rather than collapsed into one number.

ideas.title: Productive multi-part pattern templates with their own interpretation
ideas.domain: Syntax and semantics of English grammatical constructions
ideas.problem: Explanatory models built only from single-unit combination rules miss that larger, multi-part patterns can be productive, structured, and carry their own meaning that is not derivable from their parts alone.
ideas.approach: Treat an extended multi-element configuration as a unit that is directly paired with its own interpretation rule, so that meaning is attached to the whole pattern as well as to its components. The pairing is productive and rule-governed rather than a list of frozen exceptions.
ideas.principle: Meaning can be attached to whole multi-element templates, not only to single elements and their combination rules, and such templates can be systematic, extensible, and worth formal study rather than being dismissed as marginal exceptions.

ideas.title: Learned meta-aggregator over disagreeing evaluators
ideas.domain: Financial reporting compliance verification (IFRS auditing with LLM annotators)
ideas.problem: Majority voting or naive averaging over several models or annotators can fall below the best individual evaluator, because each evaluator carries systematic biases that the aggregation does not correct.
ideas.approach: Train a gradient-boosted meta-classifier that takes each evaluator's output probabilities together with frozen content embeddings of the item, using unanimous-consensus items as cheap labels and human-adjudicated disagreement items as the hard training set. Its hyperparameters are tuned by a sequential Bayesian search.
ideas.principle: When several imperfect scorers disagree, learn a combiner that conditions on both their confidence signals and the item's own content, rather than voting, and fit it mainly on the cases where the scorers conflict.

ideas.title: Self-baselined bounded gain control
ideas.domain: Inference-time safety defense for large language models
ideas.problem: Intervening on a system's internal signal needs a fixed target or reference, but a single global threshold or predefined target cannot account for per-input variation, so benign inputs get over-corrected.
ideas.approach: Measure the signal's deviation against the same input's own early baseline, normalize that deviation by its typical scale, accumulate it over time to capture persistence, and use the result to set a bounded gain that scales the system's own internal updates instead of pushing toward a predefined target.
ideas.principle: A controller judges a running signal against the baseline it recorded from the same episode, normalizes the deviation, accumulates it over time, and maps it to a bounded corrective gain applied to the system's own outputs, so no fixed external target is needed and inactive cases stay near unchanged.

ideas.title: Graded control ladder
ideas.domain: Urban planning and public participation policy
ideas.problem: Debate over shared decision-making is conducted in vague, loaded terms, so it is unclear how much real authority each party holds.
ideas.approach: Arrange the possible degrees of one party's decision authority into an ordered ladder, where each rung is defined by how much of the outcome that party actually determines. Lower rungs are tokenistic forms of involvement and higher rungs are increasing transfers of control.
ideas.principle: Ordering the forms of a shared decision by how much of the outcome each participant controls turns a fuzzy debate about involvement into a graded scale that can be compared and argued about precisely.

ideas.title: Complex-number encoding of memory and handedness
ideas.domain: Active chiral particle transport and lattice random walks
ideas.problem: Stochastic processes with memory and a directional bias are described by many interacting microscopic parameters, which obscures how each one controls the symmetric and antisymmetric (handedness-driven) behaviour of the process.
ideas.approach: Pack the two memory-related couplings, one for retention of the current state and one for a preferred sense of rotation, into a single complex parameter. Closed-form moments and correlations are then read off from this one number, with its real part giving the symmetric response and its imaginary part the odd response.
ideas.principle: A sequential process whose state is retained with some strength and whose transitions carry a preferred cyclic sense can be summarized by one complex number. Its real part sets the symmetric, even response and its imaginary part sets the antisymmetric, odd response, and all higher-order statistics follow in closed form from powers of that number.

ideas.title: Winner-among-attrited-racers statistics
ideas.domain: Stochastic first-passage of many independent random walkers under a killing field
ideas.problem: The statistics of the first agent to reach a goal among many competing independent agents are usually analysed without accounting for attrition, so it is unclear how a hazard that removes agents along the way changes the winner's arrival time, the exit location, and the population still present when the first arrival occurs.
ideas.approach: Model each competitor's path with a time-dependent flux and an attrition term, then derive asymptotic formulas for the earliest arrival in the large-population limit and for the number of survivors at the moment the first arrival occurs. Compare how these two quantities respond to the attrition strength, and use an optimal-control argument to identify where the fastest survivors concentrate.
ideas.principle: In a race of many identical independent contestants where each contestant can be eliminated at a rate that depends on location, the time of the first finisher and the number of contestants still alive at that moment respond to the elimination hazard in different ways, so redundancy can protect one statistic while leaving another unchanged or even reversing its sensitivity.

ideas.title: Signed memory-time control of transient deviation from baseline
ideas.domain: Nonequilibrium quasiparticle transport in condensed matter
ideas.problem: For a carrier that spreads through a dissipative environment, it is unclear what decides whether its transient motion is slower or faster than the standard baseline, and how large that departure is.
ideas.approach: Treat the environment's influence as a memory kernel with a single signed timescale. The sign of that timescale sets whether the transient departs from the baseline in one direction or the other, and its magnitude sets the strength; setting it to zero recovers the baseline with no lag. The sign is changed by tuning how closely the environment's frequencies match the carrier's natural spectrum.
ideas.principle: A process whose past influence is weighted by a memory timescale that can take either sign produces transient deviation from its baseline whose direction flips with the sign of that timescale, and whose strength scales with its magnitude. When the memory timescale vanishes, the process returns to baseline without delay. Matching the environment's frequencies to the system's own spectrum is a tunable control of that sign.

ideas.title: Standardized excess-cost membership score
ideas.domain: Spatial network science (shortest paths in random geometric graphs)
ideas.problem: Predicting which intermediate elements lie on minimal-cost routes between two endpoints typically requires separate knowledge of several interacting factors, with no single compact measure of how likely an element is to be included.
ideas.approach: A Gaussian approximation combines the three contributing variables into one standardized score: the excess cost of routing through the element, divided by the spread of route costs between the endpoints. Membership probability then falls off as a single function of this score.
ideas.principle: When an element's inclusion in an optimal route depends on how far its detour exceeds the best option relative to the natural variability of route costs, one standardized excess-cost quantity collapses several factors into a single predictor of inclusion probability.

ideas.title: Context-embedded rule deployment over inherited structure
ideas.domain: Critical economic geography of neoliberal restructuring
ideas.problem: A single universal rule is often assumed to produce the same effects wherever it is applied, which ignores how it interacts with the inherited structures it is introduced into.
ideas.approach: Treat the outcome of introducing a uniform rule as determined by its interaction with the path-dependent legacy of each setting, and read the change as both dismantling old structures and unevenly reshaping them across scales.
ideas.principle: A uniform rule imposed on a system already shaped by its history yields context-specific, unevenly distributed outcomes, because the rule's effects are determined by its interaction with the accumulated structure it enters, and that interaction both destroys and reorganizes the existing structure at multiple levels.

ideas.title: Passive-engagement recovery of depleted control
ideas.domain: Environmental psychology (attention restoration theory)
ideas.problem: A limited capacity for effortful, goal-directed control is depleted by sustained demanding work, and everyday settings often either add further demands or fail to provide a way for that capacity to recover.
ideas.approach: Expose the controller to stimuli that engage it gently and involuntarily, with modest capture and no need for active filtering, so the effortful control system can replenish. Stimuli that are dramatic or that themselves demand active filtering are treated as non-restorative.
ideas.principle: A depleted effortful-control resource regenerates when the surrounding input engages the system through low-demand, involuntary capture and removes the need for active suppression; inputs that are intense or that require continued effortful filtering block this recovery.

ideas.title: Atypicality-scaled memory of starting conditions in fluctuations
ideas.domain: Quantum many-body dynamics after quenches
ideas.problem: Long-run averages are known to retain information about a system's starting condition, but it was unclear whether that memory also appears in the fluctuations around those averages, and how it scales.
ideas.approach: Build a family of starting states, score each one by how far it departs from a reference class of standard starts using an entropy-like deviation measure, and relate the size of the long-time fluctuations to that score. The fluctuation size varies smoothly with the score, and the score separates atypical starts from reference starts by decay rate.
ideas.principle: The variability of a system around its long-run average keeps a record of how atypical its starting point was relative to a reference class. Fluctuations shrink at a rate set by a smooth deviation measure from that class, so a single scalar of starting-point atypicality predicts the scaling.

ideas.title: Joint mean-and-noise reading of state-dependent increments
ideas.domain: Stochastic dynamics and trajectory inference of diffusing particles
ideas.problem: When the noise amplitude depends on state, the conditional mean of observed increments (the inferred drift) includes a spurious component that looks like a directed force, so equilibrium systems can appear driven or active.
ideas.approach: Estimate the spurious part of the conditional mean directly from moments of the observed increments, and only interpret the mean together with a consistently inferred state-dependent noise matrix, so that the two are reported as a pair.
ideas.principle: A conditional average of observed changes in a system whose fluctuation size varies with position contains a term produced by that variation rather than by any directed influence. The average is meaningful only jointly with a consistently estimated fluctuation model; pairing it with a mismatched fluctuation model manufactures apparent directed effects.

ideas.title: Designing within a standing exception regime
ideas.domain: Urban studies and urban planning theory
ideas.problem: A formal ordering scheme assumes its categories cover all cases, so the cases that fall outside them are treated as anomalies to be suppressed, which leaves a large part of the system unmanaged and ungoverned.
ideas.approach: Treat the non-conforming cases as a legitimate, persistent operating regime rather than a deviation. Build the governing policy so that it works inside that regime, instead of trying to eliminate the exceptions or assuming they will disappear.
ideas.principle: A system governed by a formal rule set should model its out-of-rule cases as a stable operating mode and design its control policies to function within that mode, rather than treating those cases as errors to be removed.

ideas.title: Role-separated multi-source fusion with per-source contribution audit
ideas.domain: Regional traffic simulation from mobile-phone, road-sensor and GPS data
ideas.problem: When several heterogeneous data sources are combined inside one simulator, it is rarely clear what each source actually contributes, and results can be inflated when the same data also informs model choices.
ideas.approach: Each data stream is assigned a distinct, separable job in the model (one sets volume and timing, another performs local correction, another guides choices). Each stream's added value is then measured by comparing the full model against simulation-free predictors on targets held out from calibration, with the overlap between tuning and test targets reported explicitly.
ideas.principle: A composite system built from several heterogeneous input streams gives each stream its own separate function. The marginal value of each stream is judged by comparing the full system with baselines that lack the simulated mechanism, using targets withheld from tuning, and any shared targets are disclosed as a limit on independence.

ideas.title: Priority inversion from local exception to global default
ideas.domain: Urban studies and political economy of gentrification
ideas.problem: A practice that began as a marginal, local exception is hard to explain when it later becomes the general rule everywhere, and the existing framing does not say what makes the shift global.
ideas.approach: The paper locates the change in a reordering of priorities: the governing objective moves from sustaining local reproduction to serving external productive circulation, and the once-marginal practice becomes the default because it connects to that wider flow.
ideas.principle: When a system's governing objective switches from maintaining its own internal needs to feeding an external circulation, a formerly isolated local exception becomes the default rule wherever the system connects to that circulation.

ideas.title: Restriction-consistent extension of an entropy via one-step marginals
ideas.domain: Thermodynamic formalism and ergodic theory on symbolic shift spaces
ideas.problem: The standard entropy and pressure machinery is defined only for shift-invariant probabilities, so it cannot be applied to the non-invariant measures that arise when a dynamical transfer operator is iterated.
ideas.approach: Define a new entropy for arbitrary measures from an expected-value function on one-step cylinders, chosen so that it agrees with the classical quantity on the invariant class. Build a divergence the same way, without requiring absolute continuity between the two measures, and derive variational principles from it.
ideas.principle: A quantity that is only meaningful for stationary objects can be extended to all objects by evaluating it through a single-step marginal functional. The extension matches the original on the restricted class, keeps concavity and semicontinuity, and yields a divergence that needs no density comparison.

ideas.title: Adoption explained by receiving context, not intrinsic merit
ideas.domain: Urban policy and critical urban geography (creative class and creative cities discourse)
ideas.problem: A popular concept's wide spread and policy influence is usually attributed to its intrinsic merits, which hides the structural conditions of the settings it moves through.
ideas.approach: Explain the reach of the idea by the configuration of the systems it travels into, and treat it as a new label that repackages existing arrangements. Test whether the new strategies change the underlying distribution of power and outcomes or only restate them in softer vocabulary.
ideas.principle: A proposal spreads according to how well it fits the pre-existing configuration of the system receiving it, and it can raise its own status by renaming established mechanisms as new imperatives while leaving their underlying dynamics unchanged.

ideas.title: Inertia-induced mode destabilization from overdamped spectrum
ideas.domain: Swarmalator dynamics (coupled position and phase oscillators)
ideas.problem: Adding inertia to a system whose relaxation is overdamped can make previously stable modes unstable and produce oscillatory motion, but the stability change is usually hard to predict without redoing the full second-order analysis.
ideas.approach: Compute each mode's eigenvalue in the overdamped (first-order) version of the system, then apply a closed-form test that says a mode is destabilized by inertia exactly when its real part exceeds a negative threshold set by its mass times the square of its imaginary part. This gives the inertial stability boundary directly from the overdamped spectrum.
ideas.principle: When a first-order relaxing system gains a second-order (mass-weighted) term, each mode's stability flips according to a single inequality that combines its overdamped growth rate with the squared frequency of its oscillation, so the first-order spectrum alone fixes where the second-order instability onset lies.

ideas.title: Robustness-defined grouping via higher-order connectivity
ideas.domain: Percolation theory and graph connectivity
ideas.problem: Standard cluster definitions treat elements as grouped whenever a single link joins them, so a group can be held together by one fragile connection and tells us little about how well it survives damage.
ideas.approach: Define groups as sets whose members stay mutually linked after the loss of any k members, and identify them efficiently by decomposing the link structure into biconnected pieces and then into finer three-way decomposition units, rather than testing every removal set directly.
ideas.principle: Strengthen a grouping rule from single-link persistence to persistence under the removal of any fixed number of members, and find such robust groups by recursively splitting the linkage structure into nested pieces that expose their own separation points.

ideas.title: Activity-based intersections as infrastructure
ideas.domain: Urban studies and urban anthropology (informal urban economies)
ideas.problem: Infrastructure is usually defined by fixed physical networks, so the flexible, provisional coordination that lets low-resource participants access shared resources is overlooked as a form of provisioning.
ideas.approach: Extend the concept of infrastructure from fixed, engineered channels to the recurring, improvised connections among participants. Treat those connections as a system that makes resources and opportunities reachable for people with limited means.
ideas.principle: A population of agents with no central design forms shifting, ad hoc links that together act as a shared access layer, expanding what each agent can reach. The layer is valued for its function, not its fixed structure.

ideas.title: Heavy-tailed aggregate stable-law scaling
ideas.domain: Percolation and epidemic spreading on inhomogeneous networks
ideas.problem: Fluctuations of a total built from many contributions are routinely assumed to be Gaussian after scaling, even when the contributions have heavy-tailed distributions, which misstates the spread and the finite-size scaling of the total.
ideas.approach: Identify the tail exponent of the contributions and use the generalized central limit theorem to predict the rescaled limit law and its scaling exponent, instead of applying the Gaussian limit. The exponent is set by the tail and can be independent of the control variable.
ideas.principle: A sum of many heavy-tailed quantities does not obey the ordinary central limit theorem; after rescaling its fluctuations converge to a stable law whose index is set by the tail exponent of the summands, so the scaling and shape of the aggregate are determined by that exponent alone.

ideas.title: Stake-holding coalitions competing for mobile investment through shared authority
ideas.domain: Urban political economy of growth coalitions
ideas.problem: Explanations of local development treat a locality's growth as a neutral market outcome, which misses that a bloc of agents with a fixed stake in one site can organize to pull mobile resources away from rival sites.
ideas.approach: Model each territory as the collective expression of a group whose returns rise with the intensity of use of a fixed asset. These groups compete with rival groups for growth-inducing inflows, and they use a shared authority to tilt those inflows toward their own asset while the costs fall on competitors and on the wider population.
ideas.principle: Agents that share a return tied to a fixed position, and that can mobilize a common decision authority, will compete to attract a mobile resource to that position, with the resulting costs externalized onto rival positions and to the bystanders who depend on them.

ideas.title: Exact noninteracting reexpression of biased exclusion dynamics
ideas.domain: Statistical physics of interacting directed strings on a cylinder
ideas.problem: Many-body stochastic systems with exclusion interactions are generally intractable, so their collective density profiles and fluctuation scaling are hard to obtain analytically.
ideas.approach: Local flip moves with excluded volume are shown to map exactly onto a noninteracting system whose steady-state one-point statistics are known. Biasing the moves changes the scaling from diffusive to drift-dominated, and the biased case maps to a growing interface.
ideas.principle: A system of mutually excluding extended objects that undergo local, possibly asymmetric, exchange moves can be exactly recast as a set of independent tracked positions. Symmetry of the moves sets the scaling exponent, and asymmetry shifts it to a drift-dominated regime, so one-point statistics become computable in closed form.

ideas.title: Two-axis decomposition of an umbrella concept
ideas.domain: Urban planning and social sustainability
ideas.problem: An umbrella term that everyone accepts as multi-part, such as social sustainability, stays vague because its components are never specified or agreed.
ideas.approach: Split the concept into two complementary dimensions, one about how evenly people can reach shared benefits and one about whether the collective unit can persist and renew itself, and define each dimension explicitly.
ideas.principle: A vague composite notion becomes operational when it is decomposed into two complementary axes, one measuring how fairly benefits are distributed and one measuring whether the collective unit sustains itself.

ideas.title: Dual-system stationary-current representation of effective spread
ideas.domain: Statistical physics of diffusion in fluctuating periodic potentials
ideas.problem: The effective long-time spreading rate of a random walker in a periodic landscape whose internal state fluctuates is hard to compute, because it normally requires solving a backward equation for an auxiliary corrector function.
ideas.approach: Replace the corrector with a dual system obtained by reversing the driving field, so the effective rate is written entirely in terms of stationary densities and probability currents of the original and dual systems. When the stationary current vanishes, the rate reduces to a local expression.
ideas.principle: A quantity defined through an auxiliary function that solves a backward equation can be rewritten, via a sign-reversed dual process, as stationary quantities of two forward processes; when net flow is zero, the global quantity collapses to a local one.

ideas.title: Enabling-topology override of energetic relaxation
ideas.domain: Nanomagnetic artificial spin ice, facilitated relaxation
ideas.problem: Relaxation in constrained many-body systems is usually assumed to follow energy minimization, but in natural materials energetics, disorder and dynamics are entangled, so the rules that actually govern which states can be reached are hard to isolate.
ideas.approach: Build a designable system whose local moves are allowed only when a neighboring configuration enables them, and tune the interactions so that the enabling structure can be varied independently of the energy landscape. Use the resulting connectivity of allowed transitions to predict which classes of states relax freely and which are kinetically isolated.
ideas.principle: When each local change is permitted only if a neighboring arrangement enables it, the set of reachable states is fixed by the connectivity of enabled moves rather than by which states are lowest in energy. Groups of states that the enabling graph does not link stay isolated and settle into non-equilibrium distributions even when a lower-energy route exists in principle.

ideas.title: Exposure-decline feedback spiral
ideas.domain: Human-nature contact and environmental attitudes
ideas.problem: Reduced direct contact with a resource can erode the motivation and valuation that would otherwise sustain contact, and this decline is rarely recognized or addressed as a self-reinforcing process.
ideas.approach: Model the loss of contact as a closed loop in which lower exposure produces weaker positive feelings and attitudes, which in turn reduce further engagement, so the loop must be broken by deliberately reintroducing contact.
ideas.principle: When reduced use of a resource lowers the value placed on it, and lower valuation further reduces use, the system falls into a self-reinforcing decline that persists until an external intervention re-establishes the original exposure.

ideas.title: Partial-view advantage equals one minus twice local decoding error
ideas.domain: Quantum error-correcting codes (toric code, fault-tolerant quantum computing)
ideas.problem: When a redundantly encoded hidden bit is spread across many components, it is unclear how much any observer who sees only a part of the system can learn about that bit, and how that leakage depends on the noise and the geometry of the observed part.
ideas.approach: Show that the best achievable advantage in guessing the hidden bit from a restricted region equals exactly 1 minus twice the failure probability of optimal decoding that uses only that region. This turns a hard information-leakage question into a local decoding-error calculation that can be evaluated per region and under any noise model.
ideas.principle: For a hidden binary value stored redundantly across many noisy components, the maximal advantage an observer gains from a restricted subset of those components equals one minus twice the error probability of the best estimator that sees only that subset. Leakage is therefore identical to local estimation error, so it can be computed from the subset alone and does not require the full system.

ideas.title: Threshold-gated capture weighting
ideas.domain: Attention in language models, modeled as Kuramoto-style synchronization of coupled oscillators
ideas.problem: A selection mechanism that aggregates many candidate inputs by a softmax-style normalization always spreads weight over the candidates, so it cannot express "nothing relevant is present" and has no principled account of when selection occurs.
ideas.approach: Model each candidate as a unit whose state carries its content and whose tuning drifts with its age, and let a receiver couple to them according to how well their tuning matches its own setting. Solving for the locked state gives a closed-form weighting with two regimes: above a critical coupling strength the receiver captures the matching units and its weights sum to one, while below it the receiver stays quiet and its total weight is less than one.
ideas.principle: A receiver with a tunable setting couples to many independent units that each carry a state and a drift. Units matching the setting are pulled into a common state and share normalized weight once coupling exceeds a critical threshold set by the pool; below that threshold the receiver produces only a sub-unit, near-zero response, so the aggregate output encodes both selection and absence.

ideas.title: Potential-gap-driven reinvestment
ideas.domain: Urban economics of land and housing markets
ideas.problem: Explanations of a shift in a place's occupancy and investment focus on who is moving in, which misses that the underlying driver can be a structural mismatch between an asset's depreciated current return and its higher potential return.
ideas.approach: Treat the location as a stored asset whose current yield has decayed while its potential yield has risen. The widening gap between the two makes reinvestment profitable, and returning capital restructures the system regardless of where the investing agents originate.
ideas.principle: A stored resource whose realized value has fallen below its attainable value creates a gap that pulls in external capital; the flow of that capital closes the gap and reshapes the system, so the trigger is the gap itself rather than the identity of the agents.

ideas.title: Replica lift of multi-copy statistics into spectral dephasing
ideas.domain: Quantum many-body dynamics of Rényi entanglement entropies in chaotic Floquet systems
ideas.problem: Nonlinear statistics of an evolving state, such as purity and higher-order moments, do not have the simple spectral decay form that ordinary linear observables follow, so their time dynamics is hard to characterize from the spectrum of the evolution operator.
ideas.approach: Stack several copies of the evolving system so the nonlinear statistic becomes a linear expectation value of a copy-permutation operator in the enlarged space. Its decay is then written as a spectral sum over eigenmodes of the stacked dynamics, and matrix elements are modeled with ansätze so the whole time dependence reduces to smooth functions that dephase.
ideas.principle: A nonlinear multi-copy statistic of an evolving state is rewritten as a linear expectation over stacked copies of the dynamics, using an operator that permutes the copies; its time decay then follows the same eigenphase-dephasing spectral form as ordinary linear observables.

ideas.title: Coarse observation hides unbounded divergence
ideas.domain: Quantum thermodynamics of driven open systems (entropy production and coarse-grained trajectory measurement)
ideas.problem: A lower bound on an asymmetry between forward and reverse processes, estimated from a coarse, imperfect observation record, may look finite and informative even when the true asymmetry is unbounded, so it is unclear how much hidden irreversibility a measurement can conceal.
ideas.approach: Construct a system whose two process laws have mismatched supports, so that the true divergence diverges, and pass both laws through a single lossy observation channel with false positives and finite efficiency. The channel's output still differs between the two laws by a finite, positive amount, while the part of the divergence that is invisible to it is controlled by a separate, explicitly computable term.
ideas.principle: When two generating processes differ most strongly in events that a noisy, lossy observer cannot separate from background noise, the observer's divergence estimate stays finite and positive while the full divergence grows without bound; the hidden part scales with the rate of the unobservable flow divided by the noise scale.

ideas.title: Admissible-perturbation susceptibility as graded intrinsic metric
ideas.domain: Quantum many-body chaos and eigenstate geometry
ideas.problem: Binary chaos diagnostics such as level-spacing statistics fail to rank systems by degree of chaos, and they can disagree with dynamical signatures like relaxation and scrambling.
ideas.approach: Measure how much each state changes under deformations drawn only from the set of modifications the system's constraints permit, and use the resulting susceptibility as a graded, intrinsic score. Because the score depends on the admissible perturbation manifold rather than on the probing protocol, it can be compared across systems.
ideas.principle: A state's graded sensitivity to changes restricted to an admissible set of modifications, where that set is fixed by the system's own structural constraints, gives an intrinsic measure of how randomized or unstructured the state is. Minimal sensitivity then tends to coincide with several independent signatures of that property.

ideas.title: Maximum-likelihood class recovery from partial syndrome
ideas.domain: Quantum error correction (surface codes)
ideas.problem: When a hidden disturbance acts coherently and only partial, syndrome-type information is observable, it is unclear which recovery action best preserves the underlying state, and whether a finite-size or asymptotic threshold can be trusted.
ideas.approach: Choose the recovery that is most probable given the observed partial measurement, meaning the equivalence class of disturbances with the highest posterior weight. The paper proves this maximum-likelihood rule maximizes overall recovery fidelity over all deterministic syndrome-conditioned strategies, and its threshold matches the information-theoretic optimum.
ideas.principle: For a hidden disturbance observed only through a many-to-one signal, the optimal corrective action is the one that maximizes the summed probability of all disturbances consistent with the signal and that restore the target state. Deterministic recovery per signal cannot beat this rule.

ideas.title: Hierarchical reconstruction of hidden profile from nonlinear response coefficients
ideas.domain: Holographic gravity and quantum information dynamics (drag force, entanglement membrane)
ideas.problem: A hidden geometric or structural profile of a system is hard to access directly, and it is unclear how an externally measured response relates to the internal profile and whether the full profile can be recovered from it.
ideas.approach: Show that the nonlinear expansion coefficients of a driven response form an invertible map to the hidden profile, with the leading coefficient fixing a global property and each higher-order coefficient fixing progressively more local features. Use this hierarchy to reconstruct the profile from the response, and add a complementary second observable to fix the remaining unknown scale.
ideas.principle: An externally driven response's successive nonlinear coefficients form an invertible map onto a hidden profile: the first coefficient gives a global property, and each higher coefficient probes a more localized part of the profile, so the full profile is recoverable from the response hierarchy plus one complementary measurement.

ideas.title: Whole-pattern relational configuration
ideas.domain: Architecture and urban spatial analysis (space syntax)
ideas.problem: Local attributes of an element, taken alone, fail to explain its role in a larger system, so function and behaviour that depend on how the parts are arranged go unexplained.
ideas.approach: Describe each element by its relations to all the other elements in the system, so that its significance comes from the whole pattern of connections rather than from intrinsic properties. Use this configurational description both to analyse existing systems and to guide the design of new ones.
ideas.principle: An element's role is defined by its position within the full network of pairwise relations, so the same element can have different roles in different overall arrangements, and analysis and design can be developed together from that relational structure.

ideas.title: Structure-constrained block decomposition of random spectra
ideas.domain: Quantum chaos and random matrix theory of symmetric quantum systems
ideas.problem: Level statistics of a chaotic system with symmetries are described one sector at a time, which misses exact coincidences that cut across differently labeled sectors and mishandles cases where sectors with different labels share part of their spectrum.
ideas.approach: Split the system into labeled sectors that are irreducible under the structure's algebra. Enforce the exact identifications and degeneracies the structure imposes, apply the generic random-ensemble statistics within each remaining block, and treat unrelated blocks as statistically independent. Sectors reachable from differently labeled configurations are allowed to share components.
ideas.principle: A system is partitioned into labeled, irreducible components. Exact shared structure is imposed deterministically across components, each remaining component follows a generic random ensemble, and components with no structural link are independent. Some components may be shared by configurations with different labels.

ideas.title: Indirect approach to a balanced center via iterated tension resolution
ideas.domain: Urban planning and sustainable development
ideas.problem: A goal that must balance three mutually competing objectives cannot be reached by optimizing for it directly, and the way the goal is defined can be too vague or backward-looking to guide action.
ideas.approach: Treat the target as the center of a triangle of competing aims. Approach it only approximately and indirectly, by repeatedly confronting and resolving the conflicts between pairs of aims, and redefine the target as those conflicts expose its weaknesses.
ideas.principle: When a target sits at the balanced center of three mutually opposed objectives, it is reached only indirectly, through a sustained cycle of resolving pairwise conflicts, and the target's definition is revised as that cycle reveals its inadequacy.

ideas.title: Minimal-support subspace entropy for a family of evolved observables
ideas.domain: quantum many-body physics (entanglement entropy of free fermions in time)
ideas.problem: Entanglement entropy is well defined for spatial subregions, but there is no principled measure of how much structure a sequence of time-evolved quantities carries across a time interval.
ideas.approach: Take the smallest sub-space that contains every member of the transformed family, restrict the joint description to that sub-space, and compute the entropy of the reduced description there. The resulting quantity scales with the length of the sequence and is stable as the sampling step shrinks.
ideas.principle: To measure how much a family of transformed objects depends on a shared underlying system, identify the minimal subspace that supports the whole family, reduce the description to that subspace, and take the entropy of the reduced description. Its growth with the family's extent reveals the structure of the sequence.

ideas.title: Map the remedy that sustains the problem before intervening
ideas.domain: coaching and organizational change
ideas.problem: Interventions aimed at removing a persistent difficulty often fail because the attempted fixes are themselves part of what keeps the difficulty going, and this is not diagnosed first.
ideas.approach: Before choosing new actions, identify the existing corrective attempts that maintain the difficulty, along with the resistances and self-deceptions that hold them in place, and treat them as components of the loop to be changed.
ideas.principle: A persistent disturbance is often sustained by the system's own corrective responses, so the loop has to be mapped and the corrections that feed it located before any change is attempted.

ideas.title: Expert-rated operational definitions for latent qualities
ideas.domain: Urban design and walkability measurement
ideas.problem: Holistic, subjective qualities of an environment are hard to measure objectively, so studies cannot test whether they relate to behaviour.
ideas.approach: A panel of experts rates the environment, and those ratings are used to derive explicit, physically measurable operational definitions of each quality. The definitions are then checked against the qualitative definitions and tested for association with an outcome in a separate validation study.
ideas.principle: A vague latent property can be made measurable by having judges score observable features, distilling those scores into explicit checkable rules, and validating the rules against an independent outcome.

ideas.title: Dephasing-suppressed series truncation onto a restricted subspace
ideas.domain: Quantum chaos and random quantum circuit simulation
ideas.problem: Exact evaluation of a multi-point correlator in individual instances of a complex dynamical system is intractable for standard classical methods, because contributions from outside a tractable subspace seem to accumulate.
ideas.approach: Expand the correlator as a rapidly converging series whose leading term is computed exactly within a small restricted subspace, with the remaining terms representing excursions outside it. Dynamical dephasing suppresses those excursion terms, so truncating after the leading term gives an accurate, polynomial-cost estimate.
ideas.principle: A hard quantity can be written as a series whose leading term lives in a small, structured subspace; randomness-driven decorrelation makes the out-of-subspace corrections cancel, so truncation becomes accurate and cheap.

ideas.title: Self-averaging of many independent heavy-tailed components into a deterministic effective model
ideas.domain: Integrable systems and soliton gas asymptotics (Toda lattice)
ideas.problem: When a dense system is built from many independent random components with large, uncontrolled individual fluctuations, it is unclear whether its macroscopic behavior is still predictable, and standard deterministic-coefficient analyses do not apply.
ideas.approach: Show that the random ensemble concentrates: as the number of components grows, the realized system converges at a polynomial rate to a deterministic continuum description, with the component density setting the macroscopic averages. The continuum description is then analysed to get the full large-scale picture.
ideas.principle: A dense collection of independent random units, each with only a finite moment of its strength, concentrates around a deterministic effective description as the count grows. The leftover fluctuation is bounded at a known rate, and the macroscopic averages are fixed by the density of the units.

ideas.title: Parameter defined by its read protocol
ideas.domain: Memristive and electrochemical synaptic devices
ideas.problem: A single reported number is treated as an intrinsic parameter of a system, but it conflates the hidden internal state with the signal produced when that state is read, so two different states can look identical and the reported value depends on an unstated measurement.
ideas.approach: Separate the evolving internal state from the observation map that turns it into a measured signal, and define the effective parameter as the result of a specified read procedure. Test whether distinct histories are distinguishable under different read conditions, and report the state, the readout, and the mapping between them.
ideas.principle: An effective parameter of a dynamical system is the output of a specified observation of its hidden state, so it is not a property of the system alone but of the system together with its observation procedure. Two hidden states may coincide under one observation and separate under another, so claims about the parameter must name both the stored variable and the observation.

ideas.title: Global position over local attributes as flow generator
ideas.domain: Urban pedestrian movement and space syntax
ideas.problem: Models of movement flow in a network attribute traffic mainly to local attractor sites, so they miss how the overall connection structure itself channels flow.
ideas.approach: Treat a node's global relational position in the whole connection structure as the primary generator of baseline flow, and treat local attractors as multipliers applied on top of that baseline. Measure the flow-relevant quantity as a global centrality-like index rather than a local count.
ideas.principle: In a connected system, the throughput a node receives is set mainly by its position relative to the entire network, and local draws act as multiplicative amplifiers on that structurally generated baseline.

ideas.title: Transfer-indexed fluctuation bound via coincidence counting
ideas.domain: Mathematical physics of eigenstate fluctuations in free-fermion lattice models
ideas.problem: Bounding the variance of a sum of local quantities within a fixed-energy configuration of a many-component system usually requires controlling many interfering off-diagonal contributions, and naive bounds grow with system size.
ideas.approach: Split the centered observable into pieces indexed by the shift each piece induces in the conserved total. Bound the zero-shift piece with a norm inequality, and bound the nonzero-shift pieces by counting exact coincidences among the underlying frequency differences, which is controlled by an algebraic result on roots of unity.
ideas.principle: A fluctuation of a linear observable in a state of fixed total energy splits into components labelled by the change they produce in a conserved quantity; the unchanged component is bounded by a norm argument, while the changing components are bounded by the number of exact coincidences among their frequency differences, so the bound scales with that count rather than with the size of the system.

ideas.title: Competing advocate proposals with explicit choice
ideas.domain: Urban planning and public policy
ideas.problem: A single authority producing one plan hides the value judgments inside it, so the public cannot see or intelligently choose between the different interests the plan serves.
ideas.approach: Several parties, each advocating a different set of interests, each produce a complete candidate plan. The full set of candidates is presented to a separate decision body, which chooses among them, so the value trade-offs become visible and are settled by deliberate selection rather than by the producer's hidden preferences.
ideas.principle: When a choice depends on value judgments rather than on facts, split production from judgment: let multiple biased agents each build a complete candidate under their own objective, then have a separate chooser select among the explicit candidates instead of accepting one hidden compromise.

ideas.title: First-unit filtering against completion-time sampling bias
ideas.domain: Parallel simulation of stochastic processes with absorbing states
ideas.problem: When workers repeatedly run units whose durations depend on their outcome, and only completed units are recorded within a fixed budget, the recorded sample over-represents fast-finishing outcomes, so the observed statistics are systematically distorted even as throughput rises.
ideas.approach: Compare continuous restart-and-record sampling with a rule that keeps only the first unit each worker attempts, and derive the exact composition of completed units and the mean-squared error of each estimator to find the worker allocations where the filtered rule becomes more accurate despite yielding fewer samples.
ideas.principle: When each parallel agent restarts after finishing and only finished items are recorded under a fixed time budget, items that finish quickly are overrepresented; keeping only each agent's first item removes this composition bias, and beyond a budget-dependent agent count the lower-variance-of-bias option yields lower total error despite having fewer samples.

ideas.title: Temporary probing to expose hidden equivalence distinctions
ideas.domain: Graph automorphisms and vertex-orbit partitioning via spectral signatures
ideas.problem: Elements of a structure can look alike under invariant summaries while not being interchangeable under any true symmetry, so fixed invariant signatures can merge distinct classes and miss the real equivalence structure.
ideas.approach: Build a hierarchy of increasingly expressive invariant signatures, strengthening each one in response to specific counterexamples where it fails. Where the unperturbed signatures still cannot separate elements, apply temporary controlled perturbations to the system and read the responses, which reveal differences hidden in the original state.
ideas.principle: To separate things that look identical under passive measurement but differ in their true relational structure, temporarily disturb the system in a controlled way, record how each element responds, and use those responses as added distinguishing evidence, strengthening the test in steps driven by observed failures.

ideas.title: Speed-separated direct-link network reconstruction
ideas.domain: Inference of coupling networks among multiscale stochastic processes
ideas.problem: Inferring which components directly interact in a network is hard when components evolve at widely different speeds, because fast components must be resolved finely while slow ones need long observation, and indirect dependencies blur the true links.
ideas.approach: Compute a rescaled pairwise dependence rate and its conditional version given the other components, keep only links that survive conditioning, and orient each link by comparing the speeds of the two endpoints. The speed gap is used as a source of identifiability rather than treated as an obstacle.
ideas.principle: When interacting units operate at different speeds, a pairwise dependence measure conditioned on all other units removes indirect paths, and the rate asymmetry between the two ends of a surviving link reveals its direction and builds a hierarchical tree.

ideas.title: Maximum-causal-entropy depth test for sequential independence
ideas.domain: Animal movement ecology and Lévy walk statistics
ideas.problem: A common model assumes each step in a sequence is drawn fresh, independent of its past, but this renewal assumption is rarely tested, and histograms of step sizes alone cannot reveal whether the sequence has memory.
ideas.approach: Build the least-committal sequence model that reproduces the observed lagged correlations, using maximum causal entropy, and let the data select the depth of the resulting chain. The selected depth then distinguishes independent steps from short-memory and long-memory dependence, and the group version separates individual memory from delayed coupling and shared drivers.
ideas.principle: To test whether a sequence of random draws is independent of its past, fit the most unbiased model that matches its observed lagged correlations, let the data choose how far back the dependence reaches, and read independence, short memory, or long memory from that chosen depth.
concepts: maximum causal entropy at fixed lagged correlations

ideas.title: Staged claim separation for intervention effects
ideas.domain: LLM-agent team frameworks informed by human-team theory
ideas.problem: When a controller changes a multi-component system mid-run, the effects are often conflated, so a requested change, its activation, its completion, and its actual benefit get reported as one outcome.
ideas.approach: The framework keeps each stage of an intervention as a separate, individually stated claim (queued, applied, assembled, understood, improved), applies changes only at defined dependency boundaries, and declares unobserved emergent states as unmeasured rather than inferring them.
ideas.principle: An action on a layered system should be recorded as a sequence of distinct, separately verifiable stages, with each stage claimed only when its own evidence exists and unmeasured internal states explicitly excluded from the claims.

ideas.title: Graded depth-of-change classification for reforms
ideas.domain: political economy of neoliberalism and urban governance
ideas.problem: Reform efforts are often labelled as deep system change when they only adjust surface parameters, and the depth of an intervention is not classified in a way that separates replacing a system from re-tuning it.
ideas.approach: Arrange interventions on a continuum by how deeply they alter the underlying system: full replacement of the system, a shift in its operating regime, or limited parameter adjustments that leave the reproduction logic intact. Then test whether a proposed change belongs to a shallow tier while being presented as a deeper one.
ideas.principle: Interventions on a system can be ordered by how far they reach into its core dynamics, from total replacement through regime change to parameter tuning. Shallow adjustments can keep the system's self-sustaining logic unchanged while being presented as transformation.

ideas.title: One-sided spectral certificate of reversibility
ideas.domain: Non-Hermitian spectral theory and stochastic dynamics (holonomy, detailed balance, entropy production)
ideas.problem: Spectral data of a linear dynamical operator are often read as evidence about whether the dynamics are reversible, but a real spectrum does not certify reversibility and the spectrum says nothing about how large the irreversibility is.
ideas.approach: Define reversibility as self-adjointness of the operator in the inner product weighted by the invariant reference state. Treat any non-real eigenvalue, exceptional point, or nonzero winding number as a sufficient certificate of irreversibility, and quantify its magnitude separately with a bound that depends on the current.
ideas.principle: For a linear process with a known invariant weighting, the process is symmetric under that weighting only if certain structural signatures are absent. Those signatures can certify asymmetry, but their absence does not certify symmetry, and the signatures do not determine the strength of the asymmetry, which needs a separate quantity.

ideas.title: Reset-driven mass concentration on a designated subset
ideas.domain: Gossip-based distributed averaging with stochastic resetting on networks
ideas.problem: In a randomly mixing network that conserves a total quantity, there is no direct way to make that quantity end up concentrated on a chosen small subset of units so that it is spread evenly across them from their initial contents.
ideas.approach: Units mix pairwise at random, and a designated subset is additionally restarted to its initial contents at a small rate. The restarts continually reinject the starting content into the subset, so the steady-state total is set by the ratio of the full population size to the subset size, and the restart schedule can be switched on and off to tune the spread.
ideas.principle: A conserved quantity that is redistributed by random pairwise exchange among many units can be steered onto a small chosen group by stochastically reinjecting that group's initial content; the long-run total is the reinjected amount scaled by the ratio of the whole population to the group.

ideas.title: Passive restoration of depleted attention
ideas.domain: Environmental psychology: exposure to natural settings and attention restoration
ideas.problem: A limited-capacity control resource that has been depleted by sustained demanding effort needs a way to recover, and it is unclear whether restoration requires active rest or whether passive exposure can do it.
ideas.approach: Expose the depleted system to a low-demand, effortlessly engaging environment and measure whether the control resource and affect recover. Compare the immersive version against a weaker simulated version, and test whether the benefit flows through a linked self-related state or through the resource itself.
ideas.principle: A depleted limited-capacity control resource recovers through passive, effortless engagement with a low-demand environment, and the recovery is stronger when the engagement is immersive rather than represented indirectly. The benefit is partly carried by a linked connectedness state rather than by the resource itself.
