ideas.title: Bottom-up derivation of an aggregate measure from its generating dynamics
ideas.domain: Statistical physics (nonextensive entropy)
ideas.problem: A generalized aggregate measure is usually postulated top-down to fit a target distribution, so its consistency properties (such as additivity and compatibility with standard laws) must be checked separately.
ideas.approach: Build the aggregate measure bottom-up from the underlying step-by-step dynamics that generate the distribution. Compute all quantities with ordinary linear averages, so the measure's consistency properties follow from the construction and the standard results are recovered in the limit where the deviation vanishes.
ideas.principle: When a non-standard summary of a system is wanted, derive it from the local rules that generate the system's states rather than postulating it. Then the summary's consistency properties follow from the construction, and the standard case appears as a limit of the general one.

ideas.title: Bounded-fluctuation window to preserve ordered periodic behavior
ideas.domain: Quantum many-body physics: monitored discrete time crystals
ideas.problem: Periodically driven interacting systems heat up under noise, so ordered periodic response is destroyed, and it is unclear whether ordered behavior survives when random fluctuations are included.
ideas.approach: Restrict the random fluctuations to a finite window, which discards rare large-deviation excursions while keeping typical ones. Narrow windows keep the periodic order, intermediate windows leave it finite-lived as the ordered runs leave one by one, and wide windows destroy it.
ideas.principle: Rare extreme excursions of a noisy process can drive an otherwise ordered system into a disordered state. Clipping the noise to a bounded range removes those excursions, so the ordered behavior persists for a time that shrinks as the allowed range widens, until a critical width is passed.

ideas.title: Relational categories over fixed labels
ideas.domain: Urban studies of megacities in the global South
ideas.problem: Fixed labels such as 'slum' and 'subaltern' treat marginalized places and people as having stable essences, which hides their livelihoods, self-organization and politics and limits how they can be analyzed.
ideas.approach: Replace ontological and topological categories with categories defined by the processes and relations that produce them, such as informality, peripheries, zones of exception and grey spaces. These categories are used to analyze how places and groups are constituted, not what they fundamentally are.
ideas.principle: When a group or place is labeled by a fixed essence or fixed location, its role in a larger system is obscured. Defining categories by the ongoing relations and processes that generate them, rather than by inherent properties, captures how the entity is produced and can change.

ideas.title: Bottom-up scaling from competition for bounded space
ideas.domain: Urban evolution and city scaling laws
ideas.problem: City planning relies on top-down strategies, and there is no integrated theory that explains how urban size and shape arise from the way many individual units develop.
ideas.approach: Treat the system as many locally acting units that grow and compete for a limited shared resource, and derive its size and shape distributions from that competition. The resulting scaling laws, drawn from network, allometric, and fractal structure, then set the resource limits and sustainability constraints the system faces.
ideas.principle: When many locally interacting units grow into a bounded shared medium, competition for that medium produces global size and shape distributions with power-law scaling, so the system-wide regularities can be predicted from local growth and congestion rules rather than imposed from above.

ideas.title: History-driven ranking inversion under shared dynamics
ideas.domain: Non-equilibrium thermal relaxation (Mpemba effect) with time-delayed Newton cooling
ideas.problem: When two units share the same dynamics and final conditions, it is unclear whether the initial state alone decides which one ends up ahead, or whether the schedule of inputs used to prepare them can reverse that ordering, and which schedule gives the largest reversal.
ideas.approach: Prepare each unit by applying a piecewise-constant sequence of input levels before both are moved to a common final input, then derive exact conditions under which the ordering reverses for limited protocols. Test whether the best protocol survives relaxing the synchrony and count constraints, using numerical optimization over the extended protocol space.
ideas.principle: Two units governed by the same rule toward a common endpoint can have their ranking inverted by the input schedule applied before they are merged; the largest inversion comes from synchronized, extreme-valued schedules with the fewest switches, and extending the schedule class tends to confirm that extreme as the optimum.

ideas.title: Hidden ordinal-spacing sensitivity in nearest-match ranking
ideas.domain: Voting advice applications (algorithmic political recommenders)
ideas.problem: When ordered categorical responses are converted to numbers to compute distances for matching, the unstated choice of numeric spacing can change which top matches are returned, even though the raw responses are identical and the choice is rarely disclosed.
ideas.approach: Parameterize the gap between adjacent ordered categories with a single spacing factor, sweep that factor over a range, and measure how often the top-ranked matches change. Report the resulting sensitivity so the hidden quantification choice becomes visible and auditable.
ideas.principle: When a ranking relies on distances between ordered labels, the numeric embedding of those labels is an unstated free parameter. Sweeping that parameter and reporting how often the top selections flip makes the outcome's dependence on an arbitrary design choice explicit.

ideas.title: Closed-loop sense-integrate-optimize adaptation
ideas.domain: Smart city IT infrastructure
ideas.problem: Shared infrastructure is often run on static rules or siloed data, so it cannot adjust its resource use to the real, changing behavior of the people who use it.
ideas.approach: Collect near-real-time measurements from both physical and virtual sensors, pool them into one integrated platform that services can share, and run analytics, modeling, and optimization on that data inside routine operational decisions. The resulting allocation then adapts to observed demand.
ideas.principle: A distributed system stays efficient when it continuously measures its own state through heterogeneous probes, pools those streams into one shared platform, and feeds them into predictive optimization that reconfigures resource allocation to match the behavior of its users.

ideas.title: Legible scaffold balanced with diverse activity
ideas.domain: urban design and planning
ideas.problem: Planners often treat dense, irregular, or apparently disordered activity as a failure to be suppressed, which can erode the vitality of the system they manage.
ideas.approach: The idea treats a healthy complex system as a balance between a readable, ordered structure and many varied local exchanges. Apparent disorder is reinterpreted as the normal rhythm that keeps the system alive, and design aims to support it rather than remove it.
ideas.principle: A complex system stays vital when a stable, legible framework coexists with many varied local interactions, and what looks like irregularity is often the functional rhythm of that activity.

ideas.title: Theory built from excluded cases to expose a dominant model's limits
ideas.domain: Urban and regional studies (metropolitan theory)
ideas.problem: Theories fitted to one dominant reference population are treated as general, so they cannot describe the variant forms that appear in other populations.
ideas.approach: Build new conceptual vectors from the experience of the underrepresented cases, then use them to deepen and revise the general framework, rather than only testing the dominant theory against those cases.
ideas.principle: A model calibrated on a single dominant population inherits that population's structure as if it were universal; generating new concepts from the cases it excludes reveals the hidden assumptions and extends the framework to cover the variants.

ideas.title: Count-conditioned local response for collective prediction
ideas.domain: Information cascades on networks of LLM agents
ideas.problem: A unit's response to a fraction of active neighbours is assumed to depend only on that fraction, so models built from it mispredict collective outcomes on heterogeneous structures and cannot be fixed from network topology alone.
ideas.approach: Measure each unit's response in its local context as a function of both the absolute number of signalling contacts and the fraction, then feed this context-conditioned response into a mean-field prediction of the aggregate outcome, including its tipping points.
ideas.principle: A decision triggered by repeated signals from a set of sources depends on how many sources there are as well as their proportion, so an aggregate prediction must be built from responses measured under the exposure structure in which the collective process actually unfolds.

ideas.title: Common-mode versus differential signature test for attributing shared fluctuations
ideas.domain: Power-grid frequency dynamics with Kuramoto-model coupled oscillators
ideas.problem: When a networked system's fluctuations could come from internal coupled dynamics or from an external shared driver, matching aggregate spectra and marginal statistics does not identify which mechanism is responsible.
ideas.approach: Separate each unit's fluctuations into a component shared by all units and a component that differs between units, then use the mismatch between the observed and simulated split to rule out candidate mechanisms that look alike on single-unit statistics.
ideas.principle: When several mechanisms reproduce the same marginal statistics of a set of coupled units, discriminate them by whether their fluctuations are common to all units or relative between them.

ideas.title: Matched-null attribution with non-invasive readout
ideas.domain: LLM agent population opinion dynamics under competing campaigns
ideas.problem: When an evolving multi-agent system is pushed by interventions, observed changes mix the intervention's effect with changes that would have happened anyway, and measuring the state may itself disturb the system.
ideas.approach: Run matched copies of the system with no intervention, subtract their trajectory drift from the intervened runs, and read the state with a separate probe that does not feed back into the dynamics. Compare intervention schedules against the same matched baselines.
ideas.principle: To credit an action with an effect in a self-evolving system, compare it against an identically configured run that lacks the action, and take measurements through a channel that leaves the system's evolution unchanged.

ideas.title: Parameter-independent histogram from a linear subspace walk
ideas.domain: Statistical mechanics of classical spin systems (partition functions via high-temperature expansion)
ideas.problem: Computing a sum over configurations weighted by a parameter-dependent factor normally requires a fresh sampling run for every parameter value, and direct sampling in the energy or parameter space is costly and sensitive to the parameter.
ideas.approach: Rewrite the sum as a sum over the null space of a binary incidence matrix over F2, whose weight distribution does not depend on the parameter. Run a Wang-Landau-style random walk directly inside that null space to estimate the weight histogram once, then obtain the full sum, and its derivatives, at any parameter value by analytic reweighting.
ideas.principle: When a parameter-weighted sum over structures can be recast as a sum over a linear subspace of binary selections, the count of selections at each size is fixed by the subspace alone. Estimating that count histogram once by a walk confined to the subspace lets every parameter value be evaluated afterward without resampling.

ideas.title: Schedule-invariant order of commitments in sequential inference
ideas.domain: Statistical physics of diffusion-based generative models on spin glasses
ideas.problem: It is unclear whether the order in which a gradually-revealing sequential process resolves its alternatives depends on the chosen timing protocol or is fixed by the target itself.
ideas.approach: The paper shows that any member of a family of noising protocols is a time-changed version of one canonical process, so the sequence of macroscopic decisions is protocol-independent. Protocols only set when decisions happen and at what cost, and each split is decided like a binary channel whose strength is set by the leading eigenvalue of the parent's correlation structure.
ideas.principle: When a process accumulates information about nested alternatives through a noisy channel, reparametrizing its clock leaves the ordering of its irreversible commitments unchanged; the schedule only moves when commitments occur and what they cost, while the commitment order is fixed by the structure of the hypothesis hierarchy.

ideas.title: Separate onset criteria for a growing variable and its eroding gate
ideas.domain: Bifurcation analysis of emergent intelligent systems and their controllability
ideas.problem: Growth in a self-amplifying quantity is often assumed to bring with it control over that quantity, but a separate gating quantity may have its own dynamics and thresholds, so the two can diverge.
ideas.approach: Model the growing quantity and the gating quantity as coupled variables, each with its own dynamics, and derive a separate onset criterion for each. The gate includes an erosion term, so it can undergo a fold with hysteresis at its own threshold, independent of whether the growing quantity has emerged.
ideas.principle: Two coupled variables, one self-amplifying and one continuously eroded, each have independent onset criteria. Crossing the onset of the first does not guarantee that the second is controllable, and the second shows history-dependent switching when its own criterion is crossed.

ideas.title: Throughput-matched condition comparison
ideas.domain: Environmental psychology of natural versus urban scenes
ideas.problem: When stimulus categories differ in how much information they deliver, outcome differences cannot be attributed to category content rather than to the volume of information presented.
ideas.approach: Equalize the information rate across the compared stimulus sets so that any difference in measured responses reflects the content category itself. The matched sets are then compared on physiological and attention measures.
ideas.principle: Compare conditions that are equated on a nuisance throughput measure, so that any difference in outcomes is attributable to the category of content rather than to the amount of signal delivered.

ideas.title: Known-truth synthetic evolution with frozen transfer
ideas.domain: LLM-driven evolution of geospatial partitioning algorithms (spatial regime discovery)
ideas.problem: Improving an algorithm by expert-driven trial and error is slow, and scoring candidate designs on real data during development lets the evaluation leak into the design, so reported real-world gains are not clean out-of-sample results.
ideas.approach: An automated multi-agent loop generates, scores, and selects candidate variants of a procedure, using fitness computed only on simulated instances whose true answer is known by construction. The winning variant is then frozen and run unchanged on real inputs, which are used only for final evaluation.
ideas.principle: A procedure is refined by iterated automated search that scores candidates only against inputs whose correct output is known by construction. The best candidate is then fixed and applied without modification to unseen inputs, so its measured performance is not tuned to the test cases.
concepts: known-truth synthetic evolution with frozen transfer
